messages.content:
The clinic will observe World Hand Washing Day on Wednesday with a short play by school students in the waiting hall. Children will show how to wash hands with soap for twenty seconds. All visitors are invited to watch. There is no fee.

Why is washing hands with soap useful?
The text doesn't say, but soap and water remove dirt and germs from your hands, which helps stop illnesses from spreading.

The ambulance service attached to our health centre is available day and night. In an emergency, call the number written on the board near the gate. The ambulance is free for patients from the nearby villages, and others pay a small charge for fuel.

Who gets the ambulance for free?
Patients from the nearby villages get it for free.

Cycle to work week begins on Monday. Staff who cycle to the office all five days will receive a small prize on Friday. A safe cycle stand has been set up near the back gate, and a pump and a repair kit are available with the guard.

What will staff who cycle all five days get?
They will receive a small prize on Friday.

Exhibition: from 15 to 20 October the library will display old maps and photographs of our town. The exhibition is in the first floor hall and is open from 10 am to 6 pm. Entry is free. School groups can book a guided tour by calling the library office.

How can school groups book a guided tour?
They can book it by calling the library office.

Mobile phones must be kept on silent in the waiting hall. The television on the wall shows health tips, but the volume is kept low. If a child cries, please step out for some time with the child. The staff will keep your place in the queue.

What does queue mean?
The text doesn't say, but a queue is a line of people waiting for their turn.

The old furniture donation drive is on 25 October. Residents can leave chairs, tables and shelves near the gate between 9 am and noon. A charity group will collect them and give them to families who need them. Broken items cannot be accepted.

Which items cannot be accepted?
Broken items cannot be accepted.

The doctor's room is on the first floor. Please wait on the chairs in the corridor until the nurse calls your name. If you have trouble climbing stairs, ask the reception for the ground floor room. Please keep your phone on silent.

What does reception mean?
The text doesn't say, but reception is the desk at the entrance where visitors are welcomed and asked what they need.

The librarian suggests that parents read aloud to children for at least ten minutes a day. Picture books with large words are kept on the low shelves. Our staff are happy to suggest books for each age. Ask at the desk any time.

Why is reading aloud useful for children?
The text doesn't say, but reading aloud helps children learn new words, listen well and enjoy stories.

The annual general meeting of the Green Valley Residents Association will be held on Sunday, 12 October at 6 pm in the community hall. Agenda: yearly accounts, security staff salaries, and the park garden plan. All flat owners are requested to attend. Tenants may attend but cannot vote.

Can tenants vote at the meeting?
No. Tenants may attend, but they cannot vote.

The nurse has asked patients to bring a small bottle of drinking water with them to the clinic on Tuesday, as the water cooler is being repaired. Disposable cups will be given at the counter. The clinic will have normal timings that day.

What does disposable mean?
The text doesn't say, but disposable means made to be thrown away after one use.

The training room is reserved for the sales team on Monday morning. If you need a room for a small meeting, please book one of the smaller rooms on the first floor using the booking sheet. Please leave the room tidy and switch off the lights after use.

What is a booking sheet?
The text doesn't say, but a booking sheet is a list where people write their names and times to reserve a room or service.

Salaries for October will be credited on 30 October, since 31 October is a holiday. Payslips will be available on the employee portal from the same day. Staff who need a salary certificate should send a request to the accounts team at least three days earlier.

When will October salaries be credited?
They will be credited on 30 October.

The society borewell pump stopped working yesterday evening. A mechanic has checked it and is waiting for a spare part. Tankers will supply water to all blocks until the pump is fixed. Residents are requested to use water carefully.

When will the pump be fixed?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know when it will be fixed. The society office can give an update.

Rain alert: Because of heavy rain forecast for tonight, the drains near Block C will be checked by the staff this afternoon. Residents on the ground floor should keep sandbags ready near the door. Sandbags are available at the maintenance room.

Where can residents get sandbags?
They are available at the maintenance room.

Lost property: a blue umbrella, a notebook with a green cover and a steel water bottle were left in the reading hall last week. They are now with the librarian. If they are yours, please collect them with some proof within ten days.

Within how many days should owners collect the lost items?
They should collect them within ten days.

Blood tests at our laboratory are done between 7 and 10 am. Please do not eat or drink anything except water for ten hours before a sugar or cholesterol test, if the doctor has asked for it. Reports are ready by 5 pm on the same day.

When are the reports ready?
The reports are ready by 5 pm on the same day.

Weekly Hindi story hour starts at the library on Sunday, 12 October, at 4 pm, and will be held every Sunday after that. The stories are meant for children aged 5 to 9 and will be told by a volunteer grandmother. Children may sit on the carpet in the activity room. No booking is needed.

Who will tell the stories?
A volunteer grandmother will tell the stories.

The company's yearly health check camp for employees will be held on 6 and 7 November in the conference hall. Staff can choose one of the two days. Each person will have a short chat with a visiting doctor, and results will be given in a sealed envelope. Please sign up with the admin team.

How will the results be given?
The results will be given in a sealed envelope.

Please note that library books should be covered with a plastic sheet and carried in a bag when it rains. Wet books may get fungus and swell. If a book gets wet, dry it in a shaded and airy place, away from direct sunlight. Do not iron the pages.

What is fungus?
The text doesn't say, but fungus is a kind of living thing, like mould or a mushroom, that grows on damp surfaces.

The children's section has moved to the first floor, next to the activity room. Story hour for young readers will take place every Saturday at 11 am. Parents are welcome to sit with their children. Please keep your phone on silent in this section.

What does silent mean on a phone?
The text doesn't say, but putting a phone on silent means turning off its ringing sound so it does not disturb others.

Books on the reserved shelf will be kept for three days only. If you do not pick up your book by then, it will be put back for others to borrow. You will get a text message when the book is ready. Please carry your library card when you collect it.

How long are reserved books kept?
They are kept for three days only.

Our morning yoga group meets in the society garden every day from 6 to 7 am. Beginners are welcome. Please bring your own mat and a towel. The group is led by a volunteer resident, and there is no fee. Sessions will be cancelled when it rains.

What does a beginner mean?
The text doesn't say, but a beginner is a person who has just started to learn something and has little practice yet.

Admission forms for nursery will be available from the school office from 1 December. Children must be three years old by 31 March. Parents should bring the birth certificate and two passport photographs while submitting the form. Interviews will be friendly and short.

How many seats are there in the nursery?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many seats there are. The school office can tell you.

Art club news: This Friday the art club will paint the wall near the playground. Members should bring old shirts to wear over their uniform. Paints and brushes will be provided. The theme is Our Village, and every member can add one small picture.

What should members wear over their uniform?
They should wear an old shirt over their uniform.

Volunteers needed: The library is looking for students from Classes 9 to 12 to help arrange books on Saturday mornings. Volunteers will get a certificate and service hours for school. Interested students should speak to Mr. D'Costa at the front desk and bring a letter from a parent.

What do volunteers get for helping?
Volunteers get a certificate and service hours for school.

Our clinic has fixed a ramp at the entrance. People using wheelchairs, walkers or prams can now come in without help. A handrail has also been added on both sides. Staff are ready to assist anyone who needs support. The work was finished last week.

What is a ramp?
The text doesn't say, but a ramp is a slope that lets people go up or down without using stairs.

Class 1 parents: Your children had their first spelling test today. The words were cat, dog, sun, hat and bed. Please practise them with your child tonight. Another test, with five new words, will be held next Tuesday.

What marks did my child get in the test?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know your child's marks. Please ask the class teacher or check the report notebook.

Dear members, due to a staff meeting, the library will open at noon on Thursday instead of 9 am. We are sorry for the trouble. Books can still be returned in the drop box near the gate. The reading hall will also open at noon.

Why is there a staff meeting?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the reason for the meeting. The library office may be able to tell you.

Residents doing interior work in their flats must inform the office first. Drilling and hammering are allowed only between 10 am and 5 pm on weekdays. No work is allowed on Sundays. Building waste should be taken away by the contractor and not left in the lobby.

On which day is no interior work allowed?
No work is allowed on Sundays.

The audio corner at the library has headphones and recorded stories for visitors who like to listen. Please wipe the headphones with the cloth provided after use. Each person may listen for up to thirty minutes. Please do not take the headphones out of the corner.

What are headphones used for?
The text doesn't say, but headphones are worn over the ears so you can listen to sound privately without disturbing others.

Quiet hours at the library are from 2 to 4 pm every day. During these hours, the staff will not give talks, and children's activities are paused. The aim is to give students and office workers a calm time. Hours may be changed during festivals.

What is paused during quiet hours?
Talks by staff and children's activities are paused.

Annual day celebration will be on 14 December at the city auditorium. The programme will begin with performances by staff and end with dinner. Each department may present one item that is not more than five minutes. Send the name of your item to Rohit in the admin team by 10 November.

How long can each department's item be?
Each item may be at most five minutes long.

Notice: The lockers in the cloakroom must be emptied by the end of this month. New locks will be fitted, and fresh keys will be given from 3 November at the admin desk. Items left in the lockers will be kept in a box in the admin office for two weeks.

Where will left items be kept?
They will be kept in a box in the admin office for two weeks.

The Class 5 science teacher announced that tomorrow's lesson is about the water cycle. Students should read pages 40 to 44 in their books tonight. They should also bring a clear glass jar with a lid for a small experiment with warm water.

What is the water cycle?
The text doesn't say, but the water cycle is how water rises as vapour, forms clouds, and falls back to earth as rain.

The laboratory is closed on Sundays. Samples dropped at the clinic on Saturday after 1 pm will be taken on Monday morning. For urgent tests, the hospital lab on Station Road is open all day and night. Please carry the doctor's slip.

What is a sample in a laboratory?
The text doesn't say, but a sample is a small amount, like a drop of blood, that is tested to learn something about the whole.

The school will have a Christmas carol evening on 19 December at 5 pm. Parents and grandparents are welcome. Students of Classes 3 to 6 will sing, and refreshments will be served after the programme. Please be seated by 4:45 pm.

Which songs will the children sing?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the song list. The music teacher can tell you.

Notice for Class 8: The science exhibition will take place on Saturday in the school lab. Each group must bring a working model and a one-page chart explaining it. Registration closes on Wednesday. Please give your group names to Mrs. Nair.

What is a working model?
The text doesn't say, but a working model is a small version of something that actually moves or does its job, so people can see how it works.

Door-to-door milk delivery is now allowed only before 8 am. Delivery staff will leave packets in the milk box near each flat's door. The security guard will check the bags of all delivery staff at the gate. Report any missing packet to the office by 9 am.

By what time should residents report a missing milk packet?
They should report it to the office by 9 am.

Our office is going green. From next month, we will stop using paper cups at the water cooler. Please bring your own mug or bottle. Steel glasses will be kept near the pantry for guests. Recycling bins have been placed on each floor.

What does recycling mean?
The text doesn't say, but recycling means turning used things like paper or plastic into new things instead of throwing them away.

Reminder: the quarterly team meeting is on Tuesday at 3 pm in Conference Room 2. Each team lead should prepare a three-minute update about their work. Slides are not needed. Light snacks will be kept outside the room. Please be on time.

What does quarterly mean?
The text doesn't say, but quarterly means happening once every three months, or four times a year.

Because of electrical work, the library lift will not work from Tuesday to Thursday. Readers who find stairs difficult may ask the staff at the ground floor desk to bring books to them. Please give the book name and shelf number to the staff.

What should readers who find stairs difficult do?
They may ask the staff at the ground floor desk to bring the books to them.

A senior citizens' tea meet will be held in the clubhouse every first Saturday of the month at 4 pm. Residents above 60 years can join for tea, board games and a chat. Volunteers from the youth club will serve the snacks and help with games.

Who will serve the snacks?
Volunteers from the youth club will serve the snacks.

The pharmacy at the town health centre is open from 8 am to 8 pm every day, including Sundays. Medicines are given only against a doctor's prescription. Please wait for your turn at the counter and keep the prescription ready. Payment can be made by cash or card.

What is needed to get medicines at the pharmacy?
A doctor's prescription is needed to get medicines.

Visitors must sign in at the reception desk, show a photo ID, and wear a visitor badge at all times. They should return the badge when they leave. Staff should come to the reception to receive their guests, and not let them walk around alone.

Why do offices ask visitors to sign in?
The text doesn't say, but offices ask visitors to sign in so they know who is in the building, which keeps it safe.

The mobile library van will visit Lakeview Colony on Wednesday afternoon. It carries about 400 books for adults and children. Members can return their borrowed books to the van. New members may join in the van with their address proof.

How long will the van stay in the colony?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how long it will stay. The library office can tell you.

The pharmacy next to the clinic will stay open for an extra hour, until 9 pm, from Monday to Friday. A new staff member has joined to help with the evening rush. Please do not crowd at the counter, and take a token when you arrive.

How many medicines does the pharmacy keep?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many medicines it keeps. The pharmacist can tell you whether a certain item is available.

Our women's network is organising a talk on healthy work habits on Thursday at lunchtime in the meeting room. A speaker will share simple tips such as taking short breaks and stretching at your desk. Everyone is welcome. Lunch can be brought into the room.

What does stretching mean?
The text doesn't say, but stretching means gently pulling your muscles, such as lifting your arms or bending, to make your body feel loose.

The school will hold a blood donation awareness talk for Class 11 and 12 on 29 October in the auditorium. A guest speaker from the town hospital will talk for forty minutes. Students may ask questions at the end of the talk.

What is the speaker's name?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the speaker's name. The school office may know.

Neighbours are invited to a Holi gathering in the clubhouse lawn on Saturday morning. We will use only natural colours made from flowers. Water guns are not allowed. Snacks and cold drinks will be served. Wear old clothes, as the colours may stain.

What is Holi?
The text doesn't say, but Holi is a spring festival in India when people throw coloured powder and celebrate with sweets.

The paediatric ward has a play corner with books and puzzles for children who have to wait. Volunteers from a local college read stories to children on Saturday afternoons between 3 and 4 pm. Parents may stay with their children throughout.

When do volunteers read stories to children?
They read stories on Saturday afternoons between 3 and 4 pm.

The school garden needs helpers. If your child likes plants, they can join the garden group every Tuesday during lunch break. They will water the plants, pull out weeds, and plant seeds of tomatoes and spinach. Gloves are kept in the green cupboard near the gate.

Where are the gloves kept?
The gloves are kept in the green cupboard near the gate.

Chess club registrations are open for Classes 5 to 9. The club meets every Thursday from 3 to 4 pm in Room 9. Beginners will learn how the pieces move, and others will play practice games. Boards will be provided. There is no fee.

How many squares are on a chess board?
The text doesn't say, but a chess board has 64 squares, eight rows of eight.

Please do not enter the doctor's room without being called. Each patient needs time to talk privately with the doctor. Only one family member may accompany a patient. Other relatives can wait in the waiting hall. Thank you for your co-operation.

Why is privacy important in a clinic?
The text doesn't say, but privacy matters because people talk about personal health details that they may not want others to hear.

Office hours during winter: from 1 November, the office will open at 9:30 am and close at 6:30 pm, Monday to Friday. Lunch break remains from 1 to 2 pm. On Saturdays, only the support desk will remain open, from 10 am to 2 pm.

When does the office open from 1 November?
From 1 November, the office will open at 9:30 am.

The clinic's morning shift nurse, Ms. Daisy, will be replaced from Monday by Mr. Peter, who will work the same hours from 8 am to 2 pm. Ms. Daisy will move to the evening shift. All patients can meet the new nurse at the registration desk.

Who will work the morning shift from Monday?
Mr. Peter will work the morning shift from Monday.

The health centre has received a new X-ray machine. It will be used from the first week of November. A trained technician has been hired. Patients will be told when X-rays can be booked, and a notice will be put up in the waiting hall.

What is an X-ray?
The text doesn't say, but an X-ray is a picture of the bones inside the body, taken with a special machine.

All new joiners will take part in a two-day induction programme starting on Monday. Day one covers company values and office rules. Day two includes a tour of the building and meetings with the department heads. Please carry your ID proof and your bank details.

Who will lead the induction programme?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who will lead it. The human resources team can tell you.

The library stays closed on 2 October for a public holiday and will open again the next day at the usual time. Members whose books fall due on that date will not be charged a fine for one day.

How many members have books due on 2 October?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many members have books due that day. The library desk may be able to tell you.

Painting competition for children aged 6 to 12 will be held on Sunday at 10 am under the big neem tree. The topic is My Dream Home. Drawing sheets and crayons will be provided. Prizes will be given for the best three drawings in two age groups.

In how many age groups will prizes be given?
Prizes will be given in two age groups.

Our new lift is working in the clinic building. It can carry six people at a time. Patients in wheelchairs get first priority. Please press the button once and wait. Children should not play inside it, and they must hold an adult's hand.

What does priority mean?
The text doesn't say, but priority means being first because your need is more important or urgent.

Switch off your phone in the scan room. The room has strong machines, and the sound of a phone can disturb the technician. Metal items like keys and belts must be left in the locker outside. A staff member will explain everything before the scan.

What is a scan?
The text doesn't say, but a scan is a test that uses a machine to take pictures of the inside of the body.

Notice for school groups: the library welcomes classes for a reading visit. Teachers should send a request letter at least one week before. A group may have up to thirty children. Each visit lasts one hour, and children can choose a book to read in the hall.

What is the largest group size for a school visit?
A group may have up to thirty children.

Our library is celebrating National Library Week with a free quiz on Thursday. The quiz is open to students of Classes 6 to 10 and covers books, authors, and general knowledge. The winning team will receive a book voucher. Prepare for a fun afternoon.

What is a voucher?
The text doesn't say, but a voucher is a small paper or code that you can use instead of money to buy something.

Painting of the outer walls of Block A will begin next week. Workers will use bamboo scaffolding around the building. Residents on the lower floors may notice some noise in the morning. Please keep windows closed when the workers are nearby.

How long will the painting take?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how long it will take. The contractor or the office can tell you.

Residents of Sunrise Apartments are informed that water supply will be cut on Sunday from 10 am to 2 pm because the tank is being cleaned. Please store enough water on Saturday night. The supply will return to normal by evening. We regret the inconvenience.

Why will the water be cut on Sunday?
The water will be cut because the tank is being cleaned.

The health centre will be closed on Wednesday, 22 October, for a public holiday. Emergency cases should go to the district hospital, which is open all day and night. The health centre will reopen on Thursday at 9 am.

Where should emergency cases go on Wednesday?
They should go to the district hospital.

The clinic has fixed a hand sanitiser dispenser at the entrance. Please clean your hands before entering the waiting hall. Masks are available at the desk for anyone with a cough. We thank you for helping us keep everyone safe.

What does a dispenser do?
The text doesn't say, but a dispenser is a machine or container that gives out a small amount of something, like soap, when you press it.

Dear residents, the pest control team will visit all flats on Saturday between 10 am and 4 pm. Please keep the kitchen cupboards clear and cover food items. Pets and small children should stay in a different room for two hours after the spraying. Please keep someone at home.

How long should pets and small children stay in another room?
They should stay in another room for two hours after the spraying.

Notice: Class 12 students must submit their board exam forms by 30 October. Forms need a recent photograph, a copy of the birth certificate and the signature of a parent. Late forms will not be accepted by the office. Collect the form from your class teacher.

Where can students collect the form?
They can collect it from their class teacher.

Dear parents, the school will start a morning breakfast club from next month. Children who come early can have a small breakfast in the dining hall from 7:15 to 7:45 am. A teacher will supervise. The cost is included in the monthly fee. Sign up at the office.

What does a supervisor do?
The text doesn't say, but a supervisor watches over a group to keep them safe and make sure the rules are followed.

On Saturday, the library will hold a book fair in the front hall from 10 am to 5 pm. Local publishers will sell story books, atlases, and dictionaries at lower prices. Members will receive an extra discount. Cash and cards will both be accepted.

What is an atlas?
The text doesn't say, but an atlas is a book of maps.

The photocopy service at the library is open from 10 am to 5 pm. One page costs Rs. 1, and a colour page costs Rs. 5. Books in the reference section may be copied up to ten pages only. Please ask the staff before you start.

How many pages of a reference book may be copied?
Up to ten pages may be copied.

Join our summer reading club for children aged 7 to 12. Each child gets a reading card, and for every book read, a star is stamped on the card. Children who collect ten stars will receive a certificate at the end of the programme. Registration is free.

What is a certificate?
The text doesn't say, but a certificate is a paper that shows you have finished something or won something.

A library trip for the Class 3 students of Green Hill School is planned on Tuesday. Children will see how books are arranged, sit in the story corner and choose one book each. Teachers must make sure that all children stay together. Please be quiet when moving between floors.

Why do children go on school trips?
The text doesn't say, but school trips let children learn by seeing and doing things outside the classroom.

Lost: a small silver bracelet with a heart charm was dropped near the playground on Friday. If you found it, please give it to the guard at Gate 1. The owner, a young girl, is very sad. A kind person has already put up a poster on the notice board.

What is a charm on a bracelet?
The text doesn't say, but a charm is a small decoration, like a heart or star, that hangs on a bracelet or chain.

Because of heavy rain, the evening session of the clinic on Friday will start at 6 pm instead of 5 pm. Patients who already have appointments before 6 pm will be called to change their time. The morning session will go on as usual.

When will Friday's evening session start?
It will start at 6 pm instead of 5 pm.

Our dental clinic has now moved to the second floor of the Rose Court building. The reception and waiting area are bigger, and a lift is available. Dental check-ups are by appointment only. Parking is available at the back of the building.

What is the new phone number of the dental clinic?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the phone number. You can look at the clinic's board or ask the front desk.

Notice to tenants: Please give a copy of your rent agreement and your ID card to the society office by the end of this month. This is needed to update the resident register. Tenants who have already submitted these need not submit them again.

What should tenants give to the office?
They should give a copy of their rent agreement and their ID card.

The office picnic will be on Sunday, 2 November, at the lakeside resort. Buses will leave the office gate at 8 am and return at 6 pm. Lunch and snacks are included. Family members are welcome, but they must be registered by 25 October with Priya in the admin team.

Who should family members register with?
They should register with Priya in the admin team.

Community blood pressure check: Every Monday between 8 and 9 am, a nurse will be at the housing society's gate to check blood pressure for residents. It is free and takes only a few minutes. Please carry a small notebook to note your reading.

Who will check residents on Monday mornings?
A nurse will check them at the housing society's gate.

Science teacher Mr. Rao has asked students of Class 9 to collect leaves from five different trees for the biology project. Each leaf must be pressed and pasted on a sheet with the name of the tree written below it. The project is due on 7 November. Neatness will carry marks.

How many different trees should the leaves come from?
The leaves should come from five different trees.

Please keep your reports in the folder provided when you visit the doctor. The folder has a pocket for X-rays and another for blood test reports. New folders are given free of cost at the desk when you register. If you lose it, ask for a new one for Rs. 20.

How much does a replacement folder cost?
A replacement folder costs Rs. 20.

A cultural evening will be held on Saturday to welcome new families who moved into the society this year. Residents can perform a song, dance or poem. Names should be given to Mrs. Kulkarni. Dinner will be served at 8 pm in the hall.

How many new families moved in?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many families moved in. Mrs. Kulkarni or the office may have the number.

Dear parents, the Class 5 annual day rehearsal will be held on Thursday, 9 October, from 2 pm to 4 pm in the main hall. Children should come in their regular uniform and carry a water bottle. Costumes will be handed out only on the day of the show. Parents are not allowed inside the hall during rehearsal.

Can parents sit in the hall on Thursday?
No. Parents are not allowed inside the hall during the rehearsal.

A sign near the reception reads: Please be patient. On busy days, our staff may take longer to call you. If you feel very unwell while waiting, tell the nurse at once, and you will be seen quickly. Thank you for understanding.

What does patient mean in this sign?
The text doesn't say, but here patient means being able to wait calmly without getting upset.

Please note that our clinic has a new payment system. Fees can now be paid by cash, debit card or bank transfer. Receipts will be printed at the counter. If you need a copy of an old receipt, please ask the accounts staff, who sit behind the reception desk.

Where do the accounts staff sit?
They sit behind the reception desk.

The library is thankful to Mrs. Kamala Rao for donating her late husband's collection of two hundred history books. They will be kept on a special shelf with his name. Visitors may read them in the hall, but these books cannot be taken home.

Can visitors take the donated history books home?
No. Visitors may read them in the hall, but they cannot take them home.

We have started a book swap shelf near the entrance. Bring a book you have already read and take another one in exchange. Please bring only books in good condition. Books with torn covers or missing pages will not be kept on the shelf.

What does in exchange mean?
The text doesn't say, but in exchange means you give one thing and receive another thing in return.

The school canteen will serve a new menu from next Monday. Items will include vegetable sandwiches, idli with sambar, fruit chaat and lemon rice. All food is cooked in the school kitchen each morning. Students pay with a prepaid card.

Who cooks the food in the canteen?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who the cooks are. The canteen manager can tell you.

Our reading hall has a new rule: please place your bag in the locker before you enter. You may carry only your notebook, a pen and the books you need. This will help us keep the hall less crowded. Lockers are free, and you keep the key with you.

What is a locker?
The text doesn't say, but a locker is a small cupboard with a lock where you can keep your things safe.

Overdue books: A fine of Rs. 2 per day is charged for each book returned late. If a book is lost, the member must pay its price or replace it with the same title. Members with unpaid fines cannot borrow new books until they clear the amount at the counter.

What is the fine for each late book per day?
The fine is Rs. 2 per day for each book.

The new magazines have arrived. You can find monthly magazines on science, nature, sports and stories in the rack near the window. They can be read in the library but not borrowed. Please put them back in the rack after reading.

What does nature mean?
The text doesn't say, but nature means plants, animals, weather and everything in the world that people did not make.

Eye check-up camp: The community hall will host a free eye check-up on Sunday from 10 am to 2 pm. Volunteers will take names at the door. Those who need glasses will get a slip and can order them at a lower price from the shop beside the hall.

What will people who need glasses receive?
They will receive a slip to order glasses at a lower price.

The office bus service for evening shifts has been extended. The last bus now leaves at 9 pm instead of 8:30 pm, and it will stop at Metro Square, Lake Road and the railway station. Staff must show their ID cards to get on the bus.

What must staff show to board the bus?
They must show their ID cards.

Attention students: the school bus for Route 4 will leave five minutes earlier from tomorrow because of road work near the market. Please be at your stop on time. Students who miss the bus must inform the transport office by phone before 8 am.

Who is the driver of the Route 4 bus?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who drives that bus. The transport office can tell you.

Mr. Anand Pillai, a writer from our town, will visit the library on Saturday to read from his new book for children. The reading will last about half an hour, followed by questions. Copies of the book will be on sale at the library desk.

What is the title of Mr. Pillai's new book?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the title. The library desk may have a poster or a copy.

Feedback box: We have placed a box near the pantry for your suggestions to improve the office. You can write your name or leave the note anonymous. The box will be opened every Friday by the human resources manager, who will read and reply to the useful points in the newsletter.

Who opens the box every Friday?
The human resources manager opens it every Friday.

Reminder: The swimming pool in our society is for residents only. Children below ten years must be with an adult. Swimmers must shower before entering the water and wear proper swimwear. The pool is closed on Mondays for cleaning.

Why do people shower before swimming?
The text doesn't say, but people shower first to wash off dirt and sweat so the pool water stays clean.

The notice reads: Hospital visiting is not allowed in the intensive care unit except at 5 pm for ten minutes. Please wash your hands before entering the unit and follow the nurse's instructions. Flowers and outside food are not allowed.

What does intensive mean here?
The text doesn't say, but intensive means very close and careful, so an intensive care unit gives very careful care.

The society cricket team won the inter-colony match on Sunday. The captain thanked all residents who came to cheer. A small celebration with sweets will be held in the clubhouse on Wednesday evening. The trophy will be kept in the office for a week.

Who scored the most runs?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who scored the most. The team captain can tell you.

The library will hold a handwriting and storytelling day on Saturday for children of Classes 2 to 5. A retired teacher will tell a folk tale and then help children write their own short stories. Paper and pencils will be given. Parents may wait in the reading hall.

What is a folk tale?
The text doesn't say, but a folk tale is an old story told by ordinary people and passed from one generation to the next.

What will the generators run during the power cut?
The generators will run only the lifts and the common lights.

Kindly note that the school photographs will be taken on Tuesday. Students should come in clean, ironed uniforms with neat hair. The photographer will click individual and class photographs, and prints will be given a week later. Siblings studying in the same school will be photographed together as well.

What time will the photographer arrive?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the time. The class teacher or the school office can tell you.

The school bus fee for the second term should be paid along with the tuition fee. Children who travel by van or on their own need not pay it. Please tell the office if your child will stop using the bus so that the seat can be given to another child.

Who does not need to pay the bus fee?
Children who travel by van or on their own do not need to pay it.

We found a small brown cat near the Block D staircase this morning. It looks healthy and friendly. It is now with the security guard, who is giving it milk. If it belongs to you, please come to the gate and collect it.

A yoga and wellness class for adults will start at the community clinic on 1 November. It will run on Saturdays from 7 to 8 am in the garden. A trained instructor will lead the class. Please bring a mat and a bottle of water.

How much will the yoga class cost?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the fee. The clinic's front desk can tell you.

Library staff will visit the nearby village school on Monday with 100 books for the children. A short story session will be held in the school yard. The books will be left at the school for one month. Teachers will keep a register of who borrowed which book.

What is a register used for?
The text doesn't say, but a register is a book or list where names and details are written down so they can be checked later.

Parents of Class 2 are invited to the open house on Saturday at 10 am. Teachers will show the children's notebooks and drawings, and parents may ask about progress. Please do not bring younger children, as the classrooms are small. Tea will be served in the corridor.

What does open house mean in a school?
The text doesn't say, but an open house is a day when parents visit the school to meet teachers and see their child's work.

Reminder to all: the society will switch the street lights to a timer from this week. They will turn on at 6 pm and turn off at 6 am. Residents who find a broken light should write it in the complaint register at the gate.

What is a timer?
The text doesn't say, but a timer is a device that turns something on or off at a set time.

Renewing books: You can renew a book once, for seven more days, if no one else has reserved it. Renewals can be done at the desk, by phone or on the library's own website. Books that are already overdue cannot be renewed.

Can a book that is already overdue be renewed?
No. Books that are already overdue cannot be renewed.

The half-yearly exams for Classes 6 to 8 begin on Monday, 20 October. The timetable is pasted on each classroom board. Students must reach school by 8:30 am, twenty minutes before the first paper. Only blue or black pens are allowed. Calculators are not needed for any paper.

What colour pens may students use in the exams?
Only blue or black pens are allowed.

Library period change: starting this week, Class 6 will have library period on Wednesday instead of Friday. Students must carry their library cards and return all books before the period begins. Books returned late will not be issued new ones until fines are cleared.

On which day will Class 6 have library period now?
Class 6 will have library period on Wednesday now.

Poetry evening will be held at the library on Friday, 24 October, at 6 pm. Members and visitors can read their own poems or poems they like. Each reader gets five minutes. The evening will end at 8 pm with tea. Please add your name to the list at the desk.

How much time does each reader get?
Each reader gets five minutes.

Sunrise Family Clinic timings: Monday to Friday, 9 am to 1 pm and 5 pm to 8 pm. Saturday, 9 am to 1 pm only. The clinic is closed on Sundays and public holidays. Please call the front desk for an appointment. Walk-in patients are seen after those with appointments.

When is the clinic open on Saturday?
On Saturday the clinic is open from 9 am to 1 pm only.

The library has bought fifty new novels and thirty new books for children. They will be placed on the new arrivals shelf near the entrance from Monday. Members can reserve books by writing the title on the form kept at the desk.

What are the titles of the new novels?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the titles. The librarian can show you the new arrivals list.

Physiotherapy sessions are available at the clinic from Tuesday to Saturday between 10 am and 5 pm. Each session lasts forty-five minutes. Patients must wear loose and comfortable clothes. Please book your time slot a day earlier at the reception.

How long is each physiotherapy session?
Each session lasts forty-five minutes.

From Monday, students will wear the winter blazer with the school tie. The blazer must be navy blue with the school badge on the pocket. Sweaters of any other colour are not allowed in class. Parents may buy the blazer from the uniform shop opposite the main gate.

Where can parents buy the blazer?
They can buy it from the uniform shop opposite the main gate.

Dr. Sunita Rao will be on leave from 20 to 27 October. During this time, Dr. Imran Khan will see her patients in the morning slot. Evening hours will be unchanged. Please call the front desk to change your appointment if you wish.

Why is Dr. Rao taking leave?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know why she is on leave. The front desk may be able to tell you, if it is not private.

Eyes and ears camp for school students: The school health team will visit Green Hill School on Monday, and Lakeview School on Tuesday. Class teachers will give each student a form. Parents must sign the form and return it before the camp day.

What must parents do with the form?
Parents must sign it and return it before the camp day.

The society requests all residents to separate wet and dry waste at home. Kitchen waste should go in the green bin and paper, plastic and metal in the blue bin. A compost pit has been made behind Block A, and gardeners will use the compost for plants.

What is compost?
The text doesn't say, but compost is a soft, dark material made from rotted kitchen and garden waste that helps plants grow.

Reminder to all parents: bring your child's vaccination card whenever you visit the clinic. The nurse will write the date of each vaccine on it. Keep the card in a safe place, because you will need it for school admission.

What does a vaccine do?
The text doesn't say, but a vaccine helps the body learn to fight a disease before the person gets ill.

Lift maintenance for Tower B will take place on Thursday between 11 am and 3 pm. During this period the lift will not work. Senior citizens who need help can call the security desk, and two staff members will help carry groceries and bags up the stairs.

Who can help residents carry bags during the maintenance?
Two staff members from the security desk can help carry groceries and bags.

Holiday notice: The school will remain closed from Wednesday to Saturday for Diwali. Classes will resume on the following Monday. Homework will not be given for the holiday period, but students are encouraged to read a book. Wishing everyone a safe and happy festival.

Why do people light lamps at Diwali?
The text doesn't say, but people light lamps at Diwali to celebrate the victory of light over darkness and good over bad.

New employees should collect their ID cards from the security cabin after completing the form in the human resources office. Please keep your card with you and do not lend it to anyone. If it is lost, tell the human resources team right away.

Why should people not lend their ID cards?
The text doesn't say, but an ID card proves who you are, so someone else could misuse it to enter places in your name.

Fire safety tip from the admin team: in case of an alarm, do not use the lift. Walk quickly down the stairs to the assembly point in the front garden. Floor wardens in yellow vests will guide you. Do not go back for your belongings.

Why should people avoid lifts in a fire?
The text doesn't say, but lifts can lose power or fill with smoke in a fire, so the stairs are safer.

The Ganesh festival committee invites residents to a planning meeting on Friday at 8 pm in the clubhouse. We will discuss the idol, decorations, and the cultural programme for the five days. Volunteers are welcome. Please bring your ideas and any old decoration items.

Dr. Mehta, a child specialist, will join our clinic from the first of next month. She will see children on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Parents may book the first visit by calling the front desk. A toy corner has been set up in the waiting room.

The clinic's waiting area is getting new chairs and a water cooler. Work will take place on Sunday, when the clinic is closed. On Monday morning, patients will find the hall tidy as usual. The staff thank everyone for their patience.

No. Senior citizens above 65 years may join without any fee.

Kindly send your child with a raincoat or an umbrella during this week. Heavy rain is expected, and the playground may be wet. Children will play indoor games in the hall if it is raining at break time. Wet shoes should be kept in the plastic bag provided.

Why do people use umbrellas?
The text doesn't say, but people use umbrellas to stay dry in the rain and to shade themselves from strong sun.

The society has decided to repaint the parking lines in the basement. Residents are requested to move their vehicles to the open ground on Tuesday and Wednesday. Work will start at 8 am each day. Keys of the vehicles may be left with the security guard if you will be away.

Class 4 field trip: We will visit the city bird sanctuary on Friday, 24 October. The bus leaves school at 7:45 am and returns by 3 pm. Children should wear comfortable shoes and a cap, and bring a packed lunch. Please return the signed permission slip by Tuesday.

The signed permission slip must be returned by Tuesday.

Notice on mobile phones: Students are not allowed to bring mobile phones to school. If a phone is found, the teacher will keep it in the office, and a parent must come to take it back. In an emergency, parents may call the school office on the landline.

What happens if a teacher finds a phone?
The teacher keeps it in the office, and a parent must come to take it back.

Our clinic offers a health information stand every Friday. Volunteers will share leaflets on washing hands, drinking clean water and eating on time. The stand is near the entrance, and the leaflets are free. Take one for your family. New leaflets arrive every month.

Remember to bring your Diwali craft box on Monday. It should have coloured paper, glue, scissors with round tips and a small lamp or diya. Children will make greeting cards in class. The finished cards will be displayed on the notice board for a week.

They will be displayed for a week.

Reminder about the dress code: formal clothing is expected from Monday to Thursday. On Fridays, staff may wear casual clothes, but torn jeans and slippers are not allowed. When clients visit the office, everyone should wear formal clothes, even on Fridays.

Everyone should wear formal clothes when clients visit, even on Fridays.

Our monsoon tree planting drive is on Sunday morning at 7 am. We will plant twenty saplings along the boundary wall. Spades and saplings will be provided by the garden committee. Children can help water the plants after planting. Bring a cap and a water bottle.

Seniors' health day: Every Wednesday morning, the clinic sets aside a quiet hour from 9 to 10 am for patients above 60 years. They will be seen without waiting and a staff member will help them with forms. Tea and biscuits will be offered in the waiting room.

Sports day will be held on Saturday, 1 November, at the school ground. Events include a 100 metre race, a sack race, long jump and a relay. Each house must send two students for every event. Names should be given to the sports teacher, Mr. Kapoor, by Friday.

How many students must each house send for every event?

Weekend timing: The children's library is open on Saturdays and Sundays from 10 am to 1 pm. Each child can borrow two picture books for one week. Children under six must be with an adult. There are no fines for children's books.

Are there fines for children's books?
No. There are no fines for children's books.

The society bus to the railway station will run from Monday to Saturday. It leaves the main gate at 7:15, 8:00 and 8:45 am. The fare is Rs. 20 per person, and monthly passes can be bought at the office. Children below five years travel free.

What is the fare for a person?
The fare is Rs. 20 per person.

Flat 304 in Block B is available for rent. It has two bedrooms, a small balcony, and a covered parking slot. Interested persons should speak to the society secretary. A police verification of the tenant is required by the society rules.

Fee reminder: The second term fee is due by 15 October. Payment can be made at the school office between 9 am and 12 noon on working days. A late fee will apply after the due date. Parents who have a problem paying on time may meet the accountant, Mr. Dsouza, before the due date.

They should meet the accountant, Mr. Dsouza, before the due date.

Maintenance bills for October have been sent by email and pasted on the notice board. The amount is Rs. 2,200 per flat. Please pay by the 10th of the month at the society office or by bank transfer. A late charge of Rs. 50 will be added after that date.

How much is the late charge?
The late charge is Rs. 50.

Several residents have complained about loud music late at night. Please keep the volume low after 10 pm, especially during exam season, when students are studying. Parties in the clubhouse must end by 10:30 pm. Thank you for respecting your neighbours.

What does being considerate mean?
The text doesn't say, but being considerate means thinking about how your actions affect other people and avoiding what would trouble them.

Garbage collection timing has changed. From Monday, the wet waste truck will come at 7:30 am and the dry waste truck at 4 pm. Please keep the two dustbins separate and tied. Bins left outside the gate after 9 am will not be emptied.

When will the dry waste truck come now?
The dry waste truck will come at 4 pm.

The management has decided to hold a blood donation drive in the office on 28 October. Employees aged between 18 and 60 may take part. A mobile team will set up in the conference room. Please register with the human resources team and bring a photo ID.

Why is blood donation important?
The text doesn't say, but donated blood is used to help people who lose blood after accidents or during operations.

This week, the clinic is giving out saplings to every family that visits. Plant your sapling in a pot or in your garden and water it regularly. The staff will tell you how to take care of it. Let us make our town greener together.

What is a sapling?
The text doesn't say, but a sapling is a young tree.

The inter-house quiz will be held in the school auditorium on Thursday at 1 pm. Each team has three members from Classes 7 and 8. The topics are general knowledge, geography, and word puzzles. The winning house gets the quiz shield for the year.

What do the winners receive?
The winning house gets the quiz shield for the year.

The office water purifier on the third floor has been repaired. Water on the third floor is safe to drink again. Until now, staff from that floor have been using the purifier on the second floor. The filter will be checked every month by the service team.

How often will the filter be checked?
It will be checked every month by the service team.

A blood donation camp will be held in the community hall on Sunday, 19 October, from 9 am to 1 pm. Doctors and nurses from the city hospital will run the camp. Donors should have eaten breakfast, and those who donate will be given a juice pack and a certificate.

What will donors receive?
Donors will receive a juice pack and a certificate.

The finance team will close the books for the half year on 30 September. Please make sure that all bills and invoices from your department reach the accounts team before 27 September. Late bills will be recorded in the next half year.

What does an invoice mean?
The text doesn't say, but an invoice is a paper that lists what was sold and how much money is to be paid.

Returning books: Please place books on the return trolley at the front desk. Do not put them back on the shelves yourself, because the staff must first mark them as returned in the register. Torn or damaged books should be shown to the librarian.

Why should readers not put books back on the shelves themselves?
Because the staff must first mark the books as returned in the register.

The school wants to thank all parents who sent old books for the book bank. Over three hundred books were collected. They will be given to children in the nearby village school on Saturday. Volunteers from Class 11 will go along to read stories with the children.

Who will go along to read stories?
Volunteers from Class 11 will go along.

Please do not leave shoes and plants in the common corridor. They block the path and can be a danger in case of fire. The committee will start checking the corridors next Monday, and items left outside will be removed and kept in the store room for a week.

Where will removed items be kept?
They will be kept in the store room for a week.

Parking rules: Each flat has one reserved parking slot marked with its flat number. Visitors must use the open area near Gate 2. Cars parked in the fire lane will be given a warning slip, and a second offence will mean a fine of Rs. 500. Two-wheelers must be parked in the shed.

Where should visitors park?
Visitors must park in the open area near Gate 2.

Reminder: Please handle the old newspapers carefully. They are kept in bound volumes in the reference section, and some are more than fifty years old. Use only a pencil to take notes. Pens may leave marks on the pages. Gloves are available on request.

What does reference section mean?
The text doesn't say, but a reference section holds books like dictionaries and atlases that you read inside the library and do not borrow.

Interview day: our office will host interviews for the accounts assistant post on Tuesday. Candidates will arrive between 10 am and noon. Please keep the main conference room free. Reception staff should guide the candidates to the waiting area on the first floor.

Where should reception staff guide the candidates?
They should guide the candidates to the waiting area on the first floor.

The veterinary clinic near the market takes dogs and cats from 10 am to 1 pm and 4 to 7 pm, except on Wednesdays, when it is closed. Pets should be on a leash or in a carrier. Please call before bringing a pet in an emergency.

On which day is the veterinary clinic closed?
It is closed on Wednesdays.

The clinic will remain closed on Friday afternoon for a staff training session. The morning session will go on as usual, and the evening session will open at 6 pm. Emergency cases may call the number on the board outside.

What will the staff learn in the training?

How early should patients arrive for their appointment?
They should arrive ten minutes before their time.

The society library corner on the ground floor is now open to all residents. It has about 200 story books for children and adults. Take a book, and return it within fifteen days. A register is kept on the table to write your name and flat number.

How can a library help a community?
The text doesn't say, but a library lets many people read the same books for free, so everyone can learn and enjoy stories.

The library cart that moves between floors will bring new business magazines every Wednesday. Staff may keep a magazine on their desk for three days and must then return it to the cart. Please do not tear or mark the pages.

How long may staff keep a magazine?
They may keep a magazine on their desk for three days.

Parking at the clinic is limited. Please use the municipal car park across the road, which is free for the first hour with a stamped ticket from the reception. The front area is kept free for ambulances and patients who cannot walk far.

What is the front area kept free for?
It is kept free for ambulances and patients who cannot walk far.

A new digital catalogue has been put on the computers near the main desk. You can search for a book by its title, author or subject. Staff will show you how to use it. The old card catalogue will be moved to the store room next month.

How many books are in the digital catalogue?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many books are listed. The librarian may be able to tell you.

The spelling bee for Classes 4 and 5 is on Tuesday at 12 noon in Room 12. Each class will send four spellers. Words will come from the reading book, pages 1 to 60. Mrs. Gomes will be the judge, and each correct word earns one point.

Who will judge the spelling bee?
Mrs. Gomes will be the judge.

The school will remain open on the second Saturday of this month for a special remedial class in mathematics. Only those students whose names are on the notice board need to attend. Timing is 9 am to 11 am. Please carry a notebook and a pencil.

Who needs to attend the Saturday class?
Only the students whose names are on the notice board need to attend.

Why was the policy changed?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know why it was changed. The IT team could explain.

The main gate will be closed to vehicles between 11 pm and 5 am. Emergency vehicles like ambulances will be let in at any time. Residents coming late may park outside and walk in through the small side gate, where a guard will be on duty.

What vehicles will be let in at any time?
Emergency vehicles like ambulances will be let in at any time.

Welcome to the Town Public Library. We are open Monday to Saturday from 9 am to 7 pm and on Sundays from 10 am to 2 pm. The library is closed on public holidays. Members may borrow three books at a time for fourteen days. Reading hall entry is free for everyone.

How many books can a member borrow at a time?
A member can borrow three books at a time.

The society will hold a fire safety demonstration on Saturday at 5 pm near the main gate. Firefighters will show how to use an extinguisher and how to leave a building safely. Residents of all ages are welcome. Please come on time.

What is a fire extinguisher?
The text doesn't say, but a fire extinguisher is a metal cylinder that sprays a substance to put out a small fire.

Please submit your travel bills for the month of September to the accounts desk by Friday. Attach all tickets and receipts, and write your employee number on each page. Bills received after Friday will be paid next month.

What is the limit for travel claims?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the limit. The accounts team can tell you.

Our monthly book club will meet on the last Sunday at 5 pm in the reading hall. This month we will talk about a short story collection chosen by the members. Tea and biscuits will be provided. Anyone may join, and no registration is needed.

Which short stories will the club talk about?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which stories were chosen. You could ask the librarian or the club members.

A health talk on healthy eating habits for teenagers will be held at the clinic next Saturday. Parents and teenagers can attend together. The talk will last forty-five minutes, followed by questions. A dietitian will speak, and seats are free.

How long will the talk last?
It will last forty-five minutes.

What does OPD stand for?
The text doesn't say, but OPD stands for outpatient department, where patients are seen without staying overnight.

What does a pharmacist do?
The text doesn't say, but a pharmacist prepares and gives out medicines and explains how to take them.

When is the baby care class held?
It is held every second Sunday at 11 am.

Our regional head, Mr. Verma, will visit the office on Wednesday. He will meet each team for fifteen minutes and then have lunch with the managers. Please keep your team boards updated and your desks tidy for the visit.

What is Mr. Verma going to talk about?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know what he will talk about. His assistant or your manager may know.

How long is a standard football match?

They should use the main staircase until noon.

The clinic is happy to share that Nurse Joseph has won the district award for best nurse of the year. A small celebration will take place in the waiting hall on Friday at 1 pm. Patients are welcome to join and say thanks.

The text doesn't say, but a nurse cares for patients and helps doctors look after them.

The trial is on the 12th.

What should students notice in their pictures?
They should notice how the light changes at different times of the day.

Spelling list for Friday: beautiful, Wednesday, library, necessary, friend. Tip from Miss Jones: say each word out loud in parts. Be-au-ti-ful. Wed-nes-day. Write each word three times and cover it to test yourself. Mum will check the list on Thursday night.

What does Miss Jones suggest doing with each word?
She suggests saying each word out loud in parts.

Notice to Class 7: The Hindi debate is postponed to next Wednesday because the hall is needed for the exam. Teams will remain the same. Each speaker has two minutes. Topic: Is it better to read a book or to watch a film? Judges will be Mrs Bose and Mr Khan.

Why has the debate been postponed?
It has been postponed because the hall is needed for the exam.

Diary, 9 September. Imran and I had a small fight about the cricket scores. He said he scored twelve, but I counted ten. We did not talk for the whole recess. In the evening, he knocked on my door with a packet of chips and said sorry.

What is the writer's name?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the writer's name. It may be written on the diary cover.

Who should be told if a student feels unwell?
They should tell the warden, Mrs Nair.

Diary, 10 January. We had sarson ka saag with makki ki roti for dinner at Dadi's house. It was served with a big lump of white butter. Dadi made it on a clay stove and the smoky smell made it special. I ate until I could not move.

Which season is sarson ka saag usually eaten in?
The text doesn't say, but sarson ka saag is usually eaten in winter, when mustard greens are in season.

Note to the electrician: The fan in the hall makes a clicking sound when on high speed. The bedroom switchboard is loose. The spare key is under the blue flowerpot. Please come after 4 pm because the baby sleeps in the afternoon.

What does an electrician do?
The text doesn't say, but an electrician installs and repairs wiring, switches and electrical fittings in buildings.

Reading log: Week one, finished two chapters of The Secret Garden and liked Mary's cousin Colin. Week two, read the whole story of the clever crow. Week three, started a book about space but it was too hard, so I put it back and chose a comic.

How many pages does the comic have?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many pages the comic has. You could check the book itself.

Diary, 15 September. We had a surprise quiz today in the geography class. I knew the answers about rivers and mountains, but I forgot the one about deserts. Miss Roy said the best way to remember is to draw maps. After school I drew one on the back of my notebook.

What is a desert?
The text doesn't say, but a desert is a very dry area that gets little rain, and often has sand.

Note from the school nurse: Please keep children at home if they have a fever. They can return when they are better and feeling active. Wash hands before meals. Water coolers on each floor have been cleaned this week.

Which classes have the most absentees this week?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which classes have the most absentees. The school office keeps the attendance records.

Rangoli sketch on the notice board: Start with a square of twelve dots. Join the dots with curved lines to make petals. Fill the centre with yellow and the petals with pink. Border in white. Let the youngest children place the last diya in the middle.

Who places the last diya?
The youngest children place the last diya in the middle.

Wildlife note: At the sanctuary we saw spotted deer, wild boar and many peacocks. The guide told us to stay quiet and not to use flash cameras. We saw the footprints of a tiger on the muddy trail but not the tiger.

What is the national bird of India?
The text doesn't say, but the national bird of India is the peacock.

Diary, 14 March. At Holi, the whole street was full of colour. My cousins hid behind the water tank with balloons. Mum put oil on my hair first so the colour would wash out easily. Everyone ate gujiya and drank cold thandai in the afternoon.

What is Holi known as?
The text doesn't say, but Holi is known as the festival of colours.

Bus note: This bus goes to Hampi via Hospet. Seats are numbered. Luggage is kept in the back. A rest stop will be made at a roadside dhaba for twenty minutes. Please keep the bus clean and do not play loud music.

How much is the ticket?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the ticket price. The booking counter or the conductor can tell you.

Race day note: The 100-metre race starts at 9. Shoes must be tied well. Do not eat a heavy breakfast. Bring your house colour band. The relay race is after the tea break. Ribbons for the winners will be given by the headmaster.

Who will give the ribbons to the winners?
The headmaster will give the ribbons.

Painting note: Put newspapers on the table before you start. Mix the colours on the plate, not on the paper. Wash the brush after each colour. Let the painting dry flat. Sign your name in the lower corner.

Which colours do you mix to make green?
The text doesn't say, but mixing blue and yellow makes green.

Note for Christmas morning: Come downstairs by eight. The cake is in the oven, so do not open it. The star on the tree was made by the twins. Presents are to be opened after breakfast. Carols at the church are at six in the evening.

Which day of the year is Christmas celebrated?
The text doesn't say, but Christmas is celebrated on the 25th of December.

Pottery class sheet: Knead the clay well to remove air bubbles. Shape a pot by pressing your thumb in the middle of the ball and pinching up the sides. Let it dry slowly in the shade. The pots will be baked in the kiln next Tuesday.

How much does the pottery class cost?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how much the class costs. The pottery centre can tell you.

Bakery notice: Our whole wheat bread is baked fresh at 6 am. Plum cake and fruit biscuits are made on Fridays. Orders for birthday cakes should be given two days ahead. We do not use eggs in the cakes marked with a green dot.

Which ingredient is used to make bread rise?
The text doesn't say, but yeast is the ingredient that makes bread dough rise.

Moving checklist: Pack the books in the small boxes because large boxes get too heavy. Wrap the glasses in old newspaper. Label every box with the room name. Keep one bag with tea, a kettle and two cups for the first evening in the new flat.

Why are the books packed in small boxes?
Books are packed in small boxes because large boxes would get too heavy.

Gardening note: I sowed marigold seeds in the red pots and spinach in the long tray. Water both every evening, but only a little for the spinach. The first marigold leaves appeared after six days. The spinach is still sleeping in the soil.

Do plants need sunlight to grow?
The text doesn't say, but yes, plants need sunlight, along with water and air, to make their food and grow well.

Rose bush care card: Water deeply twice a week. Remove dead flowers so new ones can grow. In winter, cut back the long branches. Add compost once a month. If you see tiny green insects, spray soapy water on the leaves.

What should be sprayed on the leaves if tiny green insects appear?
Soapy water should be sprayed on the leaves.

Window note: It is cold and misty this morning. The temperature dropped overnight and there is dew on the grass. Wear a sweater. The school will start at the normal time. Hot tea will be available in the staff room.

Will school start at the normal time?
Yes, the school will start at the normal time.

Teacher's remark in the diary: Divya has done very well in her reading this term. She still forgets to put the full stop at the end of a sentence. Please ask her to read aloud at home for ten minutes a day. We will meet again after the half-yearly exams.

What does Divya still forget to do?
She still forgets to put the full stop at the end of a sentence.

The class begins with a warm-up of simple beats.

Diary, 14 July. We took the toy train up the hill. It moved so slowly that I could count the pine trees. In one tunnel, everyone clapped and shouted. At the top station we had hot corn on the cob and Dad lost his cap in the wind.

Dad lost his cap in the wind at the top station.

Each member should bring one question for the group.

Science homework: Observe the moon every night for five days and draw its shape. Write the date under each drawing. If it is cloudy, leave the box empty and write cloudy. Submit the sheet on Monday. Use a pencil so you can fix mistakes.

The text doesn't say, but no, the moon does not make its own light. It shines because it reflects light from the sun.

The text doesn't say, but wool comes from the fleece of sheep, and sometimes goats or other animals.

They should be sown about one centimetre deep.

Fridge note from Meera:

The text doesn't say, but hockey is often said to be India's national game, although it has no official status.

The steep 5 km path leads to the old fort.

The text doesn't say, but curd is made from milk, which turns into curd when a little starter is added and it is left to set.

How many people does this recipe serve?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many people it serves. Aunty Lata could tell you.

Diary, 21 March. Today my sister Rhea went to her first day at the big school. She wore her new uniform and carried the pink bag. Mum made her a small lunch and Dad dropped her at the gate. Rhea waved with both hands and walked in alone.

Which class is Rhea in?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which class Rhea is in. You could ask the family.

Plants should be watered in the evening so that less water dries up.

It should be run for thirty seconds at a time, so the motor does not heat up.

Diary, 31 October. Lakshmi Puja at home was beautiful. We set up the diyas along the steps and Mum made payasam. Papa drew a small footprint design on the floor with rice flour. My cousins came and we played cards till late.

Papa drew a small footprint design on the floor with rice flour.

The cup at the bottom right is empty, because Mum is waiting for new coriander powder.

Diary, 14 June. Mum made rasam for lunch and the whole house smelled of pepper and curry leaves. I had two helpings with rice. Afterwards I fell asleep on the sofa and woke up when the pressure cooker whistled again for dinner.

What is rasam usually eaten with?
The text doesn't say, but rasam is usually eaten with rice, or sometimes drunk on its own as a thin soup.

The text doesn't say, but coins and notes together are called money, or currency.

The text doesn't say, and I don't know the price of the oil. The shop or its website would show the current price.

Chhotu walked to Dad.

Bird watch diary: Saw a pair of parakeets on the guava tree at six this morning. They ate the half-ripe fruit and made a loud screeching noise. A crow chased them away. Later, three sparrows came for the rice grains I had put in a dish.

What did the sparrows come for?
The sparrows came for the rice grains left in a dish.

Field note: The peepal tree outside our school drops yellow leaves in March. By April, new red-brown leaves come out. Squirrels run up and down all day, and a pair of mynas has built a nest in the highest fork. Nobody is allowed to throw stones near it.

Where have the mynas built their nest?
The mynas have built their nest in the highest fork of the peepal tree.

Diary, 20 July. It rained all morning, so the school bus came late. I wore my yellow raincoat and still got wet socks. At lunch, the playground looked like a pond and the boys made paper boats. By evening, the sun came out and there was a rainbow.

Will it rain on 21 July?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know what the weather will be on 21 July. A local weather forecast will tell you.

Poster: Evening of Light Music, Saturday at the community hall. A young group from the music school will sing songs in Tamil, Hindi and English. Entry is free. Please sit before 6:30 so that the singers can start on time.

The text doesn't say, but a group that sings together is called a choir, or sometimes just a singing group.

When is the pool closed for cleaning?
It is closed on the first Monday of every month.

Diary, 12 February. I finally learned to play the first lines of a new tune on the flute. My fingers ached and my lips felt strange. Papa said it sounded like a tired bird, but then he clapped. I will practise again after school.

What did Papa say the flute sounded like?
Papa said it sounded like a tired bird.

The writer asks Dev to reply soon because the phone battery is low, at ten percent.

Sticky note on the cage: Tweety is a green parrot. Feed seeds and fruit pieces each morning. Change the water daily. Keep the cage away from the kitchen smoke. Cover at night with the cotton cloth. Tweety likes to whistle in the morning.

Can parrots copy human words?
The text doesn't say, but yes, many parrots can copy words and sounds that they hear often.

The bathroom tap still needs a new part.

Key list on the board: Key 1 opens the front gate. Key 2 opens the store room. Key 3, the one with a red tag, is for the back door. The key for the terrace is with Mr Reddy. Please return the keys to the board after use.

The text doesn't say, and I don't know where the spare key for the main door is. Whoever looks after the key board might know.

The label says to repot it every two years, into a slightly bigger pot.

Bruno has two walks each day, one at 6:30 in the morning and one at 7 in the evening.

Neem leaves placed between the layers help keep moths away.

Yoga class sheet: Morning class at 6:30 in the hall. Bring your own mat. Wear loose, comfortable clothes. Do not eat anything for two hours before class. The class ends with five minutes of quiet sitting. Our teacher is Mrs Menon.

The class ends with five minutes of quiet sitting.

Varun shouted because he was upset about his result.

Invitation: You are invited to the Onam feast at the community hall on Sunday. A sadya will be served on banana leaves. Children can take part in the flower carpet contest at ten. Please arrive on time.

The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many dishes there will be. The organisers can tell you.

The lift will keep working as usual.

You should look at something far away for twenty seconds.
