Where are the candles?
The candles are in the first drawer of the dining table.

Menu for the school picnic: Vegetable pulao, boondi raita, aloo fry and fruit salad. Water and glucose biscuits will be carried by the teachers. Children who have allergies should tell the class teacher in advance. Please carry your own plates and spoons.

What should children carry for eating?
Children should carry their own plates and spoons.

Class project note: Our group watched an anthill near the school gate for one week. On Monday there were few ants. By Thursday the hill was twice as tall because it rained and the ants rebuilt it. We took photos each day and pasted them in the chart.

How many legs does an ant have?
The text doesn't say, but an ant has six legs, like all insects.

Homework diary entry: English - write five lines about your best friend. Maths - finish page 32, sums 1 to 10. Science - bring a leaf of any tree for tomorrow's class. Drawing - colour the peacock. Teacher said to cover the notebooks with brown paper.

What should be brought for science class?
A leaf of any tree should be brought for science class.

Dear students, the school library will be closed on Monday for stock checking. Books can be returned in the drop box near the office. The library will reopen on Tuesday at 8:30 in the morning. Please carry your ID cards when you come.

What should students bring when the library reopens?
They should bring their ID cards.

Office board: The printer on the second floor is out of order. Please use the printer in the accounts room until it is fixed. A technician will visit on Wednesday afternoon. Paper is kept in the grey cabinet near the window.

How long will the repair take?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how long the repair will take. The technician can tell you after looking at the printer.

Doorbell label: Press once only. If we do not answer, please call the number below. There is a dog inside who barks but does not bite. Newspapers can be left on the stand outside. Please close the gate after you enter.

What should visitors do if nobody answers?
They should call the number given below the label.

Note passed in class: Meet me near the swing at recess. Bring your skipping rope, I will bring chalk to draw the hopscotch squares. Rina said she may come too. Do not tell the others yet, it is a surprise for Kabir's birthday.

How is hopscotch played?
The text doesn't say, but in hopscotch you toss a small stone onto a square, then hop through the chalk squares on one foot to pick it up.

Instructions for the new rice cooker: Wash the rice and add water up to the line marked 2. Close the lid and press the red button. The light turns green when the rice is ready. Keep it closed for five more minutes before opening.

Why do we wash rice before cooking?
The text doesn't say, but rice is washed to remove loose starch and dust before it is cooked.

Stamp collection note: I put the old stamps in a green album, one country on each page. The oldest stamp is from before my grandfather was born. I use tweezers to pick them up and a soft brush to clean the edges. I have four stamps with birds.

Why are tweezers used for stamps?
The text doesn't say, but tweezers let you pick up stamps without touching them, so you do not tear or dirty the paper.

Fish tank note: Feed the goldfish only a pinch of flakes, once in the morning. Do not overfeed because the water turns cloudy. Clean the filter on the first Sunday of each month. The big orange fish is Gopal and the small one with the black spot is Gudiya.

Which fish has a black spot?
The small fish called Gudiya has the black spot.

Airport note, written by Aunt Rekha: Flight lands at 9:50 pm. Please wait at gate B, not at gate A. I will wear a green shawl so you can see me. The taxi is booked and the driver will hold a sign with my name. Call me if the flight is late.

What will Aunt Rekha wear?
Aunt Rekha will wear a green shawl.

Reminder from the shop owner: The new stock of school bags will come on Thursday morning. Please clear the lower shelf before that. Price tags should be put on only after Mr Das checks the bills. Keep the front counter clean because visitors come on Friday.

What should be cleared before Thursday?
The lower shelf should be cleared before the new bags arrive on Thursday.

Diary, 5 May. It was so hot today that the road looked wavy. Granny kept the curtains closed all afternoon. We drank nimbu pani and lay on the cool floor. At night, a light breeze finally started and we slept on the terrace.

Which season is usually the hottest in most parts of India?
The text doesn't say, but summer, from about April to June, is usually the hottest season in most of India.

Luggage tag: Name - Kavita Rao. Flight to Pune, seat 14C. Contact - Aunty Sheela, phone number written on the back. If found, please hand over to the airline desk. Blue suitcase with a yellow ribbon on the handle.

What is tied to the handle of the suitcase?
A yellow ribbon is tied to the handle.

Reading plan: Read twenty pages every night. On Sundays, read an extra story out loud to your little sister. Keep a list of new words in the back of your notebook. Ask Miss Rani on Monday if you do not understand a word.

What should be done on Sundays?
On Sundays you should read an extra story out loud to your little sister.

Diary, 30 June. Monsoon arrived at last. The sky went grey at noon and the first drops fell with a loud sound on the tin roof. Grandpa stood on the veranda smiling. The dust on the road turned to mud and the frogs began to croak at night.

What is a monsoon?
The text doesn't say, but the monsoon is a seasonal wind that brings heavy rain to India, usually between June and September.

Grocery label on the kitchen shelf: Jaggery from the farm of Uncle Murugan. Brown block, about half a kilo. Break with a hammer, not a knife. Use in tea, payasam and sweet rotis. Wrap tightly after cutting to keep it from getting sticky.

How should the jaggery be broken?
It should be broken with a hammer, not a knife.

Morning note: There is thick fog over the whole colony. The school bus will go slowly and may reach ten minutes late. Please send children with a light jacket. If the fog is still thick at noon, the sports period will be held indoors.

Where will the sports period be held if the fog stays?
It will be held indoors.

Note on the door: Gone to the market with Grandpa. We took the red cloth bag and the small umbrella. There are biscuits in the tin if you are hungry. Lock the gate if you go out. - Ravi

What time will Ravi and Grandpa come back?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know when they will return. You could call Ravi and ask him.

Diary, 28 December. We reached Jaipur at dusk. The fort on the hill was lit in gold. Our guide, Mr Singh, told us how the old kings stored rain water in big tanks. I climbed the steps slowly and bought a small blue elephant for my sister.

What did the writer buy for the sister?
The writer bought a small blue elephant for the sister.

Ferry timetable note pinned at the jetty: Boats leave every thirty minutes from 6 am to 7 pm. Life jackets must be worn by everyone, including adults. Bicycles are allowed on the lower deck. The crossing takes about fifteen minutes. Fares are paid to the conductor on board.

Where can bicycles be taken?
Bicycles can be taken on the lower deck.

Slip on the washing machine: Clothes in the blue basket are for the delicate cycle. Put the white shirts in separately. Use one scoop of powder only. Drying rack is on the terrace. Bring everything down before the evening, since rain is likely.

Why should the clothes be brought down by evening?
They should be brought down because rain is likely in the evening.

Timetable for Friday: Period 1 English, Period 2 Maths, Period 3 Science lab, break, Period 4 Social Studies, Period 5 Games, Period 6 Library. Wear the white sports shoes for games. Bring the lab coat for Period 3.

What should be brought for Period 3?
The lab coat should be brought for Period 3, the science lab.

Diary, 22 November. Today we reached the old fort at Gwalior. It was windy and there were many steps. At the top a guide told stories about the queens and the old palace. I bought some postcards and a cold drink from a small stall.

How old is the fort?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the exact age of the fort. A guidebook or the site's official information would tell you.

Diary, 12 November. We cleaned the whole house for Diwali. Dad hung lights on the balcony and Mum drew a rangoli with white and orange powder. My little cousin Zoya lit a sparkler and clapped. We ate sweets from the blue box first.

Is Diwali called the festival of lights?
The text doesn't say, but yes, Diwali is widely known as the festival of lights.

Sandwich plan: Take two slices of bread. Spread green chutney on one and butter on the other. Add thin slices of cucumber and tomato. Sprinkle a pinch of salt and chaat masala. Press the slices together and cut into triangles.

What shape are the sandwiches cut into?
The sandwiches are cut into triangles.

Diary, 25 January. We hoisted the flag at school for Republic Day. The band played and the sports captain, Nandini, gave the salute. Afterwards each child got a small laddoo and a paper flag. My grandfather watched the parade on television and wore his old cap.

Who gave the salute at school?
The sports captain, Nandini, gave the salute.

Fee receipt: Received from Sneha Rao, Class 5, tuition fee for the month of October. Paid in cash. Please note that the fee for November is due before the fifth. A late charge applies after that date. Receipt number is written in the corner.

By when must the November fee be paid?
It must be paid before the fifth of November, to avoid a late charge.

Aquarium note: The water is changed on Sundays, one third each time. Do not tap on the glass. The snails clean the sides of the tank. Switch on the light only for eight hours a day. Keep the tank away from direct sun.

Do fish breathe with lungs?
The text doesn't say, but fish breathe with gills, which take oxygen from the water.

Hotel door card: Breakfast is served from 7 to 10 in the garden restaurant. Checkout time is 11 am. The swimming pool closes at 8 pm. For help, dial 0 from the room phone. Please leave the key card at the front desk when you go out.

What is on the breakfast menu today?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know what is on the menu today. The restaurant staff or the front desk can tell you.

Packet label: Roasted peanuts, lightly salted. Net weight 200 grams. Best before six months from packing. Keep in an airtight container after opening. Packed in a unit that also handles sesame, so may contain traces of sesame. Please read the label before giving it to young children.

What might the peanuts contain traces of?
They may contain traces of sesame.

Menu board at the canteen: Idli with sambar, thirty rupees. Vada, fifteen rupees. Masala dosa, forty-five rupees. Filter coffee, twelve rupees. The canteen is closed on Sundays. Tokens must be bought at the counter before ordering. Lunch is served from noon to two.

What is idli made from?
The text doesn't say, but idli is made from a fermented batter of rice and urad dal, which is steamed.

Daily walk record: Monday 20 minutes, Tuesday rest, Wednesday 30 minutes, Thursday 25 minutes, Friday rest, Saturday 40 minutes with Dad around the lake. Sunday, play badminton instead of walking. Goal is to walk four days each week.

On which day was the longest walk?
The longest walk was on Saturday, for 40 minutes around the lake with Dad.

Letter extract: Dear Kiran, thank you for the lovely scarf. It is so soft that I wore it all through the cold evening at the cricket match. Our team lost, but we laughed a lot. Please come to our house during the holidays. Mum will make your favourite dosas.

What will Mum make when Kiran visits?
Mum will make Kiran's favourite dosas.

Housekeeping note: Please switch off the fans and lights when you leave the room. Keep the windows closed in the afternoon to keep the heat out. The mosquito net is in the cupboard. Lock the main door when you leave.

Why are fans and lights switched off when nobody is in the room?
The text doesn't say, but switching them off saves electricity.

Topic card for the science fair: Our group will show how a plant bends towards the light. We will use two pots, one near the window and one in a dark box. We will take a photograph every day and write what we see.

Why do plants need light?
The text doesn't say, but plants use light to make their own food through a process called photosynthesis.

Dictionary corner rules: The big dictionary stays on the table and must not leave the room. Pocket dictionaries can be borrowed for one day. Look up the word, write it in your word book and copy one example sentence. Put the book back in order.

For how long can pocket dictionaries be borrowed?
Pocket dictionaries can be borrowed for one day.

Train compartment notice: Please do not sit on the upper berth before ten at night. Keep your luggage chained under the seat. The pantry car is two coaches ahead. Tea and snacks are served at every major station stop. Throw rubbish only in the bin at the door.

Where is the pantry car?
The pantry car is two coaches ahead.

Bookshelf note: The top shelf has the dictionaries and atlases. The middle shelf is for storybooks. The bottom shelf holds the old textbooks. Please put the book back where you found it and do not lend books outside without telling Didi.

Where are the storybooks kept?
The storybooks are kept on the middle shelf.

Skating club note: Wear knee guards, elbow guards and a helmet at all times. Beginners will skate on the smooth floor near the pillars. The slope behind the hall is only for advanced skaters. Practice is from 4:30 to 5:30.

Which skaters may use the slope behind the hall?
Only advanced skaters may use the slope behind the hall.

Message to cousins: Wedding in the family next month. Mamaji says everyone must reach by the 12th. The mehendi function is on the 13th afternoon and the wedding on the 14th evening. Wear yellow for the first function. Rooms are booked at the guest house near the temple.

When is the mehendi function?
The mehendi function is on the afternoon of the 13th.

Lunchbox idea written by Mum: Monday, lemon rice with peanuts. Tuesday, vegetable sandwich. Wednesday, curd rice with a small pickle. Thursday, poha with sev. Friday, cheese roll and an apple. Saturday is half day, so a banana only.

Which lunch does my brother like best?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which lunch your brother likes best. You could just ask him.

Piggy bank diary: I opened the piggy bank today with Dad. There were forty-two coins and three folded notes. I counted them twice on the carpet. I want to buy a football, so I will keep saving. Dad said he will add a note on my birthday.

How much money was in the piggy bank in total?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the total, because the value of the coins and notes isn't given. You could count it with Dad.

Reading note: Today I finished a story about a lighthouse keeper who saves a ship during a storm. The best part was when he climbed the stairs in the dark and lit the lamp. The ending made me feel proud of him. I want to read more sea stories.

What is a lighthouse for?
The text doesn't say, but a lighthouse is a tall tower with a bright light that guides ships and warns them of rocks.

Label on the sapling pot: Neem. Planted in July by Class 6 as part of the tree drive. Water twice a week. Fence it with a net until it is taller than a goat. Class monitor of 6B is in charge of the label and the watering roster.

Who is in charge of watering?
The class monitor of 6B is in charge of the watering roster.

Auto driver's note on the dashboard: Fare from the station to the school road is sixty rupees by meter. Night charges after ten. Children go half price when sitting on laps. Do not leave belongings. Lost things are kept with Raju at the stand.

Where are lost things kept?
Lost things are kept with Raju at the auto stand.

Savings chart: Week 1, saved 20 rupees. Week 2, saved 15 rupees because of the school trip. Week 3, saved 30 rupees after Aunt gave me a coin on my cousin's wedding. Week 4, saved nothing. Goal is to buy a skipping rope.

In which week did the writer save nothing?
The writer saved nothing in Week 4.

Birthday cake note: I will bake the cake on Friday evening. The eggs are in the second shelf of the door. Butter has to be soft, so take it out an hour before. The cake tin is the round one with the dent. Icing will be done on Saturday morning.

How many guests will eat the cake?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many guests there will be. The person baking the cake would know.

Door note: Dear delivery person, please do not ring the bell. The baby is asleep. Leave the parcel with Mrs Rodrigues in flat 2B. We will be home after six in the evening, so please come back then if you need a signature. Thank you for understanding. - Flat 2A

Where should the parcel be left?
It should be left with Mrs Rodrigues in flat 2B.

Pet care list: Give the rabbit fresh grass and carrots. Clean the hutch on Saturdays. Keep the water bottle full. Do not let the rabbit near the stove. Brush the fur gently once a week. The rabbit's name is Bunty.

How do rabbits move around?
The text doesn't say, but rabbits move by hopping on their strong back legs.

Raita recipe: Beat one cup of curd until smooth. Add grated cucumber, a pinch of roasted cumin powder and salt. Mix well and chill for half an hour. Top with chopped mint leaves just before serving so they stay green.

When are the mint leaves added?
The mint leaves are added just before serving, so they stay green.

Gym-free morning plan from Grandpa: wake at 5:30, drink a glass of warm water, and walk twice around the park. Do ten minutes of stretching under the neem tree. Then sit with the newspaper and a cup of tea without sugar.

What is a newspaper?
The text doesn't say, but a newspaper is a printed paper, usually published daily, that reports the news.

School notice: Hand-washing week begins Monday. Each class will make a poster. Soap will be kept near all the taps. Teachers will show the children how to wash hands for twenty seconds. Prizes for the best poster.

Why do we wash our hands before eating?
The text doesn't say, but washing hands removes dirt and germs, so they do not get into our food and make us ill.

Note on the tiffin box: Dosa with chutney, one banana, and water. Do not forget to bring the box home. The rubber seal is loose, so keep the box upright in the bag. Wash it with warm soapy water.

What is a tiffin box used for?
The text doesn't say, but a tiffin box is a lunch box, often made of steel, used to carry food to school or work.

Diary, 17 August. Granny came from the village today with a big bag of guavas from her tree. She told me how, when she was small, she walked three kilometres to school with no shoes. I helped her unpack and she gave me a hug that smelled of coconut oil.

What did Granny bring from the village?
Granny brought a big bag of guavas from her tree.

Diary, 3 August. Our train left Chennai at dawn. I sat by the window and watched the paddy fields go by. Dad kept counting the stations. Around noon, a vendor came in with hot vadas, and we bought a whole packet.

Which crop grows in paddy fields?
The text doesn't say, but paddy fields are flooded fields used for growing rice.

Pet shop slip: One pair of lovebirds, one cage, one bag of seeds. The cage should be kept in a sunny but sheltered place. Fresh water twice daily. They get lonely, so do not separate the two. The shopkeeper advised a cloth over the cage at night.

Why should the two birds not be separated?
They should stay together because they get lonely.

Letter: Dear Meghna, I am writing to tell you that I have moved to a new school. The teachers are kind and my classroom has big windows. I miss our walks together. I hope you will write to me soon. Your friend, Preeti

What is the name of Preeti's new school?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the name of Preeti's new school. You could ask her in your reply.

Receipt note: Two bunches of spinach, one cauliflower and half a kilo of peas. Vegetable seller Rani said the peas are from the farm near her village and are very sweet. Total was cheaper than last week since the cauliflower was on offer.

Where do the peas come from, according to Rani?
She said the peas are from a farm near her village.

Scorebook note from the Sunday match: Team Red made 64 runs in eight overs. Team Blue chased well and finished on 61, three runs short. The best catch was taken by little Ishaan at the boundary. Both teams shook hands and shared lemon juice.

Who bowled the first over?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who bowled the first over. The scorer of that match would have it written down.

Tomato soup steps: Chop five tomatoes, one onion and a small piece of ginger. Boil them with a little water for ten minutes. Let it cool a bit and then blend. Strain, add salt and pepper, and reheat. Serve with toasted bread cubes.

What is served with the soup?
Toasted bread cubes are served with the soup.

Teacher's note on the chart: Today we planted a bean seed in a small cup. Each child has labelled their cup with their name. Please water it gently each day. We will compare the heights on Friday. Please do not pull the seeds out to look at them.

Whose bean will grow the tallest?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know whose bean will grow tallest. You will have to wait and measure them on Friday.

Knitting diary: I started a muffler for Dad with grey wool. The first row took me an hour because I kept dropping stitches. Nani showed me how to count each row. Today I finished fifteen rows, and I can finally knit while talking.

Who showed the writer how to count rows?
Nani showed the writer how to count each row.

Diary, 4 January. Our kite flying contest was on the terrace today. The wind was just right. My kite was red with a long tail and it went higher than all the others until Ishan's kite cut my string. We both laughed and shook hands.

Why do kites need wind?
The text doesn't say, but wind pushes against the kite and lifts it into the air, so a kite needs moving air to fly.

Courier slip: Parcel for Mr Anil Gupta, 3rd floor, Sunrise Apartments. Delivery attempted at 11 am, but nobody was at home. Next attempt will be tomorrow between 10 and 1. A neighbour can sign on his behalf if they show an ID.

Why was the parcel not delivered?
It was not delivered because nobody was at home when the courier came at 11 am.

Message to Aisha: Happy birthday! I hope you have a lovely day with your family. I made a card for you with the picture of our school bus. I will give it to you on Monday. Let us go for ice cream after school.

What do people usually do on a birthday?
The text doesn't say, but people usually celebrate with family and friends, with cake, gifts and good wishes.

Notice for parents: Class 3 will go on a walk to the nearby park on Tuesday. Children should wear their sports shoes and cap. Teachers will be in the group. The walk will be short and children will return before lunch.

How many children are in Class 3?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many children are in Class 3. The class teacher or school office can tell you.

Label on the steel tin: Besan. Bought from the Saturday market, opened on the 3rd. Store tightly closed because it gets lumpy in damp weather. Used for pakoras, kadhi and the sweet laddoos Nani makes. Do not mix with the wheat flour tin.

Why must the tin be kept tightly closed?
It must be kept closed because the besan gets lumpy in damp weather.

Diary, 6 October. Today at the music class, we learned a new raga for the evening, and I managed to sing the whole line without losing breath. Sir said my voice is getting steadier. On the way home, I hummed it so much that Amma asked me to rest my throat.

What did Amma ask the writer to do?
Amma asked the writer to rest their throat.

Lunchbox label: Arjun, Class 3B. Contains: two parathas, mango pickle (small), and cut cucumber. Please let him finish the cucumber first. He does not like the pickle on the paratha, so it is kept in a separate lid.

Where is the pickle kept in the lunchbox?
The pickle is kept in a separate lid, not on the paratha.

Lemonade tips: Squeeze two lemons into a jug of cold water. Add sugar slowly and stir until it dissolves. Put in a pinch of salt and a few mint leaves. Add ice at the end, so the drink does not get watery too soon.

Why is ice added at the end?
Ice is added at the end so the drink does not get watery too soon.

Jar label: Mango pickle, made in May by Nani. Keep the jar dry and use only a clean dry spoon. Store in a cool place, away from sunlight. Best finished within one year. Shake gently once a week. It was a good mango year.

How many mangoes did Nani use?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many mangoes she used. You could ask Nani.

Message from the school bus driver, Mr Thomas: The route has changed for two days because of road repair near the market. Pick-up from Green Park will be at the east gate instead of the main road. Children should stand in a line and not run near the bus.

Where will the Green Park pick-up be?
The Green Park pick-up will be at the east gate instead of the main road.

Dinner note from Amma: The kheer is in the glass bowl in the fridge. Have one bowl only, it is for everyone. Rotis are in the hot case and the brinjal curry is on the stove. Please wash your plates and leave the kitchen clean.

Where are the rotis?
The rotis are in the hot case.

Diary, 8 June. Today I saw a spider spinning a web between the two chairs on the balcony. It moved so fast that I could hardly see its legs. By evening the web was shining with tiny drops of dew, and a small fly was caught in the middle.

What do spiders use their webs for?
The text doesn't say, but spiders use their webs mainly to catch insects to eat.

Meeting notes, Tuesday. Present: Anita, Joseph, Farhan. Decided to move the team lunch to Friday. Joseph will book the hall. Farhan will send the agenda by Wednesday evening. Anita will bring the projector from the store room. The next meeting will be held the following Tuesday.

What does a projector do?
The text doesn't say, but a projector shines an image from a computer onto a wall or screen so a group can see it.

Nature walk note: We saw a kingfisher near the pond at 7 am. It dived twice and caught a small fish. Near the banyan tree there were many ants carrying leaf pieces. We did not see any snakes, but our guide showed us old fox tracks in the mud.

What was the guide's name?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the guide's name. The group leader or the park office could tell you.

Message to Sneha: I am sorry I missed your call last night. My phone was charging in the other room and I fell asleep early. Can we meet near the park gate on Sunday at five? I will bring the notes for the history test.

What will the writer bring on Sunday?
The writer will bring the notes for the history test.

Rangoli contest notice: Last date to join is Friday. The floor design must be made with natural colours, such as flower petals and rice flour. Size not more than one metre. The judges will come at 11 am on Saturday. Prizes will be given at the temple lawn.

What is a rangoli?
The text doesn't say, but a rangoli is a colourful pattern made on the floor, often at festivals, with powder, rice flour or flower petals.

To-do for Sunday: help Dad wash the scooter, clean my cupboard, finish the science drawing, and go to Aunt Priya's house for lunch at one. Take the sweets box from the kitchen and do not eat any of it.

What should be taken to Aunt Priya's house?
The sweets box from the kitchen should be taken there.

Message from the sports teacher: Tomorrow's athletics practice has moved from the ground to the covered court because the grass is wet. Wear sports shoes with a good grip. Bring a towel. Practice will end at 5, and the school bus will wait until 5:15.

Why has the practice moved to the covered court?
It moved because the grass on the ground is wet.

Diary, 11 April. Today we went to Kanyakumari and watched the sun rise over the sea. The sky turned pink first, then gold. Dad bought us hot tea in paper cups and we sat on the rocks till the sun was fully up.

In which direction does the sun rise?
The text doesn't say, but the sun rises in the east.

Origami class note: Today we folded paper cranes. Fold the square into a triangle, then again into a smaller triangle, and open the corners gently. The most difficult part was the neck. Sir said we may take the red paper home to practise.

How many cranes did the class make?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many cranes the class made. The teacher or other students could tell you.

Notice from the vet's clinic: The clinic is open from 9 to 1 and 5 to 8. Please bring your pet in a basket or on a leash. Keep other animals separate in the waiting room. Bring the earlier visit records so the doctor can see them.

What does a vet do?
The text doesn't say, but a vet is an animal doctor who treats sick pets and other animals.

Instruction slip in the water filter box: Rinse the filter candle gently under tap water every week. Do not use soap. Fill the top tank with tap water and wait for it to drip down. Change the candle every six months or when the flow gets very slow.

How often should the candle be rinsed?
The candle should be rinsed gently under tap water every week.

Chai instructions left by Papa: Boil one cup of water with two crushed cardamom pods and a small piece of ginger. Add a spoon of tea leaves and let it darken. Pour in one cup of milk and wait until it just rises. Strain and serve hot.

What is added after the tea leaves darken?
One cup of milk is added, and the tea is heated until it just rises.

River walk note: We saw a heron standing in the shallow water for about ten minutes without moving. Then it struck at a fish and flew off. There were pebbles of many colours near the bank, and I put two in my pocket.

How deep is the river?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how deep the river is. Local people or an official sign near the bank would know.

Plant label: Tulsi. Keep near a sunny window. Pinch off the flower tops to get more leaves. Water lightly every morning. Bought at the Sunday nursery for the balcony. The pot is blue and sits on the left side.

Why is tulsi often grown in Indian homes?
The text doesn't say, but many Hindu families grow tulsi because they consider it a holy plant, and its leaves are often added to tea.

Kite-making note: Cut thin bamboo sticks for the frame. Tie them in a cross with strong thread. Stick the coloured paper over the frame with glue. Attach the string to the middle with a small loop. Tie a tail made of cloth strips to the bottom.

What is the tail made of?
The tail is made of cloth strips.

Tiffin note from Dadi: The paratha has aloo inside. The small box has green chutney, so keep it upright. Drink all the water in the bottle before games period. Give the extra paratha to Sameer, he forgot his lunch yesterday.

Who should get the extra paratha?
Sameer should get the extra paratha.

Notice at the village well: The rains have been low this year. Please use water carefully. Use the washing area only until noon. Do not waste the water used for rinsing vegetables, give it to the plants. The village council will review the situation next month.

Where does rain come from?
The text doesn't say, but rain comes from clouds. Water from the sea and land rises as vapour, forms clouds and falls back as rain.

Library slip: Title - The Little Fox of Nilgiri. Borrowed by Sanjay on the 4th. Due back on the 18th. Fine for late return is two rupees a day. Please keep the book in a cover and do not fold the pages.

What is a fox?
The text doesn't say, but a fox is a small wild animal with a pointed face and a bushy tail, related to dogs.

Sweet shop board: Fresh jalebi is made from 4 pm each day. Rasgulla comes in boxes of six and twelve. Ask for sugar-free options at the counter. Festival orders must be placed three days in advance. Closed on Wednesdays. The shop is near the bus stand.

What is jalebi shaped like?
The text doesn't say, but jalebi is a crisp, orange spiral made from fried batter soaked in sugar syrup.

Farm notice for workers: Start picking the beans at 6 am before the sun is hot. Put the beans in the green crates, not the blue ones. Drink water often. The truck will leave at 11 for the market, so finish by 10:30.

Which crates are for the beans?
The beans go in the green crates, not the blue ones.

Who will lead the drum circle?

Football trial notice: Boys and girls of Classes 6 to 8 can come for the trial on Monday at 3:30. Wear shorts and boots, not slippers. The coach will watch you play for ten minutes each. Names of selected players will go on the board by Wednesday.

When will the names of selected players be put up?
The names will be on the board by Wednesday.

Observation sheet: Day 1, the bean seed is soaked and soft. Day 3, a white root has come out. Day 5, the root is longer and a green shoot is pushing up. Day 8, two small leaves have opened. We kept it near the window and wet the cotton every morning.

A white root came out first on Day 3.

Packing list for the hill trip: two sweaters, a rain jacket, thick socks, a torch, a water bottle, snacks, one extra pair of shoes and a small first-aid kit that Mum will check. Leave the heavy camera at home. Everything must fit in one backpack.

What should be left at home?
The heavy camera should be left at home.

Postcard from Tara: Greetings from the hills! The air is cool and the pine trees smell lovely. We went for a walk to the waterfall and I took many photos. I have kept a small stone for you. See you soon. Love, Tara

Class chart: The mango tree in our school grows new leaves in February. Flowers come in March, and green mangoes by May. The children from Class 4 count the fruits that fall and put them in the basket. The watchman keeps the extra ones for the staff room.

Are mangoes a fruit or a vegetable?
The text doesn't say, but a mango is a fruit.

Badminton club sheet: Practice on Tuesday and Thursday at 5:30. Bring your own racket. Shuttlecocks are kept in the cupboard in the hall. Please wipe the floor if you spill water. Doubles matches will be played on the last Saturday.

How many players are there in a doubles match?
The text doesn't say, but a doubles match has four players, two on each side.

Craft note: To make the paper lantern, fold the coloured sheet in half and cut slits from the folded side, stopping before the edge. Open it, roll it into a tube and glue the sides. Add a strip of paper on top as a handle.

What is glue used for?
The text doesn't say, but glue is a sticky substance used to stick things such as paper together.

Cycling club note: We will ride to the lake on Sunday. Meet at the park gate at 6 am. Helmets are a must. The ride is twelve kilometres each way, and we will rest at the banyan tree halfway. Bring a bottle of water. Slow riders will go in front.

Where will the riders rest?
They will rest at the banyan tree halfway.

Note in the notebook: Thanks, Pari, for helping me with the maths sums yesterday. I could not figure out the one with the fractions. I will return your pencil box tomorrow. Let us study together again next week. - Hamza

What did Pari help Hamza with?
Pari helped Hamza with the maths sums, especially the one with fractions.

Note from Dad on the table: I have gone to the station to pick up Uncle Ramesh. His train comes at 4:40. Please do not wait for us to have lunch. There is fresh buttermilk in the jug. If the doorbell rings, it will be the gas delivery man.

Who is Dad going to pick up?
Dad is going to the station to pick up Uncle Ramesh.

Parent circular: The annual day will be held on 22 December in the school hall. Classes 1 to 5 will perform a folk dance, and classes 6 to 8 will stage a short play. Parents may enter from 4 pm. Seats are not reserved, so please come early.

What is a folk dance?
The text doesn't say, but a folk dance is a traditional dance of a region or community, usually handed down over many years.

Message from Mum: I will be late today, around 8 pm. Take the spare key from the neighbour, Mrs Kapoor. Heat the sabzi in the small pan, not the big one. Finish your homework before you watch anything. Do not open the door for strangers.

The text doesn't say, and I don't know which sabzi Mum cooked. Look in the pan, or ask her when she is back.

Notice at the bus stop: Because of heavy rain, the 8:20 bus to the city will leave ten minutes later. All other buses will run on time. Passengers are asked to wait inside the shelter. Umbrellas are available at the ticket window.

What is delayed because of the rain?
The 8:20 bus to the city is delayed by ten minutes.

To-do list before the exam: pack the hall ticket, sharpen three pencils, carry a transparent water bottle, reach the school by 8:30 and sit in the room number written on the ticket. Sleep early the night before. Also keep your school ID card in the pocket.

What is a hall ticket for?
The text doesn't say, but a hall ticket is a card that shows you are allowed to sit the exam and tells you your seat or room.

Lunch order slip: Table four wants two plates of veg biryani, one without onions, and a mint lime soda. Table seven asked for the dessert menu. Table nine is waiting for the bill. Please serve table four first as they have a train at two.

Why should table four be served first?
Table four should be served first because they have a train at two.

Farmer's diary: First rains came on the tenth. We ploughed the field the next day and sowed the maize on the twelfth. Birds ate some of the seed, so we put up a scarecrow made of old clothes and a pot. By the end of the week, the first green shoots were up.

What did they put up to stop the birds?
They put up a scarecrow made of old clothes and a pot.

Receipt note stuck inside the bag: Bought two notebooks, one geometry box and a pack of five pencils. The shopkeeper said the geometry box can be exchanged within seven days if the compass is loose. Keep the paper slip for the exchange.

What is a compass used for in a geometry box?
The text doesn't say, but the compass in a geometry box is used to draw circles and arcs.

The monsoon fills the ponds in our village, and soon the frogs begin to croak at night. Children go to the edge of the water to look for tadpoles. Their grandmother tells them not to go close after dark. The older children make paper boats and race them along the edge of the water.

What do tadpoles grow into?
The text doesn't say, but tadpoles grow into frogs.

When you exercise, your heart beats faster. The muscles need more oxygen, and the blood brings it. After you stop, the heart rate slowly goes back to normal, and you feel tired but warm. Doctors say that regular exercise is good for growing children.

What organ do we use to think?
The text doesn't say, but we think with the brain.

Mushrooms are not plants. They belong to a group called fungi, and they cannot make food from sunlight. What we see above ground is only a small part. Most of a fungus is a network of fine threads under the soil or inside rotting wood.

Where is most of a fungus found?
Most of it is a network of fine threads under the soil or inside rotting wood.

On the coast, the sea breeze starts around mid-morning. The land warms faster than the water, so air above the land rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in to take its place. At night the pattern turns around and the wind blows towards the sea.

Why does warm air rise?
The text doesn't say, but warm air rises because it is lighter than the cooler air around it.

A thunderstorm cloud builds when warm, damp air rises quickly. As the air climbs it cools, and the water in it turns into droplets and ice. Rubbing between these pieces builds up electric charge, and a lightning flash releases it with a loud crack of thunder.

What builds up electric charge inside a storm cloud?
Droplets and pieces of ice rubbing against each other build up the charge.

A cheetah can reach a very high speed over a short distance, but it tires quickly. After a chase it must rest for a long while before it can hunt again. If a bigger animal finds the kill, the cheetah often gives up its meal.

What kind of food does a cheetah eat?
The text doesn't say, but cheetahs are meat eaters, and they hunt animals such as antelope.

A rainwater tank on the school roof collects water in the monsoon. A pipe carries it from the gutter to the tank, and a mesh keeps the leaves out. The water is used to wash the floors and water the plants.

Does water flow uphill or downhill by itself?
The text doesn't say, but water flows downhill by itself, because of gravity.

A baby is born with more bones than an adult has. Some small bones join together as the child grows. By the time a person is fully grown, there are about two hundred and six bones. Some of the softer ones are made of a bendy material called cartilage at first.

What is the hardest part of a tooth?
The text doesn't say, but the enamel, the outer layer, is the hardest part of a tooth.

Dr Rao's talk at our school was about the importance of sleep and breakfast for growing children. He told the class that screens before bedtime make it harder to fall asleep. Afterwards, students could ask questions and take a leaflet home.

What did Dr Rao have for breakfast that day?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know what he ate. You could ask him directly if you meet him.

A banyan tree starts life when a bird drops a seed in the fork of another tree. The young banyan sends thin roots down toward the ground. Over many years these roots thicken into pillars, and the banyan slowly covers and often outlives its host.

How does a banyan tree begin to grow?
A bird drops a seed in the fork of another tree, and the young banyan sends roots down from there.

A flood in a river valley is often not caused by rain in that valley. Heavy rain far upstream, or melting snow in the mountains, can send a large wave of water downstream days later. This is why people living near rivers listen to the weather office's flood warnings.

Can rain far away cause a flood in a river valley?
Yes, heavy rain far upstream or melting mountain snow can send a flood wave downstream.

The first Indian satellite was launched in the 1970s. Since then, India has built many satellites for weather, communication and mapping. Many schools watch the launches on television, and children in small towns gather around the screen to follow the countdown.

What do we call a person who travels into space?
The text doesn't say, but a person who travels into space is called an astronaut.

Dolphins live in groups called pods. They talk to each other with clicks and whistles, and they often leap out of the water. Some pods work together to herd fish into a tight ball before feeding. They are curious animals and sometimes swim alongside boats.

Are dolphins fish or mammals?
The text doesn't say, but dolphins are mammals, not fish.

In winter, the air in the north of India is often cold and still at night. Smoke and dust get trapped near the ground, and mixed with fog they form a thick haze. Light winds or a change in the weather can clear it, but until then visibility is poor.

What can clear the winter haze?
Light winds or a change in the weather can clear it.

Hail forms inside tall storm clouds. Strong winds inside the cloud carry raindrops up into very cold air where they freeze. The ice pellet falls, collects more water, and is carried up again, growing bigger each trip until it is too heavy to stay up.

Why does a hailstone fall to the ground?
It becomes too heavy for the winds to hold it up.

Butterflies taste with their feet. When a butterfly lands on a leaf, sensors on its feet tell it if the plant is a good place to lay eggs. This matters because the caterpillars that hatch can usually eat only one or a few kinds of plant.

How does a butterfly decide where to lay its eggs?
It tastes the leaf with its feet to see if the plant is suitable.

This year's monsoon reached Kerala a few days late. Farmers in the area waited to sow their rice, and some fields were planted only after the third week of June. Most farmers expect a normal harvest.

What will the harvest be like in the end?
The text doesn't say, and I can't know the final harvest. The farmers' reports at the end of the season would show it.

An echo happens when sound bounces off a hard surface, such as a wall or a cliff, and comes back to your ears. The sound needs a small delay to return, so you hear it as a second, fainter version of your shout. Soft materials like curtains soak up sound and give no echo.

Why do curtains give no echo?
Soft materials soak up the sound instead of bouncing it back.

Farmers in Punjab sow wheat in the cool months and harvest it in spring. The green fields turn golden as the grain ripens. After harvest, the grain is dried and stored in sacks or large bins.

Once the wheat is ground into flour, what is the flour used to make?
The text doesn't say, but wheat flour is used to make rotis, bread and many other foods.

The sea around the Andaman Islands is clear and warm. Divers go there to look at coral and colourful fish. Boats are kept away from the most delicate reefs so that the coral is not broken. The water is calm in the morning and the best time to go out is early.

Is the sea salty or sweet?
The text doesn't say, but sea water is salty.

A newspaper article reported that scientists spotted a bright new comet through a telescope last week. It is still far away, and it is too faint to see without help. If it keeps coming closer, it may be visible to the naked eye in a few months.

Will the comet be visible in our city?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know if it will be visible from your city. An astronomy club or an observatory can tell you when it is close enough.

A tiger's stripes are different on every animal, like fingerprints. The stripes help the tiger hide in tall grass and forest light, where the pattern breaks up its outline. Tigers prefer to hunt alone, usually at dusk or at night.

What do a tiger's stripes help it do?
They help the tiger hide in tall grass and in the forest light.

Your eyes have a small opening in the middle called the pupil. In bright light it gets smaller so that less light gets in, and in dim light it opens wide to let more light in. This change happens on its own, without you thinking about it.

What does the pupil do in dim light?
It opens wide to let more light in.

The Moon seems to change shape through the month, but it is only our view that changes. Half of the Moon is always lit by the Sun. As the Moon moves around Earth, we see more or less of the lit half, and that gives us the phases from new Moon to full Moon.

Why does the Moon seem to change shape?
We see more or less of its lit half as it moves around Earth.

Termites build mounds that can be taller than a person. Inside, small tunnels let air move through the mound and keep the temperature steady. Workers carry soil bit by bit, and each mound can be home to millions of termites.

What do the tunnels inside a termite mound do?
They let air move through and keep the temperature steady.

Some students made a small filter from a plastic bottle. They put in layers of pebbles, sand and cotton, then poured muddy water through the top. The water that dripped out was much clearer, though the teacher reminded them it was still not safe to drink.

At what temperature does water boil?
The text doesn't say, but water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.

Ants had been marching in a thin line across our kitchen floor all week. Mother found they were coming from a crack under the window and heading for the sugar jar. She put the jar in a bowl of water, and the line slowly disappeared.

How many ants were in the line?
The text doesn't say, and I can't know that number. Someone would have to count the ants the next time they appear.

A dust storm begins when strong winds blow across dry, bare land and lift loose soil into the air. The cloud can be a kilometre high and travel hundreds of kilometres. Planting trees and grass helps hold soil in place and lowers the risk.

How does planting trees and grass help with dust storms?
It helps hold the soil in place, which lowers the risk.

Rivers do not stay in one place for ever. Water carries soil and sand from the banks, and where the river bends, the outer bank wears away while the inner bank collects mud. Over many years the bends grow, and the river's path slowly moves across the land.

Where does a river bend wear away the bank?
The outer bank wears away, while the inner bank collects mud.

Wolves live and hunt in packs. Each pack has a leader pair, and the other wolves are usually their young. They talk to each other by howling, and the sound can carry for many kilometres on a quiet night. They travel long distances every night in search of food.

Are wolves related to dogs?
The text doesn't say, but yes, pet dogs are descended from wolves, so they are close relatives.

Coral reefs look like rocks or plants, but they are built by tiny animals called polyps. Each polyp makes a hard cup of limestone around its soft body. When polyps die, their cups stay behind, and new polyps grow on top, so the reef rises very slowly over centuries.

What are coral reefs built by?
They are built by tiny animals called polyps, which make hard limestone cups around their bodies.

A cave in Meghalaya has a river flowing through it, and the water carved the passage out of limestone over thousands of years. Visitors walk in with guides and helmets because the floor is wet and uneven. The guides ask everyone to keep to the marked path to protect the rock shapes.

Why are visitors asked to keep to the marked path?
To protect the rock shapes in the cave.

A map shows land and water from above. On many maps, blue is used for water and green for lowlands. Mountain areas are drawn in brown, and the lines on them join places of the same height.

What are the four main directions on a compass?
The text doesn't say, but they are north, south, east and west.

A forest has layers. At the top are the tall trees that form the canopy. Below them live smaller trees and shrubs, and on the ground are ferns, fungi and fallen leaves. Each layer gets a different amount of light and shelters different animals.

What grows on the forest floor?
Ferns, fungi and fallen leaves are found on the ground.

The layers of Earth are the crust, the mantle and the core. The crust is a thin skin of rock that we live on. Below it, the mantle is thick and hot, and at the centre the core is made mostly of iron and is about as hot as the surface of the Sun.

What is the core of Earth made of?
It is made mostly of iron.

A glacier is a huge river of ice that moves very slowly down a mountain valley. Snow piles up at the top and is pressed into ice by its own weight. At the lower end the ice melts into streams, which feed many of the great rivers of the plains.

What do the streams from a glacier feed?
They feed many of the great rivers of the plains.

A pair of hornbills nest in the tall tree behind the old hospital. The female stays inside a hole in the trunk, which is sealed with mud, while the male brings her food through a small gap. A bird watcher has been keeping a diary of their visits.

What is the bird watcher's name?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the name. You could ask at a local bird-watching group.

Your lungs fill with air each time you breathe in. A muscle under the lungs, flat like a sheet, pulls down and makes room for the air to rush in. When the muscle relaxes, the air is pushed out again.

How many lungs does a person have?
The text doesn't say, but a person has two lungs.

Owls hunt mostly at night. Their large eyes gather dim light, and their ears sit at slightly different heights on the head, which helps them find the exact spot where a sound comes from. Soft feather edges let them fly almost without a sound.

How do soft feather edges help an owl?
They let the owl fly almost silently.

A shadow forms when something blocks the light. It is longest early in the morning and late in the afternoon, when the sun is low in the sky. At noon, when the sun is high, shadows are short and sit close to the object.

When are shadows shortest?
They are shortest at noon, when the sun is high in the sky.

The water we drink has been around for billions of years. It goes up into the air as vapour, forms clouds, falls as rain or snow, runs back to the sea, and goes up again. Scientists call this long loop the water cycle.

What do scientists call the loop of water going up and coming down?
They call it the water cycle.

Fog is a cloud that touches the ground. It forms on calm, cool nights when the air close to the ground cannot hold all its water vapour, and the vapour turns into tiny droplets. Morning sunshine warms the air and usually clears the fog by late morning.

When does fog usually clear?
It usually clears by late morning, once the sun has warmed the air.

A day on Earth is the time the planet takes to spin once. Because it spins, each part of the planet faces the Sun for some hours and then turns away. The side facing the Sun has daytime, and the side facing away has night.

What causes day and night on Earth?
Earth spinning, so that each side faces the Sun for part of the time and then turns away.

A spring day, according to Rohan's science journal: The pond near our house was full of tadpoles. I counted about thirty before they swam off. A heron stood still at the edge of the water, and I think it was waiting for a meal.

What was the heron doing at the pond?
It stood still at the water's edge, probably waiting for a meal.

Every year, a stork couple returns to the roof of the old school. They repair their big nest with fresh sticks and raise two or three chicks. The caretaker puts a ladder away so that no one climbs up and disturbs them.

How many years have the storks come to the school?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the number of years. The caretaker may remember.

Silkworms feed on mulberry leaves for about a month and then spin a cocoon around themselves. The silk thread in one cocoon can be hundreds of metres long. Workers soften the cocoons in hot water and unwind the thread.

What do silkworms turn into if they are left alone in the cocoon?
The text doesn't say, but they turn into moths.

A team of students measured the depth of the village pond with a long rope tied to a stone. They found that it was deeper near the old banyan tree than near the road. They wrote their results in a table and put it on the class notice board.

How deep was the pond near the banyan tree?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the exact number. The table on the notice board should have it.

A small earthquake shook the district one night, but no damage was reported. Most people slept through it, and a few woke up when the windows rattled. The district office asked families to review their safety plans. The shaking lasted only a few seconds.

What was the strength of the earthquake?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the strength. The national seismology office publishes the figures for every quake.

Astronomers have found thousands of planets that go around stars other than our Sun. Most of them are too far away to see directly. They are found by watching for tiny dips in the light of their star when a planet passes in front of it.

What is the name of our galaxy?
The text doesn't say, but our galaxy is called the Milky Way.

Sparrows used to be common in cities, but their numbers have fallen in many places. Nest sites in old buildings have become scarce, and there are fewer insects for the chicks to eat. Some neighbourhoods put up small wooden nest boxes to help them.

What do sparrow chicks hatch from?
The text doesn't say, but they hatch from eggs.

Coal is found in layers under the ground. In India it is mined in states like Jharkhand and Odisha. Miners work in large open pits or go down shafts, and the coal is then carried by train to power stations.

What do power stations make by burning coal?
The text doesn't say, but power stations burn coal to make electricity.

Kingfishers dive from a branch above the water to catch small fish. They often sit very still before the dive. After catching a fish, the bird returns to the perch and hits the fish on the branch before swallowing it head first.

What colour are many kingfishers?
The text doesn't say, but many kingfishers are bright blue, with orange or white on the chest.

Parrots can copy sounds because of the way their throats and tongues are built. In the wild, they use calls to stay in touch with their flock. A pet parrot may copy the sounds of a family, since the family has become its flock.

Why might a pet parrot copy its family's words?
The family has become its flock, and parrots copy sounds to stay in touch with their flock.

The school's new electric bus runs on a battery that needs about five hours to charge. The driver plugs it in every evening in the shed behind the sports ground. The bus makes almost no noise, and the children say it feels like riding in a library.

How much did the bus cost?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know its price. The school office or management could tell you.

The weather office has warned that a low-pressure area over the sea may bring heavy rain to the coast over the next two days. Fishing boats are asked to stay in harbour, and schools in low-lying areas may close at short notice. Updates will be given every six hours.

Will it rain in the city next week?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the forecast for next week. The weather office's latest update is the best place to check.

Last night's school sky-watch lasted until ten. We saw the Moon, a bright planet low in the west and a few shooting stars. Our teacher, Mrs Kapoor, pointed out three star patterns and promised to bring a telescope next time.

Which planet did the students see in the west?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which planet it was. Mrs Kapoor could tell you, or a sky-chart app on a phone could.

The text from the town council says that a new water-testing van will visit the colony next month. It will test samples from taps and wells, and the results will be put up on the community board. Residents who want their well tested should give their names at the office.

What will the test results show?
The text doesn't say, and I can't know the results before the test is done. The community board will show them once they are ready.

Stalactites hang from the roof of a cave like icicles, and stalagmites rise from the floor beneath them. Both grow when drops of water that carry dissolved minerals fall and leave a thin layer behind. They grow only a tiny bit each year, so a big one is very old.

Why is a big stalactite very old?
They grow only a tiny bit each year, so a big one has taken a very long time.

Ravi kept a jar with a few caterpillars and fresh leaves for a school project. Each day he cleaned the jar and counted how much they ate. After a week, two of them had hung from the lid and begun to form their cases.

What kind of butterfly did the caterpillars become?
The text doesn't say, and I can't know the kind. Ravi could tell you what leaves they ate, which would help to find out.

Mangrove trees grow along coasts in salty mud. Their roots stick up out of the water like stilts, helping them to breathe and holding the mud in place. Young fish hide among the roots, and the whole forest softens the force of big waves during storms.

How do mangrove forests help during storms?
They soften the force of big waves.

The life of a butterfly has four stages: egg, caterpillar, pupa and adult. The caterpillar eats leaves and grows quickly. Then it forms a hard case, the pupa, and inside it the body is rebuilt. After about two weeks, a butterfly comes out.

What happens inside the pupa?
The caterpillar's body is rebuilt into a butterfly.

The new baby elephant at the sanctuary was born in March and weighs about as much as a grown man. Keepers feed it milk several times a day. Visitors can watch from a viewing platform but cannot go near.

What name have the keepers given the baby elephant?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the name. The sanctuary's office or website can tell you.

Dragonflies spend most of their lives in water. The young, called nymphs, live in ponds for months or even years and catch small creatures. When ready, a nymph climbs up a plant stem, splits its skin and comes out as a winged adult that lives for only a few weeks.

Where do young dragonflies live?
They live in ponds, in the water.

The school's science room has a tank of goldfish. Students take turns feeding them once a day, and a small chart on the wall shows whose turn it is. Last week a new fish was added, and it has been hiding behind the plastic plants.

What is the new fish called?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know if it has a name. The students who look after the tank could tell you.

Note from Anaya's field diary: Today I saw a green lizard on the wall behind the kitchen. It stayed still when I came close, then ran into a crack near the water pipe. I will try to see it again tomorrow morning.

What was the lizard's name?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know if Anaya gave the lizard a name. You could ask her.

Rainwater that soaks into the ground does not stop there. It trickles down through soil and cracks in rock until it reaches a layer that is full of water, called an aquifer. Wells are dug down to this layer so people can pump water up for farms and homes.

Where do wells get their water from?
They reach down to an aquifer, a layer underground that is full of water.

A new pond was dug in the village last winter. It filled up in the first week of the monsoon, and ducks arrived soon after. The village council plans to stock the pond with fish and to plant trees all around it.

Which kind of fish will the council put in the pond?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which kind they chose. The village council can tell you.

A windmill turns because moving air pushes on its blades. The turning blades spin a shaft, and in a wind farm that shaft drives a machine that makes electricity. If the wind is too strong, the blades are turned sideways so that they do not break.

What do the blades do if the wind is too strong?
They are turned sideways so that they do not break.

Salt flats are wide, flat areas covered in a crust of salt. They form where a shallow lake dries out and leaves the salt behind. In the dry season the surface is hard and white, but after rain it can turn into a thin mirror of water.

How do salt flats form?
A shallow lake dries out and leaves the salt behind.

Tea bushes are grown on hill slopes because the roots do not like standing water, and the steep ground lets rain run off. Pickers pluck only the top two leaves and a bud, since the young leaves make the best tea. New leaves grow back within a week or two.

Which parts of the tea bush do pickers pluck?
They pluck the top two leaves and a bud.

A newly hatched chick is covered with soft down and stays close to its mother hen. The hen scratches the ground to find seeds and bugs, and calls the chicks to eat. At night she spreads her wings and keeps them warm.

What do hens give us that people eat?
The text doesn't say, but hens give us eggs.

Weaver birds build hanging nests from strips of grass and leaves. The male ties knots with his beak and feet, and he hangs the nest from a thin branch. If the female does not like it, he may pull it apart and start again.

What happens if the female weaver bird does not like the nest?
The male may pull it apart and build it again.

Seeds travel in surprising ways. Dandelion seeds have light fluffy parts that carry them on the wind. Burrs have tiny hooks that stick to fur and clothes. Coconuts float on the sea and may land on a beach far from the tree that dropped them.

How do burrs travel?
Tiny hooks on them stick to fur and clothes.

The lotus grows in muddy ponds, but its leaves and flowers stay clean. Water rolls off the leaf in round drops that carry dust away with them. The flower opens in the morning and closes towards the evening. In many Indian paintings and poems, the lotus is used as a sign of purity.

Which flower is India's national flower?
The text doesn't say, but the lotus is India's national flower.

Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System, but a day there is short. It spins once in about ten hours, so the planet's clouds are stretched into bands of brown, white and orange. The famous Great Red Spot is a huge storm that has lasted for well over a hundred years.

What is the Great Red Spot?
It is a huge storm on Jupiter that has lasted for well over a hundred years.

The Sun's heat dries wet clothes on a line. Wind helps too, by carrying away the damp air near the cloth. This is why clothes dry fastest on sunny, breezy days. On cloudy, damp days, the same clothes can stay wet for a whole afternoon.

What is the process called when water turns into vapour?
The text doesn't say, but it is called evaporation.

Dolphins sleep with half of their brain at a time. One half rests while the other half stays awake, so the dolphin can still rise to the surface to breathe. After a few hours the halves swap jobs.

How does a dolphin manage to keep breathing while it sleeps?
One half of its brain stays awake, so it can still rise to breathe.

Doctors say that growing children need a good night's sleep. During sleep, the body repairs itself and the brain sorts what you learned during the day. Many schools ask students to go to bed early before exams. Teachers often remind the class to drink water and eat a good breakfast as well.

Which organ in the body pumps blood?
The text doesn't say, but the heart pumps blood around the body.

Fingerprints form before a baby is born, and they do not change as a person grows. Each person has their own pattern. The tiny ridges help us grip things and feel textures. Police and offices often use them to check who a person is.

How many fingers are there on one hand?
The text doesn't say, but there are five fingers on one hand, counting the thumb.

The deepest parts of the sea are dark and very cold. Some fish there make their own light to attract food, using a glowing bit on a stalk above the mouth. Others have huge mouths and stretchy stomachs so that they can swallow whatever comes by.

How do some deep-sea fish attract food?
They use a glowing part on a stalk above the mouth.

The monsoon in India starts when winds blowing from the sea bring wet air over the land. As the air rises over hills and mountains, it cools and drops its water as rain. The first showers usually reach the southern coast in early June.

Where do the first monsoon showers usually arrive?
They usually arrive on the southern coast, in early June.

Locust swarms can eat as much food in a day as thousands of people. A swarm moves with the wind and may cover many kilometres. Farmers who see young locusts on the ground report them early so that officials can act before the insects can fly.

How many legs does an insect have?
The text doesn't say, but insects have six legs.

Our class is growing beans in paper cups to see how roots and shoots grow. We put cotton wool at the bottom and keep it damp. After three days, the seeds swelled, and a small white root came out of each one. We are measuring the shoots every day.

Which student's bean will grow the tallest?
The text doesn't say, and I can't know that. You will have to keep measuring and compare the results.

Snakes do not have ears like ours. They feel shaking in the ground through their jaw bones and pick up smells with their tongue, which flicks in and out. A snake sheds its skin several times a year as it grows.

How do snakes pick up smells?
They pick them up with their tongue.

Honeybees tell each other where flowers are by dancing. A bee that finds good flowers returns to the hive and waggles in a figure of eight. The angle of the waggle shows the direction, and a longer waggle means the flowers are farther away.

What does a longer waggle in the bee dance mean?
It means the flowers are farther away.

A volunteer group rescued a young monkey that had been caught in a fence near the highway. A vet cleaned its leg and kept it for two days. Then the volunteers took it to the forest and let it go near a troop of monkeys.

What was the name of the vet?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the vet's name. The volunteer group could tell you.

Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System, even hotter than Mercury. Thick clouds of gas trap the Sun's heat, and the surface is hot enough to melt lead. Spacecraft that landed there stopped working within a couple of hours.

Which planet is closest to the Sun?
The text doesn't say, but Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

Granite is a hard rock made of tiny crystals. It forms when hot melted rock cools slowly deep underground. Builders use it for steps, pillars and kitchen counters because it does not wear away easily. Old temples and forts in many parts of the country are built from it.

Is granite an igneous rock or a sedimentary rock?
The text doesn't say, but granite is an igneous rock, since it forms from cooled melted rock.

Satellites orbit Earth at different heights. Weather satellites take pictures of clouds, and some others help ships and planes find their way. A satellite stays up because it moves sideways very fast while Earth's pull bends its path into a circle around the planet.

What do weather satellites do?
They take pictures of clouds.

The old peepal tree near the temple is more than a hundred years old, the priest says. Birds nest in its branches, and children play under it after school. When a storm broke one big limb, the villagers decided to cut no more branches.

Who planted the peepal tree?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who planted it. Older people in the village may remember the story.

The colour of the sky changes at sunrise and sunset because the sunlight has a longer path through the air. On the way, most of the blue light is scattered away, and more of the red and orange light reaches our eyes. At midday the path is shorter, and the sky looks blue.

Why does the sky look red or orange at sunset?
The sunlight travels a longer path through the air, and the blue light is scattered away.

The Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system in the world. It is made of thousands of separate reefs and can be seen from space. Warm water can cause corals to lose their colour and may harm them.

In which country is the Great Barrier Reef found?
The text doesn't say, but it is off the coast of Australia.

A solar panel changes sunlight into electricity. Light knocks tiny charged particles loose inside thin slices of a material called silicon, and the loose particles are pushed along wires as a current. On a cloudy day a panel still works, but it makes less power.

What happens to a solar panel on a cloudy day?
It still works, but it makes less power.

The article about the new telescope says it will be switched on next year. Scientists plan to use it to look at distant galaxies and the atmospheres of faraway planets. The first pictures will be shared on the project's website.

What will the first picture from the telescope show?
The text doesn't say, and I can't know that. The project's website will show it once it is released.

A new bamboo grove was planted at the edge of the school ground last month. Students watered it in turns, and a small sign says the shoots can grow very fast in the rains. The gardener hopes the bamboo will become a green fence in a few years.

How tall is the bamboo now?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the current height. Someone could measure it with a tape.

Notes from the zoo visit: The red panda spent the morning asleep in a fork of a tree. The keeper said red pandas are most active at dawn and dusk. They eat mainly bamboo leaves, but they also enjoy fruit and eggs. Its thick tail wraps around the body like a blanket.

When are red pandas most active?
They are most active at dawn and dusk.

The municipal office says that the water supply in Ward 12 will be shut from nine in the morning to four in the evening on Thursday, while a main pipe is repaired. Tankers will be sent to the main streets. Residents are asked to store water on Wednesday night.

Who will repair the pipe?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which workers will do it. The municipal office could tell you if you call them.

Jaya spotted a nest of sparrows in the old streetlight outside her house. Three tiny eggs lay in a cup of grass and thread. She watched from the window for days, and one morning heard faint chirping from inside.

How many chicks hatched from the eggs?
The text doesn't say, and I can't know how many hatched. Jaya could tell you if she watched until the end.

Sound travels as waves of shaking air. When a drum is hit, its skin vibrates and pushes the air next to it, and that push passes along from one bit of air to the next until it reaches your ear. In water, sound moves faster than it does in air.

Where does sound move faster, in water or in air?
It moves faster in water.

A rain gauge is a simple tube that collects rainfall. It is placed in an open spot, away from trees and roofs. At the same time every morning, the water level is read from the scale on the side and the tube is emptied.

Where should a rain gauge be placed?
It should be placed in an open spot, away from trees and roofs.

Our village school has a mango tree in the yard, and the children love it. Each summer the tree is full of fruit, and the teachers share the ripe ones at lunch. In the last storm, a branch fell and the headmaster had it cut into stools.

How many mangoes did the tree give last year?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the number. The headmaster or the teachers might remember.

The solar lamps in our village were installed last year. Each lamp charges during the day and glows all night. The panchayat has asked residents to keep the panels clean and to report any lamp that does not work. Before that, the lanes were dark and people carried torches after sunset.

Who made the solar lamps?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the maker. The panchayat office may have the installation papers.

Message to the class: The telescope night is on Friday, if the sky is clear. We will look at the Moon first, then at Saturn, whose rings are easy to see even in a small telescope. If it is cloudy, we will move the night to the following Friday.

What will happen if Friday is cloudy?
The telescope night will move to the following Friday.

Cicadas spend years underground as young insects. Then, on one warm evening, they climb out, shed their skins and sing loudly in the trees. The loud buzzing is made by special drum-like parts on the sides of the male's body.

How many legs does a cicada have?
The text doesn't say, but a cicada, like all insects, has six legs.

Sunflowers are named for their habit of facing the sun. Young flowers turn from east to west during the day and swing back at night. Once the flower is fully grown, it stops moving and stays facing east, where bees visit it early in the morning.

Which way does a fully grown sunflower face?
It faces east.

Paper is made from wood fibres, so using less paper helps save trees. Collected waste paper can be soaked in water and mashed into pulp, then pressed into new sheets. Recycled paper uses less water and less energy than making paper from fresh wood.

How is recycled paper made?
Waste paper is soaked and mashed into pulp, then pressed into new sheets.

At low tide, the rock pools near the old lighthouse are full of small crabs and sea snails. Students from the nature club go there once a month to record what they find. They always put the animals back in the same spot.

How many crabs did the club find last month?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know that number. The nature club's record book would show it.

Bones are alive. They have blood vessels and cells that keep building new bone to replace old bone. When a bone breaks, these cells make new material that joins the two ends, which is why a cast keeps the pieces still while the bone heals.

Why is a cast used on a broken bone?
It keeps the pieces still so that the bone can join and heal.

Crows are among the smartest birds. They can use sticks as tools to pull insects out of holes, and they remember human faces. In some towns, crows have learned to drop nuts on the road so that passing cars crack them open.

How have some town crows learned to open nuts?
They drop the nuts on the road so passing cars crack them open.

After the rains, the hills near our village turn green. Streams that were dry in summer begin to run, and tiny waterfalls appear on the rock faces. Farmers from the valley go up to graze goats on the new grass.

Which season comes after summer in India?
The text doesn't say, but the monsoon season comes after summer in India.

In rural areas, some families use biogas for cooking. A tank is filled with cow dung and water, and as it breaks down, it gives off a gas that burns. The leftover slurry is used as manure for the fields.

What is the main gas in biogas that burns?
The text doesn't say, but the main gas in biogas is methane, which burns with a clean blue flame.

Two weeks ago, a family of otters moved into the river near our town. People stand on the bridge in the evenings to watch them slide down the bank. A local group put up a sign asking visitors to stay quiet and not to feed them.

How many otters are in the family?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the number. The local group may have counted them.

The forest guide told us that the path to the waterfall takes about an hour on foot. He asked everyone to wear shoes with a good grip and to carry water. Children under ten must walk beside an adult, and nobody may swim in the pool at the bottom.

What is the height of the waterfall?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know its height. The forest office or the guide could give you the number.

Grasshoppers have strong back legs that let them jump long distances. They eat leaves and, in large numbers, can damage crops. Their ears are on the sides of their bellies, not on their heads. They are usually green or brown, which helps them hide in grass.

Does a grasshopper have wings?
The text doesn't say, but yes, most grasshoppers have wings and can fly short distances.

A bat finds its way in the dark by shouting very high squeaks that people cannot hear. The squeaks bounce off objects and return as echoes. By listening to how long an echo takes to come back, the bat can tell how far away a moth or a branch is.

How does a bat tell how far away something is?
It listens to how long the echo of its squeak takes to come back.

Marble is a smooth rock that was once limestone. Heat and pressure deep inside Earth changed it over millions of years. Sculptors and builders like marble because it can be cut and polished to a shine.

Is marble a hard rock or a soft substance like clay?
The text doesn't say, but marble is a hard rock, though softer than granite.
