Mars is called the red planet because its soil has a lot of iron that has rusted. The planet is cold and has a thin air that people could not breathe. Robots on wheels have been sent there to study the rocks and look for signs that water once flowed.

Why is Mars called the red planet?
Its soil has a lot of rusted iron.

Hummingbirds can hover in the air because they beat their wings very fast, sometimes dozens of times in a second. They drink nectar with a long tongue and need to feed often. At night they can slow their bodies down to save energy.

How do hummingbirds save energy at night?
They slow their bodies down.

Neem trees are common along Indian roads and in village yards. They stay green through the dry season and give good shade. Many families use the twigs, and the leaves are known for their very bitter taste.

What gas do trees take in from the air?
The text doesn't say, but trees take in carbon dioxide from the air.

Ginger is grown from pieces of rhizome that have buds on them. Farmers plant the pieces in warm, damp soil before the rains. Eight or nine months later, they dig up the thick, knobbly rhizomes to sell. Many people add it to tea on cold mornings.

Is ginger a spice?
The text doesn't say, but yes, ginger is a spice used in food and tea.

The lake behind our school freezes over in a thin layer in the coldest weeks. On those mornings, students can see a pattern of tiny crystals on the ice. The caretaker puts up a sign to keep everyone off it until the sun melts it.

What is frozen water called?
The text doesn't say, but frozen water is called ice.

Pigeons can find their way home from hundreds of kilometres away. For centuries, people used them to carry messages. Scientists think that pigeons use the Sun, smells and a sense of Earth's magnetic field to find the way.

What group of animals do pigeons belong to?
The text doesn't say, but pigeons are birds.

A rainbow appears when sunlight passes through raindrops. Each drop bends the light and splits it into its colours, from red to violet. To see a rainbow you need the sun behind you and the rain in front of you.

Where must the sun be for you to see a rainbow?
The sun must be behind you, with the rain in front of you.

Every autumn, monarch butterflies in North America fly thousands of kilometres to warm forests in Mexico. No single butterfly makes the whole round trip. The ones that fly south are several generations younger than those that left in spring, yet they somehow find the same forests.

Does a single monarch butterfly make the whole round trip?
No. No single butterfly makes the whole trip; it takes several generations.

Hot-water bottles and radiators both work because heat moves from warm things to cold ones. A hot cup of tea loses heat to the air around it until both are the same temperature. A lid slows the loss, so the tea stays warm for longer.

Why does a lid keep tea warm longer?
It slows the loss of heat from the tea to the air.

Grandmother's tulsi plant stands in a small clay pot on the front step. Every morning she waters it and lights a lamp beside it. When we had a cold last winter, she made tea with a few of its leaves, and the whole house smelled fresh.

How old is the tulsi plant?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know its age. Grandmother could tell you when she planted it.

Mother crows protect their nests fiercely. Near our building, a crow chased a cat away when it came too close to a tree. The next day, the same crow followed the cat's path from far above, as if it were keeping watch.

What do baby birds hatch from?
The text doesn't say, but baby birds hatch from eggs.

Dew forms on grass overnight when the ground cools and the air just above it can no longer hold all its water vapour. The vapour turns into tiny drops on the cold leaves. Dew is most common on clear, still nights, since clouds and wind keep the ground warmer.

On what kind of night does dew form most often?
It forms most often on clear, still nights.

A snail carries its shell on its back, and it pulls its soft body inside when it feels danger. It moves on a single muscular foot and leaves a trail of slime behind it. In dry weather, the snail seals the opening of the shell and waits for rain.

How many legs does a snail have?
The text doesn't say, but a snail has no legs. It moves on a single foot.

Lichens are made of two living things working together: a fungus and an alga. The fungus gives shelter and holds water, and the alga makes food from sunlight. Together they can grow on bare rock, where neither could live alone.

What does the alga do in a lichen?
It makes food from sunlight.

Flamingos are pink because of what they eat. The tiny shrimp and algae in their food contain a colour that the birds' bodies turn into pink. Chicks are born grey and become pink only after they eat this food for some time.

Why are flamingos pink?
The colour comes from the tiny shrimp and algae they eat.

Eagles build large nests called eyries on cliffs or in tall trees, and they return to the same nest year after year. Each year they add more sticks, so an old nest can become huge. The chicks stay in the nest until they are strong enough to fly.

How do eagles see so well?
The text doesn't say, but eagles have very large, sharp eyes that can spot small animals from far away.

Teeth are covered with enamel, the hardest material in the body. Enamel cannot grow back once it is worn away, so it is important to brush twice a day. Sugary food feeds bacteria in the mouth, and these produce acid that eats into the enamel.

Why can bacteria harm the enamel?
They feed on sugar and produce an acid that eats into the enamel.

A tsunami is a series of very long waves. In deep water the waves are low but fast. When they reach the shallow water near the coast, they slow down and rise into a tall wall of water.

What most often sets off a tsunami?
The text doesn't say, but an earthquake under the sea is the most common cause of a tsunami.

Sweat helps the body cool down. When sweat dries on the skin, it takes some heat away with it. On humid days, sweat dries slowly, so you can feel hotter than on a dry day with the same temperature.

Why do humid days feel hotter?
Sweat dries slowly in humid air, so it takes away less heat.

Ice floats on water because it is lighter for its size than liquid water. When water freezes, its tiny parts arrange themselves in a pattern with gaps between them. That is why a lake freezes from the top and fish can live in the water under the ice.

Why can fish live under a frozen lake?
Ice floats, so the lake freezes from the top and the water below stays liquid.

A mirror shows you your picture because its smooth, shiny surface sends light back in an orderly way. A rough wall also sends light back, but in all directions, so you cannot see a picture in it. That is the main difference between a mirror and a wall.

Why can you not see a picture of yourself on a rough wall?
A rough wall sends the light back in all directions instead of in an orderly way.

Our class watched a short film about rockets. The narrator said that a rocket must burn a lot of fuel in the first few minutes to leave the ground. After that, it glides smoothly through the empty space above the air.

What pulls rockets and everything else back toward the ground?
The text doesn't say, but gravity pulls everything toward Earth.

Fireflies make light inside their bodies with a chemical reaction, and almost none of the energy is lost as heat. This is why the glow feels cool. Each kind of firefly flashes in its own pattern so that partners of the same kind can find one another.

Why do different fireflies flash in different patterns?
Each kind has its own pattern so that partners of the same kind can find each other.

Penguins cannot fly, but they are very good swimmers. Their wings have become flippers, and they move through the water almost as if they were flying. A thick layer of fat and tight feathers keeps them warm in icy seas.

What have a penguin's wings become?
They have become flippers.

Meerkats live in groups in the deserts of southern Africa. While most of the group looks for food, one meerkat stands guard on a rock or a mound and watches the sky. If it sees danger, it barks, and everyone dives into the nearest burrow.

What does a guard meerkat do when it sees danger?
It barks, and the others dive into the nearest burrow.

Bees live in colonies with one queen, thousands of workers and some males called drones. The queen lays eggs. Workers clean the hive, make honey and guard the entrance. A queen may live for several years, but a worker lives only a few weeks in summer.

What is the queen bee's job?
She lays the eggs.

When a cyclone comes towards the coast, the weather office gives warnings, and fishermen are asked to stay in harbour. Schools may close, and people move from low areas to shelters. After the storm, volunteers help clear roads and give out food.

What is the calm centre of a cyclone called?
The text doesn't say, but the calm centre of a cyclone is called the eye.

Our neighbour keeps hens in a bamboo coop. Each morning she lets them out to scratch in the yard, and at dusk they walk back in by themselves. She closes the door at night so that foxes and stray dogs cannot get in.

Why does the neighbour close the coop door at night?
So that foxes and stray dogs cannot get in.

The summer was hotter than usual in our town. The market closed early on several afternoons, and the schools shifted their classes to the morning. By June, the river was so low that the stepping stones in the middle were all visible.

What was the highest temperature in the town that summer?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the exact number. The local weather office would have the records.

A stethoscope helps a doctor listen to the sounds inside the chest. The doctor places the round end on the skin and listens through the ear tubes. A steady lub-dub tells the doctor the heart is beating regularly.

What does a doctor use to take a person's temperature?
The text doesn't say, but a doctor uses a thermometer.

Comets are balls of ice and dust that travel around the Sun on long paths. When one comes close to the Sun, the ice starts to turn to gas and forms a glowing tail. The tail always points away from the Sun, no matter which way the comet is moving.

Which way does a comet's tail point?
It always points away from the Sun.

An ant colony works without a boss giving orders. Worker ants leave a scent trail when they find food, and other ants follow it and add their own scent. The more ants that follow a trail, the stronger the smell gets, so the best paths are used by the most ants.

How do other ants find the food that one ant has found?
They follow the scent trail the first ant leaves behind.

A dam holds back a river and makes a large lake behind it. The water stored there can be sent through pipes to turn machines that make electricity, or let out slowly to fields in the dry season. It also helps to reduce floods downstream.

What can the water stored behind a dam be used for?
It can make electricity, water fields in the dry season and help reduce floods.

The mountain trail near our town was closed for a week after a landslide. The rain had soaked into the slope until the soil became too heavy to stay in place. A team checked the path before opening it again. Many hikers use it on weekends, and some local families sell snacks near the start.

What is a landslide?
The text doesn't say, but a landslide is a mass of soil and rock sliding down a slope.

In a hydroelectric plant, falling water spins turbines. The higher the water falls from, the more power it can make. Such plants make no smoke, but the dam they need can change a river and the land around it.

Is hydroelectric power a renewable source of energy?
The text doesn't say, but yes, it is renewable, because rain keeps refilling the rivers.

The neighbourhood association placed a water cooler outside the community hall for all passers-by. A volunteer fills it each morning, and a small tin cup hangs from a chain. In summer, the cooler is often empty by the afternoon. Many people stop there on the way back from the market.

Who pays for the cooler?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who pays for it. The neighbourhood association could tell you.

The weather office measures wind with a cup anemometer, a pole with three small cups that spin in the wind. The faster the wind, the faster the cups spin. A counter turns the number of spins into the wind speed. The reading is written in a register each day and sent to the main office.

What instrument measures temperature?
The text doesn't say, but a thermometer measures temperature.

Notice: the electricity will be cut on Tuesday between ten and one so that the line can be repaired. People are asked to charge phones and lamps in advance. The supply will return once the work is done. Shops on the main road have said they will open as usual.

Will the work finish on time?
The text doesn't say, and I can't know that. The electricity office could tell you if there is a delay.

On Sunday we found a large beehive hanging from the branch of the mango tree. Dad told us to stay away from it and called the forest office. A man in a white suit came in the evening and moved the bees carefully into a wooden box.

What was the name of the man who moved the bees?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know his name. The forest office would have a record of who came.

Some plants catch insects. The pitcher plant has a deep, slippery cup with a pool of juice at the bottom. An insect slides in, cannot climb out, and is slowly broken down by the juice. The plant uses the food to make up for poor soil.

Why does the pitcher plant catch insects?
The insects give it food that makes up for the poor soil it grows in.

Sea turtles return to the beach where they were born to lay their eggs. A mother digs a hole in the sand, lays her eggs and covers them before going back to the sea. The warmth of the sand decides how fast the eggs grow, and the babies hatch at night.

When do the baby sea turtles hatch?
They hatch at night.

Muscles can only pull, not push. That is why they work in pairs. When you bend your arm, the muscle on the front of your upper arm gets shorter, and the one at the back relaxes. To straighten your arm, the roles are swapped.

Why do muscles work in pairs?
Muscles can only pull, so one muscle pulls one way and its partner pulls back the other way.

Our PE teacher asks us to stretch for five minutes before every sports class. He says warm muscles get hurt less often than cold ones. This week we practised relay races, and the girls' team won two out of three.

What is the PE teacher's favourite sport?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know what his favourite sport is. You could ask him.

Our village well used to dry up every April. Last year, the school built a pit near the playground that collects rainwater and lets it sink into the ground. By this April, the well still had water, and the villagers hope the pit keeps helping.

What did the school build to help the village well?
It built a pit that collects rainwater and lets it sink into the ground.

The school canteen uses peels and tea leaves to feed a worm bin. Each week, students turn the bin over and check that it is damp but not wet. The dark liquid that collects at the bottom is diluted and poured on the garden beds.

What is done with the dark liquid from the worm bin?
It is diluted and poured on the garden beds.

A power cut in our street lasted until midnight, and we sat on the roof watching the stars. Without street lamps, the sky was darker than usual, and the Milky Way showed as a faint band. My little sister fell asleep on a rug before the lights came back.

What time did the little sister fall asleep?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the exact time. Her family would remember, so you could ask them.

An eclipse of the Sun will be visible from parts of India later this year, according to the newspaper. The article says you should never look at it without special glasses. Many schools will hold a viewing event in the playground.

Which school will hold the biggest viewing event?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know that. Your local education office or school notices may have details.

Rice grows best in fields that are flooded with a few centimetres of water. The water keeps weeds down and gives the young plants the water they need. Before harvest, farmers drain the field so that the grain can dry and the ground becomes firm.

Why do farmers drain the rice field before harvest?
So the grain can dry and the ground becomes firm.

On 12 July the village got a heavy shower that lasted most of the afternoon. The fields were soaked, and the stream behind the school rose and covered the lower path. By evening the water had gone down again.

How many millimetres of rain fell on 12 July?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the amount. The local weather office may have a record.

Volcanoes form where hot melted rock, called magma, finds a way to the surface. Once it flows out it is called lava. When lava cools it hardens into new rock, and after many eruptions the layers can pile up into a tall mountain with a bowl-shaped opening at the top.

What is melted rock called after it flows out of a volcano?
It is called lava.

Starfish have no brain, but they can sense light and touch with their arms. If a starfish loses an arm, it can often grow a new one. They move on hundreds of tiny tube feet on the underside of their arms, which also help them pull open shellfish.

What do starfish use to move?
They use many tiny tube feet on the underside of their arms.

A cricket makes its song by rubbing one wing against the other. Only males sing. The song calls to females and warns other males to stay away. A cricket sings faster on warmer evenings and more slowly when it is cool. You can often hear them in the grass around a house after the rains.

Which crickets sing?
Only the males sing.

An earthquake is the shaking of the ground when rocks deep inside Earth suddenly slip along a crack called a fault. The shaking spreads out in waves from the place where the slip began. Buildings made with strong frames and flexible joints are less likely to fall.

What is a fault?
It is a crack in the rocks deep inside Earth, along which the rocks can slip.

The fishermen of our town go out before dawn and return by noon. The catch is sold on the beach, where traders wait with ice boxes. When the sea is rough, the boats stay on the sand, and many families have to wait for better days.

How much money do the fishermen earn in a week?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know their earnings. You could ask a local fishermen's group or a trader.

A food chain shows who eats whom. Grass is eaten by a grasshopper, the grasshopper by a frog, the frog by a snake, and the snake by an eagle. If any link disappears, the animals above and below it are affected.

What eats the frog in this food chain?
A snake eats the frog.

The skin is the largest organ of the body. It keeps out germs, holds in water and lets us feel heat, cold and touch. Sunlight helps the skin make a substance the body needs, but too much sun can burn it.

How many senses do people usually count?
The text doesn't say, but people usually count five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

The peacock spreads its tail feathers to attract a mate. Each feather has a bright eye-shaped spot, and when the bird shakes them, they make a soft rustling sound. After the mating season, the long feathers fall off and grow back the next year.

What is a female peacock called?
The text doesn't say, but a female peacock is called a peahen.

Archaeologists digging near the river bank found pieces of old clay pots. Some had simple patterns pressed into them with a stick. The pieces were carefully washed, numbered and put in trays to be studied later at the university.

How old are the clay pots?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know their age. The university team can probably tell you after testing them.

Squirrels bury nuts in many different places in autumn. They find most of them again in winter by smell and memory. The ones they forget sometimes sprout into new trees, so squirrels help forests spread. On a winter morning you can see them digging in the leaves with their front paws.

How do squirrels help forests spread?
The nuts they forget to dig up sometimes sprout into new trees.

The village dog, a brown one with a torn ear, has been following the school bus every morning for a month. The children give him a piece of roti at the gate. The headmaster has asked students not to feed him inside the school grounds.

How old is the dog?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know his age. A vet could estimate it if someone takes him for a check-up.

A hand pump in the village school yard pulls water up from a borehole. Children take turns working the handle, and the water is clean and cool even in summer. Because the water comes from deep underground, it is not warmed by the sun.

Is water made of hydrogen and oxygen?
The text doesn't say, but yes, a water molecule is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

When you hold your breath, a part of your brain keeps watching the amount of waste gas in your blood. As it builds up, the urge to breathe grows stronger, until you have to take a breath. This is why it is hard to hold your breath for very long.

What makes the urge to breathe stronger?
The waste gas that builds up in the blood.

Mosquito eggs are laid on still water. Within days the eggs hatch into wigglers that hang under the surface and breathe through a small tube. This is why emptying buckets and flower pots every few days helps stop mosquitoes from breeding.

Why does emptying buckets help stop mosquitoes?
Mosquito eggs need still water, so removing it stops the wigglers from growing.

The Sun is a star, and all the planets of the Solar System travel around it. The ones closer to the Sun are rocky, and the ones far away are large worlds made mostly of gas and ice. The journey of each planet around the Sun is called its orbit.

How many planets are in the Solar System?
The text doesn't say, but there are eight planets in the Solar System.

A cuckoo does not build a nest. The female lays an egg in another bird's nest, and the foster parents feed the chick as if it were their own. The cuckoo chick often hatches first and may push the other eggs out.

Who feeds a cuckoo chick?
The foster parents, the owners of the nest, feed it.

Thick fog on the hills near our camp meant we could not see the valley at breakfast. By ten the fog had thinned, and a pair of eagles was circling above the trees. Our guide said they like to ride the warm air that rises from the slopes.

Why do eagles circle above the slopes?
They ride the warm air that rises from the slopes.

Roses are often pruned in winter. The gardener cuts away the dead and weak stems so that the plant can use its energy to grow strong new shoots. By spring the bush is full of fresh leaves and soon after, flowers.

Which part of a flower becomes the fruit?
The text doesn't say, but the ovary of the flower becomes the fruit.

The Moon does not make its own light. It shines because it reflects sunlight, and a full Moon is bright enough to cast shadows on a clear night. When Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, a lunar eclipse can happen.

Which is bigger, the Moon or Earth?
The text doesn't say, but Earth is bigger than the Moon.

Giraffes have the same number of neck bones as people, just seven, but each bone is very long. Their tall bodies let them reach leaves at the top of trees that other animals cannot reach. A giraffe's heart is strong to push blood up its long neck.

How many neck bones does a giraffe have?
It has seven, the same number as people.

The Indian rhinoceros has a single horn and thick skin that folds like armour. It likes to wallow in muddy water to stay cool. Most of the wild ones live in a few protected grasslands in the north-east, where rangers keep a close watch.

Does a rhinoceros eat plants or meat?
The text doesn't say, but a rhinoceros eats plants.

In the dry season, tanker trucks bring water to some neighbourhoods in the city. Families fill buckets and drums and store them with lids on. A residents' group takes turns to keep the area around the tanker tidy.

What do we call water that falls from clouds?
The text doesn't say, but water that falls from clouds is called rain.

Your sense of smell is closely tied to taste. When you chew food, smells rise from your mouth up to the back of your nose. This is why food seems to have little flavour when your nose is blocked by a cold.

Why does food seem to have little taste when you have a blocked nose?
Taste depends on smell, and a blocked nose stops the smells from being noticed.

Ducks have webbed feet that work like paddles. Their feathers are coated with oil from a gland near the tail, and the oil stops water from soaking in. A duck spends a lot of time preening to spread this oil over its feathers.

What are baby ducks called?
The text doesn't say, but baby ducks are called ducklings.

Bamboo is a grass, not a tree. Some kinds grow almost a metre in a day. The stems are hollow with solid joints, which makes them strong but light. In many places, bamboo is used for building scaffolding, baskets and furniture.

What kind of plant is bamboo?
It is a grass.

The hills around Mahabaleshwar turn a deep green in the rains, and clouds often touch the road. Our bus stopped at a viewpoint where a tea seller had a small stall. Everyone took photos, and the sun came out for a few minutes before the fog came back.

How high is the viewpoint above sea level?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the exact height. A tourist office or a map of the region may give it.

The class built paper models of the planets and hung them from the ceiling. Aarav's Saturn had a ring made from a paper plate, and Kiran's Earth had cotton clouds. The teacher said the models were not to scale, since the real distances would not fit in the school.

Whose model did the teacher like best?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which one she liked best. You could ask the teacher.

Villagers near the river dig small channels to carry water to their vegetable plots. They open one channel at a time so that each plot gets its share. In the dry months the river shrinks, and families decide together when to stop watering.

What do plants need besides water to grow?
The text doesn't say, but plants also need sunlight, air and nutrients from the soil.

On a hot day, the pavement can be much warmer than the grass next to it. Dark surfaces take in more of the Sun's heat than light ones. That is why people in hot regions often paint their houses white.

Which season is the hottest in most of India?
The text doesn't say, but summer, from about April to June, is the hottest season in most of India.

At the edge of the forest, a signboard asks visitors to take their litter home. Plastic bags can stay in the soil for years and sometimes get swallowed by animals. The forest officer says clean paths are the easiest way for everyone to help.

Which gas do plants give out that people need to breathe?
The text doesn't say, but plants give out oxygen.

Your heart is a muscle about the size of your fist. It squeezes about once every second at rest, pushing blood through tubes called vessels. The blood carries oxygen from the lungs to every part of the body and brings waste gas back to be breathed out.

What does the blood carry from the lungs to the body?
It carries oxygen.

Camels can go for days without drinking, but they do not store water in their humps. The humps hold fat, which the camel uses as energy when food is scarce. When the fat is used, the hump may flop over until the camel eats well again.

What do a camel's humps store?
They store fat, not water.

A ladybird eats aphids, tiny insects that suck juice out of garden plants. Gardeners are glad to see ladybirds, since they protect the plants without any spray. The bright red wings with black spots warn birds that the ladybird tastes bad.

How many wings does a ladybird usually have?
The text doesn't say, but a ladybird has four wings, two hard outer ones and two soft ones underneath.

Swifts spend almost their whole life in the air. They eat, drink and even sleep while flying, and they come down only to build nests and raise chicks. Their legs are so short that they have trouble taking off if they land on flat ground.

Do birds lay eggs?
The text doesn't say, but yes, all birds lay eggs.

Lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun, and it heats the air around it so fast that the air bursts outward. That burst is thunder. Light travels much faster than sound, so you see the flash first and hear the thunder a little later.

Why do you see lightning before you hear thunder?
Light travels much faster than sound.

When you get a small cut, tiny pieces in your blood called platelets gather at the spot and stick together. Together with a protein, they make a clot that plugs the hole. Later a scab forms, and new skin grows beneath it.

What plugs the hole in a small cut?
A clot made by platelets gathering and sticking together.

Cotton bolls burst open when they are ripe and show white, fluffy fibre around the seeds. Pickers walk through the fields and collect it by hand or by machine. The fibre is then spun into thread and woven into cloth.

Which clothing items are often made from cotton cloth?
The text doesn't say, but cotton cloth is used for shirts, sheets and towels.

Farmers in many villages plant pulses such as lentils and peas between their main crops. The roots of these plants live alongside tiny bacteria that turn nitrogen from the air into a form the soil can use. The next crop then grows better without much extra fertiliser.

Why do farmers plant pulses between their main crops?
The bacteria on pulse roots put nitrogen into the soil, so the next crop grows better.

A battery stores energy in chemicals. When you connect a torch bulb to a battery, the chemicals react and push a small electric current through the wire. After a while the chemicals are used up, and the torch grows dim.

Why does a torch grow dim after a while?
The chemicals in the battery get used up.

The ocean has tides because the Moon pulls on the water. On the side of Earth facing the Moon the sea bulges up, and there is another bulge on the opposite side. As Earth turns, most coasts see two high tides and two low tides each day.

How many high tides do most coasts see each day?
Most coasts see two high tides a day.

There was a first aid class at school on Friday. The nurse showed us how to clean a small scrape and how to hold a cold cloth on a bump. She told us that for anything serious, we should call an adult at once.

What is the nurse's name?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know her name. The school office could tell you.

In winter, some parts of Kashmir get heavy snow, and the roads over the mountain passes may be closed for days. Shops in the towns stock up on food and fuel before the first snow. Snow also adds water to rivers when it melts in spring.

At what temperature does water freeze?
The text doesn't say, but water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius.

Meena's grandfather walks in the park every morning at six. He says the cool air makes him feel fresh, and he meets his friends near the fountain. The group has been meeting for years and often shares tea from a flask.

How many kilometres does he walk each morning?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the distance. Meena could ask her grandfather.

A mother cat carries her kittens one by one by the scruff of their necks to a new hiding place. Kittens are born with their eyes closed and open them after about a week. They drink their mother's milk for several weeks.

Is a cat a mammal, a bird or a reptile?
The text doesn't say, but a cat is a mammal, which is why the kittens drink milk.

The International Space Station circles Earth about sixteen times a day. The crew sees sixteen sunrises and sunsets in that time. They exercise every day to keep their muscles from becoming weak in the floating conditions.

Besides the space station, what is the name of Earth's natural satellite?
The text doesn't say, but Earth's natural satellite is the Moon.

Cactus plants store water in their thick stems. Their leaves have become sharp spines, which lose much less water than flat leaves would and also keep animals away. The stem does the job of making food from sunlight. Many kinds grow in dry areas where it rains only a few times in a year.

What have a cactus's leaves become?
They have become sharp spines.

When you rub your hands together quickly, they feel warm. The rubbing, called friction, turns the energy of your moving hands into heat. Brakes on a bicycle work in a similar way, using friction to slow the wheel and making the rim a little warm.

What is the rubbing between your hands called?
It is called friction.

The Moon has no air, so there is no wind or weather on its surface. Footprints left there by visiting astronauts stay in the dust almost unchanged. Only tiny space rocks hitting the ground and the slow effect of sunlight can wear them away over a very long time.

Why do footprints on the Moon last so long?
There is no air, wind or weather there, so nothing disturbs the dust.

Seawater is salty because rivers carry tiny amounts of salt from rocks into the sea. When sea water evaporates in the sun, the water goes into the air and the salt stays behind. People in coastal areas collect salt by letting sea water dry in shallow pans.

How do people on the coast collect salt?
They let sea water dry in shallow pans, which leaves the salt behind.

Our school garden has a small compost heap in the corner. We add vegetable peels, dry leaves and tea leaves, but no cooked food. Worms and tiny creatures slowly turn the pile into dark, crumbly soil that we use for the flower beds in spring.

What do students add to the compost heap?
They add vegetable peels, dry leaves and tea leaves, but no cooked food.

A blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived, yet it eats some of the smallest. It swallows huge mouthfuls of water and pushes the water out through plates in its mouth, trapping tiny shrimp-like animals called krill. One whale may eat millions of krill in a day.

What does a blue whale eat?
It eats tiny shrimp-like animals called krill.

Elephants live in family groups led by the oldest female. She remembers where water holes are, even those that are visited only in dry years. Young males leave the group when they grow up, while the females stay with their mothers and aunts for life.

Who leads an elephant family group?
The oldest female leads it.

Soil is made from broken rock mixed with dead plants and animals. Earthworms help by pulling leaves down into the ground and by making tunnels that let air and water in. A handful of healthy soil can hold billions of tiny living things.

How do earthworms help the soil?
They pull leaves down and dig tunnels that let in air and water.

When white light passes through a glass prism, it spreads into a band of colours. Red is bent the least and violet the most. A rainbow is nature's version of this, with raindrops doing the job of the prism.

What are the seven colours of the rainbow?
The text doesn't say, but they are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

A magnifying glass is a lens that is thicker in the middle than at the edges. It bends the light that passes through it, so that an object looks larger. If you hold one in the sun, the lens can gather light into a bright, hot point, so never point it at anyone's eyes.

What shape is a magnifying glass lens?
It is thicker in the middle than at the edges.

Shells found high in the mountains tell scientists that the land there was once under the sea. Over millions of years, the movement of Earth's crust pushed the seabed upward. Fossils of fish and sea plants are sometimes found in the same layers of rock.

What do shells found on mountains tell scientists?
They show the land was once under the sea.

Sand on a beach is made of tiny pieces of rock and shell. Waves and wind break bigger stones into smaller and smaller bits over thousands of years. On some islands the sand is white because it comes mostly from the shells of sea animals.

Why is the sand white on some islands?
It comes mostly from the shells of sea animals.

When you are cold, your body can make you shiver. The small, quick shaking of your muscles makes heat, which helps keep the inside of your body warm. Your skin may also form tiny bumps, which once helped furry animals trap warm air.

Why does shivering help when you are cold?
The quick shaking of the muscles makes heat that keeps the body warm.

Note from Meera's field diary: Today I watched a spider repair its web after the rain. It walked along the broken threads and pulled the loose ends together with its front legs. In ten minutes the web looked new again, and a small fly was already stuck in it.

What did the spider do after the rain?
It repaired its web by pulling the loose threads together, and soon caught a fly.

The class made a pinhole camera from a shoebox. They poked a tiny hole in one end and put tracing paper at the other. When they held it up to a window, a small upside-down picture of the tree outside appeared on the paper.

Why does light make the picture upside down?
The text doesn't say, but light travels in straight lines, so rays from the top of the tree cross at the hole and land at the bottom of the paper.

Astronauts on the space station seem to float because they are falling around Earth all the time, along with the station. They are not beyond Earth's pull. The station is moving so fast sideways that as it falls, it keeps missing the ground.

Why do astronauts on the space station seem to float?
They are falling around Earth together with the station, so they feel weightless.

In the early morning, a flock of parakeets lands on the neem tree outside our window. They eat the small fruits and scatter the seeds on the ground. Sometimes a crow tries to chase them away, but they come back each day.

How many parakeets are in the flock?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many there are. You could count them one morning.

Leaves look green because of a substance called chlorophyll. It takes in sunlight, which the plant uses to turn water and carbon dioxide into food. In autumn, in cool places, the green fades, and the yellow and red colours that were hidden underneath show up.

Why do leaves look green?
They contain chlorophyll, which is green.

Science Club notice: On Saturday we will visit the city lake to count the birds that spend the winter there. Please bring a notebook, a water bottle and a hat. We leave from the school gate in the morning, and the trip is open to all students from class six upwards.

How many birds will the club count at the lake?
The text doesn't say, and I can't know that before the count. You could check the club's notes after the trip.

Bats hang upside down in the old fort at the edge of town. At sunset, hundreds fly out together to feed. Some people are afraid of them, but they eat a great many insects, and they do not harm humans if left alone.

Are bats birds or mammals?
The text doesn't say, but bats are mammals, and they are the only mammals that can truly fly.

A coal power station burns coal to heat water into steam. The steam turns a large wheel called a turbine, which drives a generator. It makes a lot of electricity, but burning coal also puts smoke and gases into the air.

Is coal a renewable or a non-renewable fuel?
The text doesn't say, but coal is a non-renewable fuel, because it took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced quickly.

Frogs begin life in water as tadpoles. A tadpole breathes with gills and swims with a tail. Over several weeks it grows back legs, then front legs, and its tail slowly shrinks. At the end it has lungs and can climb out onto land.

How does a young frog breathe while it is a tadpole?
It breathes with gills.

Moss does not have true roots. It takes in water straight through its leaves and uses tiny threads to hold on to rocks, bark or soil. This is why moss grows best in damp, shady places and turns dry and brown when the weather is hot.

Why does moss grow best in damp places?
It takes in water through its leaves instead of through roots, so it needs a damp spot.

Nature club notice: Next Sunday we will walk along the canal path to look for dragonflies and damselflies. Wear closed shoes, since the bank can be muddy. Hand lenses will be shared, two students to each lens. We meet at the library steps at half past six and will be back before lunch.

How will the hand lenses be shared?
Two students will share each lens.

Jellyfish have no brain, no heart and no bones. Their bodies are mostly water. They drift with the current and use stinging cells on their arms to catch small fish. Some kinds of jellyfish can sting people, so beachgoers are told to stay away from them.

What do jellyfish use to catch small fish?
They use the stinging cells on their arms.

Octopuses are clever. They can open jars, solve small puzzles and squeeze through gaps no bigger than their beak, which is the only hard part of their body. They change colour in a flash to match rocks or sand when they feel in danger.

What is the only hard part of an octopus's body?
It is the beak.

The Himalayas are still growing. Two huge pieces of Earth's crust, one carrying India, are pushing into each other, and the land between them is slowly forced upward. The mountains rise by a few millimetres each year, but erosion also wears them down.

What is pushing the Himalayas upward?
Two huge pieces of Earth's crust pushing into each other.

Kangaroos carry their young in a pouch on the mother's belly. A newborn is tiny and climbs into the pouch by itself. It stays inside for months, drinking milk, and later it hops out for short trips while staying close to its mother.

Which continent do kangaroos come from?
The text doesn't say, but kangaroos come from Australia.

The Thar Desert in western India gets very little rain, but life still finds a way. Plants like the khejri tree have deep roots that reach water far below the sand. Camels, lizards and desert foxes have all learned to live on small amounts of water.

How can the khejri tree survive in the Thar Desert?
Its deep roots reach water far below the sand.

In our balcony garden, the tomato plants started flowering in March. We tie the stems to sticks and water them every evening. A few small green tomatoes have already appeared, and my father says he will make chutney with the first ripe ones.

When will the first tomatoes ripen?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know exactly when they will ripen. It depends on the weather and the variety, so the seed packet may give a rough time.

The geography teacher showed the class a rock collection. Each piece had a small label with its name and the place where it was found. A black, shiny piece caught everyone's eye, and it turned out to be a piece of obsidian from a volcano.

Where exactly did the obsidian come from?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the exact place. The label on the rock, or the teacher, should have it.

A potato plant makes its tubers under the ground. Farmers heap soil around the stems so the potatoes stay covered and do not turn green. After the leaves die back, the potatoes are dug up and left to dry.

Is a potato a root or a fruit?
The text doesn't say, but a potato is a tuber, the swollen underground part of a stem, and we eat it as a vegetable.

Many birds rest at sunset in the old banyan tree by the village well. The villagers say it is the oldest tree in the village, and a small shrine stands among its roots. Children often play hide-and-seek around the thick trunks.

Do birds usually sleep during the day or at night?
The text doesn't say, but most birds sleep at night.

The Ganga starts as a small stream from a glacier high in the mountains and grows as many other streams join it. It crosses the plains slowly and ends in a huge delta. Millions of people live along its banks.

Into which sea does the Ganga flow?
The text doesn't say, but the Ganga flows into the Bay of Bengal.

Stars look as if they twinkle because their light has to pass through moving layers of air before it reaches your eyes. The air bends the light a little, and the bending keeps changing. Planets usually shine with a steadier light than stars.

What makes starlight twinkle?
The light is bent by moving layers of air on its way to your eyes.

Turmeric is a plant whose underground stems, called rhizomes, are dried and ground into yellow powder. Farmers dig up the rhizomes after the leaves turn yellow and dry. Many Indian kitchens use it every day in cooking.

Do roots usually grow above or below the ground?
The text doesn't say, but roots usually grow below the ground.

Last week our class tested which materials soak up water. We put a drop on cotton cloth, paper and plastic. The cloth soaked it up in five seconds, the paper in twenty, and the drop stayed on top of the plastic. Mr Verma said this is why raincoats are made of plastic-like material.

Which material soaked up the drop fastest?
The cotton cloth soaked it up fastest, in five seconds.

Salt makes water heavier. It is easier to float in the Dead Sea than in a swimming pool, because the water there is far saltier. Visitors can lie on the surface and read a book without sinking.

Is the Dead Sea a sea or a lake?
The text doesn't say, but the Dead Sea is actually a salt lake.

The Arctic tern makes one of the longest journeys of any bird. It breeds near the North Pole in summer, then flies to the seas around Antarctica for the other summer. Because it chases daylight in both places, it sees more sunshine than almost any other animal.

Why does the Arctic tern see so much sunshine?
It travels between the north and the south to follow the summer, so it gets daylight in both places.

A school trip took the class to the aquarium in the city. They saw sharks, rays and a tank full of sea horses. The guide let them touch a smooth sea star and told them to wash their hands afterwards.

Which animal did the guide like most?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the guide's favourite. You could ask the aquarium staff.

The railway bridge near the town of Pamban crosses a narrow stretch of sea. A section lifts to let boats pass underneath. Passengers often stand at the door of the carriage to look at the water. Many tourists take the trip only for this short, slow crossing.

Question: What is a bridge for?
The text doesn't say, but a bridge lets people and vehicles cross water, a road or a valley.

The Nilgiri hills are covered with green tea gardens in neat rows. The air is cooler than on the plains, and mist often settles in the valleys. Pickers carry large baskets and work in groups early in the day. Tea from these slopes is packed in the nearby town.

What do the pickers carry?
They carry large baskets.

The market in Madurai is busy at dawn, with farmers unloading baskets of jasmine and vegetables. Cooks from nearby restaurants arrive early to pick the freshest ones. A small stall sells hot idlis wrapped in banana leaves. By eight o'clock the lanes are too crowded for carts.

What is an idli made from?
The text doesn't say, but idli is made from a batter of rice and black lentils, which is steamed.

The shadow puppet show in Kerala is performed in front of a temple at night. Puppeteers use flat figures made of leather and a bright oil lamp behind a cloth screen. The stories come from an ancient epic poem. Crowds sit on the ground and watch until the early morning.

Question: What is a puppet?
The text doesn't say, but a puppet is a figure that a person moves with strings, rods or hands.

The overnight train from Jodhpur arrives in Delhi before sunrise. Passengers have a choice of seats or sleeping berths. The tea seller walks through the carriages at every stop. A small pantry car near the middle serves simple meals, and the berths have clean white sheets.

At what time does the train leave Jodhpur?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the departure time. The railway enquiry office or the official timetable would tell you.

The lighthouse keeper's log at Cape Merin shows that on one stormy night in 1934, the keeper rang the fog bell for eleven hours without a break. Three fishing boats found their way home by the sound. The bell is still on display at the base of the tower.

How did three fishing boats find their way home?
They followed the sound of the fog bell that the keeper rang.

The old toy train in Darjeeling climbs through tea gardens at a slow walking pace. It stops for twenty minutes at one station so that passengers can take photographs and have tea. A round trip takes about two hours and tickets sell out quickly in the busy season.

Question: How long does a round trip take?
A round trip takes about two hours.

The bus from Dehradun to Mussoorie takes about ninety minutes. It has narrow seats and climbs a winding road with many turns. Passengers who get queasy are advised to sit near the front. It leaves from the main stand every half hour in the morning.

What does a bus run on?
The text doesn't say, but most buses run on diesel, petrol or gas.
