Question: How should papers be sorted?
They are sorted by date first and then by subject.

Instruction for the geometry box: place a ruler along the line you wish to draw and hold it with one hand. Hold the pencil with the other hand and draw along the edge. To draw a circle, put the needle of the compass on the point and turn the pencil end around. Keep the pencil sharp.

How do you draw a circle?
You put the compass needle on the centre point and turn the pencil end around it.

Under-14 cricket trial: bring your cap, shoes and a water bottle. Coach Bhatt will watch batting first, then bowling and fielding. Selected players will get a call by evening. Trials start at 6 a.m. at the municipal ground. No parents on the field, please.

How many players will be selected?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many players will be picked. Coach Bhatt will know the number.

Dal tadka method: boil washed toor dal with turmeric and salt until it turns soft and mushy. In a small pan, heat ghee and add cumin, garlic slices and a dried red chilli. When the garlic turns light brown, pour this tempering over the dal and stir. Serve hot with rice or roti.

Q: Is dal a good source of protein?
The text doesn't say, but yes, lentils like dal are a good source of plant protein.

Yoga for beginners at school: sit on a mat with your legs crossed and your back straight. Close your eyes and breathe in slowly through the nose for four counts, then out through the mouth. Do this for one minute. After that, stretch your arms up and bend gently to each side.

Question: Is a yoga mat usually hard or soft?
The text doesn't say, but a yoga mat is usually thin and slightly soft so that it grips the floor and cushions the body.

Sports day sign-up: students who want to enter the long jump must give their names to Mr. Verma by Thursday. Each student can enter at most two events. A student who enters a race must also be present at the practice session on Friday after school.

How many events can one student enter?
A student can enter at most two events.

Ludo for four: each player picks a colour and keeps four tokens in their home square. A token leaves home only when its player rolls a six. After a six, you roll again. If your token lands on a square holding an opponent's token, that token goes back home. The first to bring all four tokens to the centre wins.

What do you need to roll to move a token out of home?
You need to roll a six.

Homework diary rule: every student writes the date, subject and task in the diary before leaving the class. Parents sign the diary each evening. The class teacher checks signatures on Monday mornings. A student who forgets the diary writes a note at the back of the notebook instead.

Q: Why do people keep a diary or a planner?
The text doesn't say, but people keep one to remember tasks and dates so they do not forget things.

School trip rules: stay with your group at all times and tell the teacher if you need to go to the washroom. Do not eat anything from strangers. Throw rubbish only in bins. Keep the money your parents gave you in an inner pocket. Be back at the bus by the time written on your sheet.

Question: What should you do if you need to go to the washroom?
You should tell the teacher.

Packing for a two-day trip: lay out your clothes on the bed before packing, and choose two shirts, two pairs of pants and one jacket. Roll the clothes to save space. Keep shoes in a separate bag. Put a small towel, toothbrush and comb in a pouch. Keep your ticket in the front pocket.

How do you save space with clothes?
You roll the clothes to save space in the bag.

Joining the school football team: trials are on Saturday at 7 a.m. Wear your sports shoes and carry water. The coach will test running, passing and shooting. A list of selected players will be pinned on the notice board on Monday.

Where will the list of selected players be put up?
It will be pinned on the notice board on Monday.

Rules of hockey for school teams: each team has eleven players, including a goalkeeper. Players may use only the flat side of the stick. A goal counts only if the ball is hit inside the circle in front of the goal. A match has two halves of thirty-five minutes.

Q: How long is each half?
Each half is thirty-five minutes long.

Spelling practice method: look at the word and say it aloud. Cover it and try to write it from memory. Check your spelling, and if you made a mistake, circle the part you missed. Write the word three times, using different coloured pens. Test yourself again the next day.

Question: What do you do if you made a mistake in spelling?
You circle the part you missed and then write the word three times in different coloured pens.

Making a paper aeroplane that flies far: fold the sheet in half lengthwise and unfold it. Fold the top corners to the middle line. Fold those edges again to the middle. Fold the plane in half and make wings by folding each side down. Launch it with a gentle push, slightly upward.

How should you launch the plane?
Launch it with a gentle push, slightly upward.

Egg bhurji in five steps: heat oil in a pan and fry chopped onions and green chillies. Add chopped tomato and a pinch of turmeric. When the tomato softens, crack in three eggs and stir quickly. Cook for a minute until the eggs are set but still moist. Add salt and coriander at the end.

When is the salt added?
The salt is added at the end, along with the coriander.

Taking care of a pet rabbit: give it fresh grass and carrots every day, and keep a bowl of water in its cage. Clean the cage every two days. Let it play outside the cage for an hour in a safe space. Always lift it with both hands, one under its feet.

Q: How do you lift a rabbit?
You lift it with both hands, one hand under its feet.

Feeding schedule for Bruno the dog: breakfast at 7 a.m. and dinner at 7 p.m. His bowl is in the kitchen corner. Fresh water should be there at all times. The vet visit is next week. Please do not give him any human sweets.

Question: What breed is Bruno?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know what breed Bruno is. His owners could tell you.

Sabudana khichdi note: soak the sabudana in just enough water for four hours until the pearls can be pressed easily. Roast peanuts and crush them. Heat ghee, add cumin and green chillies, then the boiled potato cubes. Mix in the sabudana and peanuts and cook gently for five minutes.

How long do you soak the sabudana?
You soak the sabudana for four hours, in just enough water, until the pearls can be pressed easily.

Chore chart for the week: Anil takes out the trash on Monday and Thursday. Sunita lays the table every evening. On Saturday, both children clean their rooms before lunch. Dad will check the chart on Sunday night and give a star for each chore done.

On which days does Anil take out the trash?
Anil takes out the trash on Monday and Thursday.

Notice from the pet shop: our goldfish are available in three colours, and tanks can be delivered on request. Each tank comes with a small bag of food. We keep a record of every sale, so please bring your receipt if you need help later. Come by between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m.

Q: How many goldfish are there in the shop right now?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many goldfish are in stock. Calling or visiting the shop is the best way to check.

How to write a letter to the principal: start with your address and the date at the top. Then write 'Respected Sir' or 'Respected Madam'. State your request in two or three clear lines and thank the principal. End with 'Yours obediently' and your name and class.

Question: What does a principal do in a school?
The text doesn't say, but a principal is the head of a school who runs it and looks after its teachers and students.

Reminder for the art teacher's request: please bring old newspapers, a glue stick and scissors on Monday. We will make paper bags. Each bag should be at least the size of a notebook. We will give the bags to the local grocery shop, and the best bags will be shown on the board.

What will the class do with the finished bags?
They will give the bags to the local grocery shop.

Reading week plan: from Monday, every class spends the first twenty minutes reading a book of their choice. Students may bring their own books or borrow from the class shelf. On Friday, each student will tell the class one thing they liked about the book.

What will students do on Friday?
Each student will tell the class one thing they liked about the book.

Boiling potatoes for aloo chaat: wash the potatoes and boil them in salted water until a fork goes in easily. Drain and let them cool. Peel, cut into cubes and fry the cubes in a little oil until crisp. Sprinkle chaat masala, red chilli powder and a squeeze of lime.

Q: Which part of the potato plant do we eat?
The text doesn't say, but the part we eat is the tuber, which grows underground.

Mango lassi recipe: blend one ripe mango, a cup of chilled curd, half a cup of cold milk and two spoons of sugar until smooth. Pour into tall glasses and top with a few chopped pistachios. Serve straight away so it stays cold and frothy.

Question: Which variety of mango tastes best in this lassi?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which variety is best here. It is worth asking the fruit seller what is sweet and ripe that week.

Lemon rice leftover trick: if cooked rice is cold, sprinkle a spoon of water over it and microwave it covered for one minute. Stir once and heat again for thirty seconds. This keeps the grains soft. Never reheat rice more than once, and keep leftovers in the fridge within one hour of cooking.

Why is a spoon of water sprinkled on the cold rice?
The water keeps the grains soft when the rice is reheated.

Keeping a diary: write the date at the top and start with what happened today. Mention one thing you liked and one thing you found hard. Write at the same time every day so it becomes a habit. Keep it in a safe place.

What is a habit?
The text doesn't say, but a habit is something you do regularly, often without thinking.

Using the lift in our building: press the button once and wait. Let others come out before you enter. Children should not play with the buttons. If the lift stops, press the alarm button and stay calm. Do not try to open the doors by force.

Q: What should you do if the lift stops?
Press the alarm button and stay calm.

Sale notice at the stationery shop: notebooks are available at a special price this week. Buy ten and get one free. Pens, markers and files are in the second aisle. The shop is closed on Sundays. Please bring your own bag for the items you buy.

Question: What is the price of one notebook?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the price of one notebook. The shop staff can tell you.

Stuffed paratha tips: knead soft dough and make small balls. Roll each ball slightly, place a spoon of the potato filling in the centre and bring the edges together. Press flat and roll gently, so the filling does not come out. Cook on a hot tawa with a little ghee on each side.

How do you stop the filling from coming out?
You seal the edges over the filling and roll the paratha gently.

Word chain game: the first player says any word, such as 'table'. The next player must say a word starting with the last letter of that word, so 'egg' might follow. You cannot repeat a word that has already been said. A player who cannot think of a word within ten seconds is out.

How much time does a player get to think of a word?
A player gets ten seconds to think of a word.

Hill station bus info: the bus leaves from platform four at 6 a.m. and stops for tea at the halfway point. Passengers may put bags on the rack above. The ride is bumpy near the end. A guide from the tourist office will meet us on arrival and take us to the guesthouse.

Q: How many seats are in the bus?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many seats the bus has. The bus company can tell you.

Dice game for two: each player rolls two dice in turn. Add the two numbers together and write the total on the score sheet. After five rounds, add up all the totals. The player with the higher total wins. If the totals are tied, each player rolls once more.

Question: What happens if the totals are tied?
If the totals are tied, each player rolls once more.

Diwali clean-up checklist: sort the old clothes and give the usable ones to a charity. Wipe the shelves and fans. Hang the toran on the main door and set out diyas on the window ledge. Buy sweets from the local shop a day earlier. Keep a bucket of water near the place where crackers are lit.

Where should a bucket of water be kept?
A bucket of water should be kept near the place where crackers are lit.

Mulching vegetable beds: spread a layer of dry grass about five centimetres thick around the plants. Leave a small gap near the stems. Mulch holds water in the soil and keeps weeds from growing. Add more mulch when it thins out in a few months.

What is a weed?
The text doesn't say, but a weed is a plant that grows where it is not wanted, such as among crops.

Giving a thank-you speech: begin by thanking the guests for coming. Mention one or two people who helped you by name. Keep your speech short, around one minute. Speak slowly and look at the audience. End by wishing everyone a pleasant evening.

Q: What is an audience?
The text doesn't say, but an audience is a group of people who gather to watch or listen to something.

Cucumber raita: whisk one cup of curd until smooth. Grate half a cucumber, squeeze out the extra water and mix it into the curd. Add a pinch of roasted cumin powder and salt. Chill for ten minutes before serving with biryani or parathas.

Question: What is curd called in some other countries?
The text doesn't say, but curd is similar to what many countries call plain yogurt.

Post office basics: write the address clearly on the envelope, with the pin code at the end. Stick the correct stamps on the top right corner. Drop the letter in the red box or hand it to the counter clerk. Keep the receipt if you send a parcel.

Where do the stamps go?
The stamps go on the top right corner of the envelope.

Thandai for the festival: soak almonds, fennel seeds and poppy seeds in warm water for two hours. Grind them with a little milk into a fine paste. Mix the paste into a litre of boiled and chilled milk. Add sugar and a few strands of saffron, and serve cold. Always strain it before pouring.

What should you do before pouring the thandai?
You should strain the thandai before you pour it.

Masala chai for two: pour one cup of water and one cup of milk into a pan. Add two teaspoons of tea leaves, a small piece of crushed ginger and one cardamom pod. Bring it to a boil, then lower the heat and let it simmer for three minutes. Stir in sugar if you like. Strain into cups and serve hot.

Q: When do you add the ginger?
You add the crushed ginger at the start, together with the water, milk, tea leaves and cardamom, before the pan comes to a boil.

Throwing a frisbee: hold the disc with your thumb on top and your fingers curled underneath. Stand sideways to your partner. Bring your arm across your body and flick your wrist as you let go. Keep the disc flat so that it glides.

Question: How should the disc be kept as it flies?
The disc should be kept flat so that it glides.

Pilgrim bus instructions: board at the temple gate at 5 a.m. Your seat number is on the ticket. Carry a light bag and wear comfortable footwear. The first stop will be after two hours for breakfast. Keep the aisle clear and tell the guide if you feel unwell.

When is the first stop?
The first stop is after two hours, for breakfast.

Meeting room etiquette: book the room on the shared calendar before using it. Arrive five minutes early and switch phones to silent. Keep the table clean and take any papers with you. Switch off the lights and the projector when you leave. Report a broken chair to the front desk.

What should you switch off when you leave?
You should switch off the lights and the projector when you leave.

How to keep bread fresh: store it in a clean, dry bread box or a cloth bag. Do not keep it in the fridge, because it dries out fast. If you will not eat it within three days, freeze the slices in a bag. Toast them straight from the freezer.

Q: Where should you not keep bread?
You should not keep bread in the fridge, because it dries out fast.

Saving seeds from a chilli plant: wait until a few chillies on the plant turn fully red. Pick them and cut each one open with a knife. Scrape the seeds onto a plate and spread them in a single layer. Dry them in a shady, airy spot for a week, then store them in a paper packet.

Question: Why do chillies taste hot?
The text doesn't say, but chillies taste hot because they contain a natural chemical called capsaicin.

Building a sand castle: use damp sand, as dry sand will not hold its shape. Pack the sand into a bucket, turn it over and tap the bottom. Lift the bucket slowly. Make towers by repeating this. Dig a moat around the castle and fill it with water.

Where do people usually make sand castles?
The text doesn't say, but people usually build sand castles on a beach.

Pond cleanup day: volunteers will gather on Sunday at 7 a.m. near the temple tank. Gloves and bags will be given to everyone. Children under twelve should work with an adult. We will sort the plastic and paper into separate bags. The water from the nearby tap is only for washing hands.

How many volunteers are coming?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many volunteers will come. The organisers would have a sign-up list.

Kheer method: boil a litre of milk in a heavy pan. Add washed rice and stir often so that it does not stick. Cook until the rice is soft and the milk thickens. Add sugar, cardamom powder and chopped nuts. Serve warm or chilled.

Q: Why do you stir milk often while it boils?
The text doesn't say, but stirring often keeps the milk from sticking to the pan and burning.

Pitthu or seven stones: stack seven flat stones in a tower. One team throws a ball to knock the tower down. They then try to rebuild it while the other team throws the ball at them. If the stack is rebuilt before anyone is hit, the team wins the round.

Question: What kind of ball is used in pitthu?
The text doesn't say, but players usually use a soft rubber ball or a tennis ball so that nobody gets hurt.

Warming up for a school race: jog slowly around the field for two minutes. Do arm circles and leg swings. Take a few quick sprints of about ten steps. Drink water, and get to the start line a minute before the whistle.

What is a sprint?
The text doesn't say, but a sprint is a short run at top speed.

How to hang a picture frame: first hold the frame against the wall and mark where the top edge sits with a pencil. Measure down to the hook on the back and mark that spot too. Tap a nail in at the second mark, slanting it slightly upward. Hang the frame and check it with a small spirit level.

What do you use to check that the frame is straight?
You use a small spirit level after hanging the frame.

Magnet experiment note: Kiran tested a bar magnet with items from the classroom. It attracted pins and a few paperclips but not the eraser. She wrote the results in a table and showed them to the class. The teacher asked her to try again with a different magnet next time.

Q: How strong was Kiran's magnet?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how strong her magnet was. Kiran or her teacher could tell you.

Origami frog: start with a square sheet of green paper. Fold it in half diagonally, then unfold. Make a small triangle fold on each side to form a base. Fold the lower corners to the centre. Press the back end down and it will jump. Aarav made six of these for the table.

Question: How high can the paper frog jump?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how high it can jump. You could test it and measure it yourself.

Idli batter tips from Meena's grandmother: soak rice and urad dal separately for four hours, then grind them into a smooth paste. Mix both with salt and leave the batter in a warm corner overnight to ferment. In the morning it should have risen and look bubbly. Stir gently and steam in greased moulds for twelve minutes.

What shows that the batter has fermented?
The batter has risen and looks bubbly in the morning.

Learning to knit: make a slip knot and place it on one needle. Insert the other needle through the loop, wrap the wool around it, and pull a new loop through. Slide the old loop off. Repeat until you have twenty stitches. Count the stitches after every few rows.

How often should you count the stitches?
You should count the stitches after every few rows.

Kabaddi rules for beginners: a raider crosses into the other half, holds his breath and chants 'kabaddi' continuously. The raider tries to touch a defender and return to his own half before running out of breath. If the defenders hold him until he stops chanting, he is out.

Q: Is kabaddi a team game?
The text doesn't say, but yes, kabaddi is a team sport with two sides.

Garbage collection schedule for our lane: the van will come on Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings. Keep wet waste in the green bin and dry waste in the blue one. Do not put glass in the bins. Please tie the bags well. The new supervisor will visit homes next week.

Question: What is the supervisor's name?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the supervisor's name. The residents' office could tell you.

Reading a road map: find the compass or arrow on the map that shows north. Look at the key to learn what each colour and symbol means. Trace your route with a finger from the start to the end. Use the scale at the bottom to estimate how far each stretch is.

Which direction is opposite to north?
The text doesn't say, but the opposite of north is south.

Exam day reminders: reach the hall fifteen minutes early and carry your admit card. Bring two blue pens and a pencil, and leave bags outside. Phones are not allowed in the hall. Read the whole paper once before you begin, and use the last five minutes to check your answers.

What should you do in the last five minutes?
You should use the last five minutes to check your answers.

Sports day circular: races for Classes 3 to 5 start at 8 a.m. on the main ground. Students should come in white shoes and house colours. Water stalls will be set up near the gate. Prizes will be given at the end of the day by the chief guest. Parents may watch from the stands.

Q: Who is the chief guest?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who the chief guest is. The school office will likely announce it closer to the day.

Badminton club notice: the new batch starts on the first of the month at the school hall. Players should wear sports shoes with soft soles and bring their own rackets. Shuttlecocks will be provided by the coach. Parents must sign a consent form before the first session.

Question: What is the monthly fee for the club?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the fee. The coach or the school office can tell you.

Preparing soil for a vegetable patch: remove stones and weeds. Dig the soil to the depth of a spade and break the lumps. Mix in compost or dry cow dung. Level the patch with a rake and water it lightly. Leave it for a week before sowing.

What does a rake look like?
The text doesn't say, but a rake is a long-handled tool with a row of teeth at the end, used for levelling soil and gathering leaves.

Rules for a quiz night: there are three rounds, each with five questions. Teams write their answers on a slip and hand it in before the buzzer. A correct answer earns two points. The last question in each round is a bonus worth four points. The host's decision is final.

How many points is a bonus question worth?
A bonus question is worth four points.

Antakshari rules: split into two teams. The first team sings a song, and the other team must start their song with the last letter of the first team's final word. Each team gets thirty seconds to begin a song. A team that cannot start in time loses a point. The team with the most points after ten rounds wins.

Q: Which team won the last game?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which team won the last game. Whoever kept the score can tell you.

Making tomato soup: chop four tomatoes and one onion and boil them with garlic and a cup of water for ten minutes. Let the mixture cool and blend it until smooth. Pour it back into the pan, add a little butter and pepper, and warm it gently. Serve with toast.

Question: Why is hot soup often served in winter?
The text doesn't say, but hot soup warms the body, so many people like it on cold days.

Instructions from the landlord: the water tank will be cleaned on the first Saturday. Please store water the night before. Garbage should be left at the door only after 7 a.m. The electrician will check the wiring next month. Contact the caretaker for any other problem.

Who is the caretaker?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who the caretaker is. Your landlord or neighbours could tell you.

Growing tomatoes in a pot: fill a large pot with loose soil and make a hole for the seedling. Plant it deep, up to its first leaves. Water well and keep the pot where it gets six hours of sun. Tie the stem to a stick when it grows tall. Water every morning, but never let the soil become muddy.

How much sun should the pot get?
The pot should get about six hours of sun each day.

Library card rules: every student can borrow two books at a time for ten days. Books must be returned to the front desk, not left on tables. If a book is late, the student cannot borrow another until it is back. Lost books must be reported to Mr. Das so they can be replaced.

Q: What is a library for?
The text doesn't say, but a library is a place that keeps books and other materials so people can read or borrow them.

Rinsing lentils before cooking: place the dal in a bowl and cover it with water. Swirl it with your fingers and pour off the cloudy water. Repeat until the water is nearly clear. Remove any stones you notice. Grandma says to use the leftover water for the plants.

Question: What kind of dal did Grandma cook?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which dal she cooked. You could ask Grandma.

Kite flying contest rules: each contestant flies one kite within the marked field. Judges look at three things: how high the kite goes, how steady it stays, and how pretty it looks. Cutting another person's string is not allowed. Each flyer gets fifteen minutes in the air.

What do the judges look at?
They look at how high the kite goes, how steady it stays and how pretty it looks.

How to read a price tag: look for the big number, which is the price of one item. Small print may show the weight or size. A line through the old price means a discount, and the new price is written next to it. Check the bill at the counter to be sure you were charged the same amount.

What does a line through the old price mean?
A line through the old price means a discount, and the new price is written next to it.

Keeping the house cool in summer: close the curtains on the sunny side during the day. Open the windows in the evening when it cools. Switch off lights and fans when you leave a room. Keep a wet cloth near the open window and sit near it in the afternoon.

Q: When should windows be opened?
Windows should be opened in the evening, when it cools.

Setting up a new email account: open the sign-up page and type your first and last name. Choose a user name made of letters and numbers. Make a password with at least eight characters and write it down somewhere safe at home. Add a phone number for recovery, then read and accept the terms.

Question: Which email service is this page from?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which service the page belongs to. Check the address bar of the page you are on.

Rules of Tic Tac Toe: draw a grid of three rows and three columns. One player uses crosses and the other uses circles. Players take turns to mark an empty square. The first to get three marks in a row, across, down or diagonally, wins. If all nine squares are full without a winner, the game is a draw.

What happens if all nine squares are filled and nobody has three in a row?
The game is a draw.

Making a wind chime: tie five small bells or old keys to strings of different lengths. Tie the strings to a wooden ring or a stick. Hang the stick on a hook near a window. When the wind blows, the pieces hit each other and ring.

What makes the chime ring?
The wind makes the pieces hit each other, and that makes them ring.

Greeting card steps: fold a thick sheet of paper in half. Draw a flower on the front with a pencil, then colour it. Write a short message inside. Add a few dots of glitter glue to the petals, and let the card dry flat for ten minutes before closing it.

Q: Who is the card meant for?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who the card is for. The person making it would decide that.

Rules for a cricket quiz: each team gets a card of eight questions. A team may pass on one question and come back to it at the end. Wrong answers do not lose points. The host will stop the clock after ten minutes and count the points.

Question: How long does the quiz run?
The quiz runs for ten minutes.

Sowing coriander seeds: gently crush the seeds first so that each one splits in two. Scatter them over damp soil and cover with a thin layer of soil. Water with a sprayer every day. The seedlings should show in about a week. Cut the leaves with scissors when the plants reach about ten centimetres.

How many plants will grow in my pot?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many plants will grow in your pot. It depends on the pot size and the seeds, so you could count the seedlings once they appear.

Rules for the swimming pool: shower before getting into the water. Walk, do not run, on the wet floor. Children under ten must have an adult nearby. Do not push others or jump in the shallow end. Listen to the lifeguard's whistle, and leave the pool at once if you hear two long blasts.

How deep is the deep end?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how deep the deep end is. A sign by the pool or the staff can tell you.

Tabla practice plan: sit with the smaller drum on your right and the larger one on your left. Tap the rim of the right drum with your index finger to make a sharp sound. Practise a simple beat slowly until it is steady, and speed up only when it feels easy. Keep your wrists relaxed.

Q: Are tabla drums played with hands or sticks?
The text doesn't say, but tabla is played with the hands and fingers, not with sticks.

Making a simple mask for the school play: cut an oval from thick card and cut two holes for the eyes. Paint the card in the colour of your animal. Stick on ears made of felt. Punch a hole on each side and tie elastic through them. Check that you can see and breathe easily.

Question: What is used to hold the mask on the face?
Elastic tied through holes on each side holds the mask on.

Friendship band instructions: cut three strings of different colours, each as long as your arm. Tie them together in a knot at one end and tape that end to a table. Braid the strings tightly by crossing the right string over the middle one, then the left string over the middle one. Tie another knot at the end.

What do you do with the end you tie first?
You tape the knotted end to a table so the strings stay still while you braid.

How to revise for exams: make a list of all the topics and mark those you find difficult. Revise the hard ones first, when you are fresh. Take a five-minute break after every thirty minutes. Practise old question papers and check your answers. Sleep well the night before.

What is a revision?
The text doesn't say, but revision means going over what you have already learned so that you remember it.

Ironing a shirt safely: let an adult plug in the iron and set it to the cotton mark. Start with the collar, then the cuffs, sleeves and the body. Press and glide, do not leave the iron resting on the cloth. When you finish, switch off at the wall and let the iron cool away from children.

Q: In what order do you iron the shirt?
You iron the collar first, then the cuffs, the sleeves and finally the body of the shirt.

Besan chilla for two: mix one cup of gram flour with water to make a thin batter. Add chopped onion, tomato, green chilli, salt and a pinch of ajwain. Heat a flat pan and grease it lightly. Pour a ladle of batter and spread it thin. Cook both sides until golden spots appear.

Question: How do you know a chilla is done?
It is done when golden spots appear on both sides.

Making a collage for the class board: collect old magazines and cut out interesting pictures. Arrange them on a sheet of paper before sticking them down. Overlap the pictures to cover the white spaces. Glue each piece, press it flat and add a title at the top. Let the glue dry before you hang it on the wall.

What is a magazine?
The text doesn't say, but a magazine is a publication with articles and pictures, usually printed every week or month.

Using a public library for the first time: go to the desk and ask for a membership form. Fill it in with your name, address and age. Attach a small photo and show your school card. The librarian will give you a card number and tell you how to borrow books.

Why do libraries want your address?
The text doesn't say, but libraries ask for it to know who is borrowing a book and where to contact them.

Book club message: this month we will read the adventure novel that Kabir suggested. Please finish the first five chapters before we meet. We will talk about the main characters and the setting. Tea and biscuits will be there, as usual. See you in the reading corner.

Q: What is the name of the novel?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the novel's title. Kabir or the club organiser could tell you.

Trekking group note: we will meet at the base of the hill at 6 a.m. Wear sturdy shoes and carry a hat and one litre of water. The guide has marked the trail with orange ribbons. If the group is slow, we will turn back at the old tree. Rohan has the first aid box.

Question: How tall is the hill?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the height of the hill. The guide or a local map should show it.

Packing a school bag at night: check tomorrow's timetable first. Put in the books and notebooks for those subjects, with the heaviest books closest to your back. Add your water bottle, tiffin and pencil box. Hang your uniform where you can see it, so you are not rushing in the morning.

Why should heavy books be close to your back?
The text doesn't say, but keeping heavy books close to your back puts less strain on your shoulders and back.

Making compost at home: use a bucket with small holes in the base. Add vegetable peels and dry leaves in layers. Keep the heap damp but not wet. Turn it with a stick once a week. In about two months you will have dark, crumbly compost for your plants.

What do worms do in garden soil?
The text doesn't say, but earthworms loosen the soil and help break down dead plant material, which makes the soil richer.

Metro rules for riders: tap your card on the reader before entering the gate and again when leaving. Stand behind the yellow line on the platform. Let passengers get off before you step in. Seats near the doors are kept for older people, pregnant women and anyone who is unwell. Eating is not allowed inside the train.

Q: What time does the last train leave?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know when the last train leaves. The station display or the official timetable will show it.

Mosquito-free evenings: close the windows before sunset and empty any water that has collected in buckets or flower pots. Wear light, long-sleeved clothes outside. Keep a clean cloth to wipe the water cooler tray every week. The residents' committee will meet on Sunday to discuss further steps.

Question: How many families live in the building?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many families live there. The residents' committee would have the number.

Making a pinwheel: cut a square of paper and draw lines from each corner almost to the centre. Fold every second corner to the middle and pin it in place with a pushpin. Attach the pin to a pencil with an eraser end. Blow on the pinwheel to see it spin.

What do you do after folding the corners to the middle?
You pin them in place with a pushpin, then attach it to a pencil.

Class group update: tomorrow's maths test will cover chapters four and five. Please revise the practice questions at the end of each chapter. Mr. Khan will let the test last forty minutes. Bring a geometry box, and do not forget your rough notebook. Good luck, everyone!

How many marks is the test out of?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the total marks. Your teacher, Mr. Khan, can tell you.

Notice for Class 5 parents: the annual day rehearsal will be on Wednesday from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. in the auditorium. Children should wear their house T-shirt and carry water. The school bus will leave at 4.30 p.m. as usual. Parents who wish to volunteer for costumes should meet Ms. Kapoor.

Q: Who should parents meet to help with costumes?
They should meet Ms. Kapoor.

Repotting a money plant: water the plant a day before so the roots slip out easily. Tilt the pot and slide the plant out with your hand on the base. Place it into a bigger pot partly filled with fresh soil. Fill the gaps with soil, press gently and water lightly. Keep it in shade for two days.

Question: Why is the plant watered a day before repotting?
The water makes it easier for the roots to slip out of the pot.

Invitation text: you are warmly invited to Tara's housewarming this Sunday at 5 p.m. Light snacks and juice will be served. There is parking inside the compound, and the lift is on your left as you enter. Please let us know by Friday if you can come.

What is Tara's phone number?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know Tara's number. You could ask the person who sent you the invitation.

Scholarship form instructions: fill the form in capital letters using a black pen. Attach one passport photo and a photocopy of the last report card. Get the form signed by your class teacher before handing it in. Late forms will not be accepted.

What must you attach to the form?
You must attach one passport photo and a photocopy of the last report card.

Cricket in the lane, house rules: use a soft ball only. One bounce off the wall counts as out. Hitting the ball into a neighbour's balcony means the batter is out and must fetch the ball politely. Each batter gets six balls, and the batter with the highest score at the end wins the round.

Q: What happens if the ball goes into a neighbour's balcony?
The batter is out and has to fetch the ball politely.

Garden club bulletin: the rose cuttings have taken root, and we are now waiting for the new leaves. The next meeting will happen in the back garden of the school. Please carry a trowel and a hat. Our thanks to the volunteers who watered the beds over the holidays.

Question: Which colour of roses are in the garden?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the colour of the roses. The garden club members could tell you.

Bathing a small dog: brush the coat first to remove loose hair. Place a mat in the tub so the dog does not slip. Wet the dog with lukewarm water, keeping it away from the ears and eyes. Use a gentle dog shampoo, rinse until the water runs clear, and dry with a towel in a warm room.

Do dogs sweat the way people do?
The text doesn't say, but dogs sweat very little, mostly through their paws, and cool down mainly by panting.

Staying safe at the beach: swim only in the area marked by flags. Do not go into the water alone. Keep your things in one place and watch them. Wear a hat and drink plenty of water. Leave the water if the waves become large.

Why does a beach have waves?
The text doesn't say, but waves are mostly made by wind blowing over the surface of the sea.

Making a rainbow with a glass of water: stand beside a sunny window and place a glass of water on the edge of a table. Put a white sheet of paper on the floor. Move the glass slowly until a band of colours falls on the paper. Do not look straight at the sun.

Q: What shouldn't you look at?
You should not look straight at the sun.

Chess basics for a first lesson: the board has sixty-four squares in alternating colours. Each player begins with sixteen pieces. The goal is to trap the opponent's king so that it cannot escape, which is called checkmate. White always makes the first move, and then players take turns.

Question: Which piece is the tallest on a typical chess set?
The text doesn't say, but the king is usually the tallest piece on a chess set.

Hosting a tea party: lay out cups, a teapot, a milk jug and a sugar bowl on a tray. Offer two kinds of snacks, one sweet and one savoury. Pour the tea only when your guests have arrived and are seated. Offer second cups without waiting to be asked.

Is tea usually a hot or a cold drink?
The text doesn't say, but tea is usually served hot, although iced tea is also made.

Science fair notice: Class 7 students must submit their project titles to Mrs. Iyer by Friday. Projects can be working models or charts, and each group may have up to three members. The fair will be held in the school hall on the second Saturday of November. Parents are welcome from 10 a.m.

Who won the fair last year?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who won last year. Ask your class teacher or check the school notice board.

Hotel check-in notes: check-in starts at 2 p.m. and check-out is by 11 a.m. Please carry one photo ID per adult. Breakfast is served in the dining hall near the lobby. The swimming pool is open until 7 p.m. For help with luggage, please press zero on the room phone.

Q: How much does a room cost per night?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the room rate. The hotel's front desk or website can give the current price.

Dumb charades for the cousins: write movie titles on slips and put them in a bowl. A player picks a slip and acts it out without speaking. The team has two minutes to guess. Pointing at objects is allowed, but mouthing words is not. Teams swap after each guess, and Neha keeps the score on a notepad.

Question: What is the first movie on the slips?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the movie titles on the slips. Whoever wrote the slips would know.

Making a kite: tie two light sticks into a cross. Cut a string around the four tips so it forms a diamond frame. Lay the frame on coloured paper, cut the paper bigger than the frame, and fold the edges over the string and glue them. Attach a tail and tie the flying string to the cross.

What does a kite need in order to fly?
The text doesn't say, but a kite needs wind blowing against it to lift it into the air.

Bird watching for beginners: go out early in the morning when birds are active. Walk slowly and quietly, and stop often to listen. Keep a small notebook to write what you see, such as colour and size. Stay at a distance and never throw things at birds or disturb their nests.

Why is early morning a good time for bird watching?
Early morning is a good time because birds are active then.

Practice room booking: music students can book the practice room for one hour at a time. Write your name in the booking sheet outside the door. Do not leave instruments in the room overnight. If you break a string, tell Mr. Dsouza so that he can order a new one.

Q: Who should you tell if a string breaks?
You should tell Mr. Dsouza so that he can order a new string.

Fruit salad tips: pick fruit that is ripe but firm, such as apple, banana and grapes. Wash everything and cut it into bite-size pieces. Squeeze a little lemon juice over the apple and banana so they do not turn brown. Mix gently and keep the bowl in the fridge until serving.

Question: Why is lemon juice squeezed over the apple and banana?
The lemon juice keeps the apple and banana from turning brown.

Learning to play the harmonium: sit cross-legged with the instrument in front of you. Pump the bellows with your left hand using slow, even strokes. Press one white key with your right hand and listen to the note. Start with the scale Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni Sa and repeat it daily for ten minutes.

Which hand pumps the bellows?
The left hand pumps the bellows, using slow and even strokes.

Keeping birds fed in summer: place a shallow bowl of clean water on a balcony railing. Change the water every morning because it gets warm and dirty quickly. Scatter a handful of millet on a flat dish. Keep the dishes in shade, and watch from a distance so the birds are not frightened.

What are birds' bodies covered with?
The text doesn't say, but birds are covered with feathers.

Library trolley rule: return a book to the shelf from where you took it, with the spine facing out. If you are not sure of the place, put it on the trolley near the door. Do not fold page corners; use a bookmark instead. Whisper if you need to talk.

Q: What should you use instead of folding page corners?
You should use a bookmark instead of folding page corners.

How we plan the family picnic: choose a park that everyone can reach easily. Each person brings one dish. Carry a mat, a ball and a bag for the waste. Meet at ten and eat at one. Leave the place clean before going home.

Question: Why do people take bags for waste to a picnic?
The text doesn't say, but people take them so they can carry their rubbish home and keep the park clean.

Folding a bedsheet: stand with a partner, each holding two corners of the sheet. Bring your corners together and fold it in half. Fold it in half again, then walk towards each other until the sheet becomes a small, neat rectangle you can stack on a shelf.

Why should a bedsheet be fully dry before you fold it?
The text doesn't say, but a damp sheet that is folded and put away can smell musty and grow mould.

A note stuck on the fridge: the paneer is in the blue box on the second shelf, and the chopped onions are in the steel bowl. Please make the gravy first, then add the paneer at the end so it stays soft. The rice is already cooked. I will be back from the tuition class before dinner.

Who wrote the note?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who wrote it. You could ask the people living in the house.

Planting a mint cutting: cut a stem about the length of your hand, just under a leaf joint. Remove the lower leaves. Put the stem in a glass of water and keep it by a bright window. After about ten days, white roots appear. Move it into a pot of soil when the roots are as long as a finger.

Q: When can you move the cutting into soil?
You can move it into soil when the roots are about as long as a finger.

Making ice cream at home: whisk cold cream until it forms soft peaks. Fold in condensed milk and a few drops of vanilla. Pour the mixture into a box, cover it, and freeze overnight. Scoop it out and serve with chopped fruit.

Question: Why does ice cream melt in the sun?
The text doesn't say, but ice cream melts in the sun because heat warms it above its melting point.

Wishing someone on Eid: say 'Eid Mubarak' with a smile. You may hug the person if both are comfortable. Offer a sweet dish, such as sheer khurma. Visit neighbours and elders to greet them. Be sure to share food with those who cannot celebrate with their family.

What does 'Mubarak' mean?
The text doesn't say, but 'Mubarak' is an Arabic word that means blessed or congratulations.

Notice on the pet adoption day: puppies and kittens will be on show at the community park from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Visitors may play with the animals under the staff's supervision. Interested families must fill out a form and speak to a counsellor before taking an animal home.

What must interested families do before taking an animal home?
They must fill out a form and speak to a counsellor.

Potluck lunch sign-up: each family can bring one dish, either sweet or savoury. Write your dish on the chart by the lift. We will set the tables in the community hall at noon. Plates and glasses are there. Please label dishes that have nuts.

Q: How many families have already signed up?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many families have signed up. The chart by the lift would show it.

Student council election: anyone from Class 8 can stand for election by giving their name to Ms. Nair before Tuesday. Each candidate speaks for one minute in the assembly on Wednesday. Voting is by secret ballot on Thursday. The results will be read out on Friday morning.

Question: When will the results be read out?
The results will be read out on Friday morning.

Rules in the school canteen: stand in a single line and wait for your turn. Pay at the counter first and show the coupon to the server. Eat at the tables, not in the corridor. Put leftover food in the dustbin and keep the plates on the trolley. No one should throw food or play with water.

Where should plates be kept after the meal?
The plates should be kept on the trolley.

Making your own booklet: take four sheets of paper and fold them in half together. Staple along the folded edge twice. Draw a cover and write a title. Fill each page with a drawing and one line of writing, and read it to a friend when you are done.

What is a title?
The text doesn't say, but a title is the name of a book, story or other piece of work.

Getting rid of ants from the plant pot: sprinkle a thin line of chalk powder around the pot. Avoid overwatering because ants like damp soil. Keep the area around the pots clean and free of fallen fruit. Check the plant again after a few days.

Q: What do ants like in a plant pot?
Ants like damp soil, so you should avoid overwatering.

Waiting at a bus stop: stand in line, behind the sign. Check the number on the front of the bus before you step in. Let people get off first. Show your ticket to the conductor and hold on to the rail when the bus moves. Press the bell when your stop is next.

Question: What does a conductor do on a bus?
The text doesn't say, but a conductor checks tickets and collects fares on the bus.

Setting the dinner table: place a plate in front of each chair with the fork on the left and the spoon on the right. Put a glass above the spoon. Fold a napkin and set it on the plate. Place the water jug in the centre. Switch off the television before everyone sits down.

Where does the fork go?
The fork goes on the left of the plate.

Hide and seek rules: one player is chosen as the seeker and counts to twenty with eyes closed. Everyone else hides. After counting, the seeker calls out 'Ready or not' and starts looking. The first player found becomes the next seeker. A hidden player may run to the base and say 'Safe' to avoid being caught.

Why does the seeker close their eyes while counting?
The text doesn't say, but closing the eyes means the seeker cannot see where the others go to hide.

Making a scarecrow: tie two long sticks into a cross and push the upright one deep into the soil. Stuff an old shirt with dry straw and slip it over the cross. Tie the shirt cuffs and bottom with string. Fill a cloth bag with straw for the head and draw a face. Finish with a hat.

Q: What is the head made of?
The head is made from a cloth bag filled with straw.

Hopscotch layout: draw a ladder of ten boxes with chalk on the ground and number them from one to ten. Toss a flat stone into the first box. Hop over it and continue to ten on one foot, using two feet in side-by-side boxes. Come back, pick up the stone and then throw it to the next number.

Question: Who invented hopscotch?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who invented it. A book on traditional games might have the history.

Leaf collection project: collect different leaves from your neighbourhood, and pick only those that have fallen on the ground. Place each leaf between two sheets of newspaper and press under a heavy book for a week. Glue the dry leaves to a chart paper and write the name of the tree under each one.

Which leaves should you collect?
You should collect only leaves that have already fallen on the ground.

Walking a dog politely: keep your dog on a leash in public places. Carry a bag to pick up after your dog. Do not let the dog jump on strangers or chase cyclists. Carry water on warm days. If another dog looks nervous, give it space and walk calmly past.

Why should you carry a bag when walking the dog?
You carry a bag so that you can pick up after your dog.

Stitching a button: thread the needle and knot the end. Push the needle up through the cloth and through one hole of the button. Go down through the opposite hole and repeat five times. Wind the thread under the button and knot it at the back. Snip the extra thread.

Q: What is a button used for on a shirt?
The text doesn't say, but a button fastens a shirt by passing through a buttonhole.

Crossing the road safely: stop at the edge of the pavement and look right, left and right again. Use the zebra crossing or the footbridge if there is one. Wait until the vehicles have stopped and then walk, never run. Hold the hand of a younger child, and do not use earphones while crossing.

Question: What should you not use while crossing?
You should not use earphones while crossing.

Looking after a turtle: keep it in a tank with both water and a dry rock. Feed it small pieces of food, such as leafy greens. Clean the water often. Keep the tank in a warm spot, not in a draught, and wash your hands after touching the turtle.

Do turtles lay eggs?
The text doesn't say, but yes, turtles lay eggs, usually in sand or soil.

Simon says rules: one person is Simon and gives orders such as 'touch your nose'. Players follow an order only if it begins with the words 'Simon says'. A player who follows an order without those words is out. The last player left becomes Simon.

What does the word 'order' mean here?
The text doesn't say, but here an order means an instruction that tells someone what to do.

Switching off a ceiling fan safely: turn the regulator down to zero first and then press the switch. Wait until the blades stop on their own. Never touch the blades to stop them. If you hear a strange rattle, tell an adult so it can be checked before you use the fan again.

Q: What should you do if the fan makes a strange rattle?
Tell an adult so that the fan can be checked before anyone uses it again.

Playing kabaddi safely: warm up for five minutes before the match. Remove watches and bangles. Play on a soft ground. Tackle only by holding the legs or waist. Stop the game at once if someone is hurt.

Question: Why do players remove watches and bangles?
The text doesn't say, but removing them helps keep both the wearer and other players from getting hurt.

Arriving at the station: look at the board for the platform number of your train. Take the stairs or the lift to the platform. Find the spot where your coach will stop by looking at the coach position boards. Stay behind the line until the train stops.

How do you find where your coach will stop?
You look at the coach position boards on the platform.

Looking after a fish tank: feed the fish a small pinch of food once a day. Remove any food they have not eaten after five minutes. Change one quarter of the water each week using water left in a bucket overnight. Keep the tank out of direct sunlight.

How do fish breathe?
The text doesn't say, but fish breathe using gills, which take oxygen from the water.

Planning a birthday surprise: pick a day when the guest of honour is free and tell everyone else early. Ask each friend to bring one small snack. Decorate the room while the birthday person is out with one trusted friend. Keep the lights off, and when the door opens, everyone shouts together. Cake comes last.

Q: Who keeps the birthday person busy while the room is decorated?
One trusted friend takes the birthday person out while the others decorate the room.

How to cover a notebook: cut a sheet of brown paper a little bigger than the open notebook. Place the notebook in the middle and fold the edges over the covers. Stick the folds down with tape. Add a label with your name, class and subject on the front.

Question: What goes on the label?
The label has your name, your class and the subject.

Planting a tree on Van Mahotsav day: dig a pit about as deep as your knee. Mix some compost into the soil you dug out. Place the sapling in the centre, fill the pit and press the soil firmly. Water it and tie it to a stick if the sapling is thin.

When do you tie the sapling to a stick?
You tie it to a stick if the sapling is thin.

Writing a short email: start with a clear subject line. Greet the person by name. Say what you need in two or three sentences. Add 'Thank you' at the end and sign with your name. Read it once before sending to check spelling.

What is a subject line?
The text doesn't say, but a subject line is the short title that tells the reader what the email is about.

Tag with a twist: one player is 'it' and wears a bright scarf. When it touches someone, the scarf is handed over and the touched player becomes it. Players standing on the painted circle are safe for five seconds only. After that, they must step out and keep running.

Q: How long can a player be safe on the painted circle?
A player is safe on the painted circle for only five seconds.

Choosing fresh vegetables: pick brinjals that are shiny and firm without wrinkles. Choose okra that snaps when you bend the tip. Select tomatoes that are red all over and feel heavy. Avoid spinach with yellow leaves. Keep leafy vegetables apart from the others in your bag.

Question: How can you tell that okra is fresh?
Fresh okra snaps when you bend the tip.

Looking after your sketchbook: keep it in a flat place, away from water. Use a soft pencil for outlines and a hard one for lines. Put a sheet of tracing paper between pages if you have used pastels. Sign and date each drawing at the bottom.

What goes between the pages after using pastels?
A sheet of tracing paper goes between the pages.

Choir practice notice: all singers should meet in the music room at 3.30 p.m. on Thursday. We will practise the opening song and the harmony part. Please bring a pencil to mark your sheets. If you cannot come, tell Ms. Fernandes in advance so she can plan the groups.

Which song is the choir opening with?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know the title of the opening song. Ms. Fernandes will tell you at practice.

Note on the board at home: Auntie Rani will come tomorrow after lunch with her two children. Please keep the guest room tidy and place fresh towels there. Bring out the board games from the cupboard. Mother will make tea at four. I am leaving early for work.

Q: How old are Auntie Rani's children?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how old her children are. You could ask Auntie Rani or your mother.

Organising a class farewell: pick a date after the exams and book the school hall with the principal. Divide the work among groups, such as decorations, snacks, and the music. Ask each student to write a short note for the teacher. Clear up together afterwards and thank the staff.

Question: How should the work be divided?
The work is divided among groups, such as decorations, snacks and music.

Stretching after a run: stand with feet apart and bend forward slowly, reaching for your toes. Hold for fifteen seconds. Then stand on one leg, hold your other foot behind you and pull gently. Switch legs. Breathe slowly the whole time.

Why is it helpful to stretch after exercise?
The text doesn't say, but stretching helps your muscles relax and stay flexible.

Stamp collecting tips from the club: keep stamps in an album and handle them with tweezers. Sort them by country or by theme. Store the album flat in a dry place. Our next swap meeting will be at the community hall, and members may bring a friend.

How many stamps does the club president have?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how many stamps the president has. Asking the president would be the best way to find out.

Boarding a flight for the first time: arrive at the airport three hours early. Show your ticket and ID at the entrance, then drop your large bag at the check-in counter. Go through the security check, keeping liquids in a small bag. Look at the screens for your gate number and wait there until boarding is announced.

Q: What do you do after the security check?
You look at the screens for your gate number and wait there until boarding is announced.

How to play Pass the Parcel: sit in a circle and wrap a small gift in many layers of paper. While music plays, pass the parcel around from hand to hand. When the music stops, whoever holds the parcel unwraps one layer. The player who takes off the last layer keeps the gift.

Question: Who keeps the gift?
The player who unwraps the last layer keeps the gift.

Cleaning a steel water bottle: fill it a third full with warm water and add a drop of dish soap. Put the cap on and shake for thirty seconds. Use a long brush to scrub the bottom and neck. Rinse three times with clean water, then leave the bottle upside down on a rack to air dry overnight.

How should the bottle be dried?
The bottle should be left upside down on a rack to air dry overnight.

Message from the neighbour: I will water your tulsi pot every morning while you are away. Please leave the key under the flower pot near the gate. The watering can is in the corner. The tap near the wall has been dripping lately, so please see if it can be tightened.

How long will the family be away?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know how long the family will be away. The family who is travelling would know.

Boiling an egg: place the egg in a pan and cover it with cold water. Heat until the water bubbles, then switch off the flame and cover the pan. Wait ten minutes. Move the egg into a bowl of cold water for two minutes, then tap it on the counter and peel under the water.

Q: How long do you wait after switching off the flame?
You wait ten minutes with the pan covered.

Auto-rickshaw stand rules: wait for your turn in the queue at the stand. Tell the driver your destination before sitting. If the meter is not working, agree on the fare before you start. Keep your bag on your lap, and take your belongings when you get out.

Question: What should you do if the meter is not working?
You should agree on the fare with the driver before you start the ride.

Kitchen safety for kids: ask an adult before using the stove. Keep pot handles turned inwards. Use a dry cloth to hold hot pans. Never touch a knife unless an adult is nearby. Wipe up spills at once so that no one slips. Wash your hands before you start.

Which way should pot handles face?
Pot handles should be turned inwards.

Taking a clear photo: wipe the camera lens with a soft cloth. Hold the phone steady with both hands and tap on the thing you want in focus. Stand with the light behind you, not in front. Take two or three photos so you can pick the best one.

Why do photos come out blurry when the camera shakes?
The text doesn't say, but a shaking camera moves while it records the picture, so the image gets smeared.

Making a clay diya: roll a ball of soft clay about the size of a lemon. Press your thumb into the middle and turn it slowly while pinching the walls thinner. Pinch one edge to shape a spout for the wick. Smooth the surface with wet fingers and leave it in the sun for two days until hard.

Q: Why do you pinch one edge of the diya?
You pinch one edge to make a spout where the wick will rest.

Veg sandwich steps: butter two slices of bread on one side each. Spread green chutney on the buttered side of one slice. Layer thin slices of cucumber, tomato and boiled potato, and sprinkle a pinch of salt and chaat masala. Cover with the second slice, buttered side down, and cut it into triangles.

Question: Did the cook use brown or white bread?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know which bread was used. Brown or white would both work with these steps, so it is your choice.

Skipping rope routine: start with a one-minute warm-up of marching on the spot. Skip with both feet for thirty seconds, rest for ten seconds and repeat five times. Keep your elbows close to your body and land softly on the balls of your feet. Finish with slow stretches.

What is a warm-up for?
The text doesn't say, but a warm-up gets your muscles ready for exercise and helps prevent strains.

Growing a bean in a glass: place a damp paper towel inside a clear glass. Push a bean between the glass and the towel. Keep the towel wet by adding a little water every day. In about a week, the root grows downward and a shoot grows upward. Write down what you see each day.

Which way does the root grow?
The root grows downward.

Making chapati dough: put two cups of whole wheat flour in a bowl with a pinch of salt. Add water a little at a time and knead for five minutes until the dough is soft and smooth. Cover with a damp cloth and rest it for twenty minutes before rolling.

Q: What is wheat?
The text doesn't say, but wheat is a cereal grass whose grains are ground into flour.

Making buttermilk: pour half a cup of curd into a blender jar and add one and a half cups of cold water. Add a pinch of salt, roasted cumin powder and a few curry leaves. Blend for thirty seconds. Pour into glasses and top with chopped coriander.

Question: What is blended with the curd?
Cold water, salt, roasted cumin powder and curry leaves are blended with the curd.

Saving a file on a computer: click on 'File' at the top left and choose 'Save As'. Pick the folder where you want to store it, for example Documents. Type a clear name in the box at the bottom, then press 'Save'. Next time, press Control and S together to save quickly.

Which keys save a file quickly?
Pressing Control and S together saves the file quickly.

Basic football passing drill: stand five steps from a partner and face each other. Use the inside of your foot to push the ball straight to your partner. Stop the ball with the same foot and pass it back. After ten passes, take one step back. Keep your eyes on the ball.

Paper boat steps: take a rectangular sheet and fold it in half, then open it to leave a crease. Fold the top corners down to the middle line to make a roof shape. Fold the bottom strips up on both sides. Pull the sides apart, flatten it into a diamond, fold the corners up and pull again.

Members should bring their membership card.

What happens to late work?
Late work loses one mark per day.

What is a fine?
The text doesn't say, but a fine is money you must pay as a punishment for breaking a rule.

What is a bugle?
The text doesn't say, but a bugle is a small brass horn with no valves, often used for signals and in marches.

Why is it important to return lost items?
The text doesn't say, but returning lost items is honest and kind, and it helps the owner get their things back.

Hi Jamal, thanks for the invite. I can come to your birthday on Saturday, but I will be a little late as I have swimming class until five. Shall I bring a game or a snack? I am thinking of cards.

Why will the writer be late?
The writer has swimming class until five.

Priya found an old diary in her grandmother's trunk. The pages were yellow, and the writing was in blue ink. She read the first line, which was a recipe for jaggery sweets, and put the diary back carefully. The trunk was in the attic, under a pile of old sarees and a few blankets.

Who wrote the diary?

Reading challenge: every student who reads five books by the end of the month will get a gold star on the notice board. Write the book names in your reading log. Mrs. Joseph will check the logs every Friday.

How many books must a student read for the star?
A student must read five books.

New in the shop this week: a set of children's picture books about animals, a pack of coloured pencils, and a notebook with a hard cover. Our shop is open from 10 am to 8 pm. Ask the counter about our monthly offers.
